FACT SHEET
Academic Year 2026-2027
The VSE’s honourable title of doctor
oeconomiae honoris causa has been
awarded to many important Czech and
international economists, e.g. the Nobel Prize
laureates Prof. Gary S. Becker, Prof. Dr.
Douglass North, Prof. Milton Friedman or
Prof. Robert A. Mundell.
Each semester approx. 1000 international students from all over the world study at VSE
in non-degree and degree programmes. VSE also offers several master (double/joint) and
bachelor (double/joint) degree programmes taught completely in English and many
doctoral programmes in English. VSE has more than 240 partners worldwide involved in
its Exchange Programme.
All Exchange Students study in the one of the three
university campuses which is situated near the centre of
Prague. The courses offered in the Exchange Programme
are given by lecturers from different faculties and
departments. Intensive courses given by international
visiting professors enrich the academic offer.
For more information and news about our school please
refer to VSE website.
VSE is highly appraised both in the Czech Republic and abroad.
Thanks to correct implementation of the credit system, VSE was
certified with the “ECTS label” and “DS Label” by the European
Commission from 2014 to 2018. Both certificates confirm the
credibility of VSE in terms of partnerships with universities abroad.
VSE is ranked by the Financial Times annually and has already
been appraised by the Eduniversal Ranking project as one of the
best “business schools” in Central and Eastern Europe during the
past couple of years. VSE is the first university in the Czech
Republic to be accredited by the Association to Advance
Collegiate Schools of Business “AACSB”, confirming its
membership in a small group of elite global economic universities.
Two Master’s degree programs have been certified with EPAS
accreditation by the European Foundation for Management
Development (EFMD). The Faculty of Business Administration has
successfully completed the EQUIS re-accreditation process and is
still the only Czech faculty with this most prestigious international
accreditation in the field of management.

Welcome to EBS Business School
Situated in the heart of Germany’s beautiful Rheingau wine
region, EBS Business School combines academic excellence
with an inspiring setting.
As one of Germany’s leading private business schools, we
offer a dynamic international environment, a strong
network of corporate partners, and a tradition of shaping
future leaders. Exchange students at EBS benefit from
small class sizes, excellent professors who know your name,
and a diverse, global student community.
Beyond the classroom, our campus provides unique
opportunities to experience German culture while enjoying
the charm of Oestrich-Winkel, just a short trip away from
Frankfurt – one of Europe’s most important financial and
cultural hubs.
Whether you are looking to challenge yourself academically, grow your international network, or
explore Germany’s history and lifestyle, EBS offers the ideal setting for a truly enriching exchange
experience.
About Us
Founded in 1971 by Prof. Dr. Klaus Evard in an empty shoe
factory in Paris, EBS Universität began as Germany’s first
private business university.
The vision: an international, practice-oriented education
closely connected to corporate partners - unlike anything
seen in Germany at the time.
We do this with state-of-the-art didactic methods, with a
coaching and leadership hub dedicated to strengthening
leadership skills and with our teaching approach of
Challenge Based Learning - together with many partners
from the field. This enables our students to bring out their
best and equip themselves to change the world.
EBS aims to develop a new leadership elite guided by
values such as courage, responsibility, and integrity.
Today, around 2,200 students from around the world study on the Oestrich-Winkel campus, supported
by 44 professors and more than 250 staff members.

Smith Undergraduate

Smith
Undergraduate

Fact Sheet 2025/26
Smith School of Business is renowned
for excellence, innovation, and leadership
in business education.
Queen’s University, home of Smith School of Business, has a rich
academic tradition dating back to 1841. Located in Kingston, Ontario
— one of Canada’s most vibrant small cities — Smith Commerce
at Queen’s is consistently ranked amongst Canada’s best
undergraduate business programs. Due to its strong reputation,
Smith attracts top students from across Canada and around the world.
Centre for International Management (CIM)
The Centre for International Management at Smith School of
Business coordinates the global activities within the school.
This includes managing relationships with business school
partners and overseeing our suite of exchange and double
degree programs at both the undergraduate and graduate levels.
Smith maintains international exchange partnerships with over
135 business schools in over 40 regions and welcomes more than
500 international exchange students annually. Every year, well
over 600 of our students travel to international destinations to
participate in an international exchange or complete their global
business projects.

The UK government is rolling out the Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) process for
visitors. This allows single semester students to visit the UK for up to 6 months and costs
£10. More details can be found at https://www.gov.uk/guidance/apply-for-an-electronic-
travel-authorisation-eta.
Students who are required to apply for a Visitor visa before travelling to the UK (i.e. ‘visa
nationals’ e.g. China, India, Turkey) are not affected by this change.

Students that don’t need a Student Visa are not entitled to regular health
care.
Students entering the UK on a Student Visa are entitled to health care the
same way as a resident:
Loughborough University can offer support across a wide range of disabilities including
dyslexia, autistic spectrum conditions and long-term health conditions.
Depending on an assessment of your specific needs, your support could include:
▪ Examination and assessment adjustments
▪ Access to free specialist software on the University IT system
▪ Orientation and familiarisation visits around campus
▪ Provision of specialist mentoring and/or study support sessions
▪ Bespoke library access
▪ Signposting to self-help material and local services related to mental health
and wellbeing
▪ Adaptions to the physical environment or provision of equipment in your Halls
of Residence
Loughborough Business School. 12

| Your health matters |
| --- |

| Students that come to the UK to study for less than 6 months don’t need to apply for a Student |
| --- |
| Visa, and therefore they will be treated as “visitors”. Visitors and are not entitled to free |
| healthcare nor a family doctor, but they can visit the hospital in an emergency. |
|  |
| Hospital visits will be charged therefore we recommend that you buy travel insurance |
| that comes with healthcare cover, so you can recover any costs that you incur. |
|  |
| If you are an EU, EEA or Swiss national you will be exempt from some medical costs if you |
| have a European Health Insurance Card (EHIC). It is important that you apply for an EHIC in |
| your own country and bring it with you. |

| Students that come to the UK to study for more than 6 months are entitled to free healthcare |
| --- |
| and they can register for a GP (family doctor) including the medical centre on campus. When |
| you apply for a visa, you will be asked to pay the Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS). This |
| costs £470 and will allow you to use most of the NHS services for free. However, services as |
| prescriptions, dental treatment and optical treatment are not included and need to be paid. |
|  |

| expenses, including food, clothing, books and local travel. |

INTERNATIONAL STUDENT EXCHANGE PROGRAM Fact Sheet
School of Business, Renmin University of China
43rd in FT MBA Ranking 2016 43rd in FT Global EMBA Ranking 2014 49th in FT EE Ranking 2014

| Name of University | School of Business, Renmin University of China |
| --- | --- |
| Overview | As one of China’s premier business schools, RBS boasts the longest history of management education in China, dating back to 1950. With close to 4,000 students and over 150 faculty members, it is the biggest and the most internationalized school among all 23 schools at Renmin University of China (total student population: 22,000+; ranked NO.1 in social sciences and humanities in China by the Ministry of Education). RBS is ranked No.1 in China in the national assessment of Business Administration discipline. Our school has obtained both EQUIS and AACSB accreditations, and ranked among the top 50 by the Financial Times in MBA, EMBA, and EE programs. We’re also a member of the GNAM (Global Network for Advanced Management) initiated by Yale School of Management. | About IE University IE University is a place for forward-thinking visionaries to learn in a transformative environment. Located in Madrid and Segovia, IE University is consistently ranked among Spain’s very best universities. This dynamic hub consists of more than 160 different countries represented on campus each year, with over 75% of its student body coming from outside of Spain. Global Experience Office Contact information: Meet the team: MADRID CAMPUS Alberto García, Director alberto.garcia@ie.edu P.º de la Castellana, 259E Offices T-9.05 / T-9.10 28046 Madrid – Spain *Please use our Madrid office as the main mailing Incoming Students to IEU address. geo.incoming@ie.edu Leanna Lovely, Junior Manager SEGOVIA CAMPUS Marisa Torola, Coordinator Raquel Parreño, Assistant Main Segovia Campus: Santa Cruz la Real Campus, Cardenal Zúñiga 12 Office SG-350 40003 Segovia – Spain Outgoing Students from IEU Segovia Creative Campus (BAS, BID & BIFD): geo.outgoing@ie.edu Palacio de Mansilla, Calle San Nicolás, 5 40001 Segovia – Spain Cathrine Cozad, Junior Manager (North America) Francesca Iacovelli, Coordinator (APAC, SA, MEA) Natalie Joos, Coordinator (Europe) PHONE: +34 91 568 96 00 Francesca Diotalevi, Assistant & Erasmus+ WEBSITE: https://www.ie.edu/university/ieu- experience/international-experience/ |

Students are expected to arrive a few days before the official start of the term. Students enrolled in BAS may have courses until May 28th during the Spring 27 semester. **Note: Kindly note, Fall and Full-Year students must both be nominated during the Fall nomination period. If a Fall student wishes to extend to Full Year, they must be nominated again during the Spring nomination period. We cannot consider any requests after the nomination period has finished. ***Note: Due to a recent reform to the Spanish immigration law, NON-EU students MUST apply for a student visa in person at least 2 months prior to the official start of the semester. Therefore, our nomination/application/admission timeline has been moved forward to meet this requirement. All students will receive a Visa Guide after they have been nominated. NON-EU students should review this information thoroughly to begin preparing as soon as possible! ****Note: Students in their final semester of studies should be made aware of this timeline as this is an official process managed by the registrar’s office and cannot be expedited. Therefore, we cannot guarantee that students in their final semester will receive their transcript before graduation. IE University Attendance Policy Please note, IE University has a strict attendance policy that applies to all students, both local and exchange. It is very important that your students are aware of this policy when considering IEU. According to IE University policy, attendance is mandatory. All students are expected to attend 100% of the sessions in person, on campus as classroom participation is an essential component of IE’s learning methodology. Health problems, visa delays, travel restrictions, personal trips, appointments, family celebrations, interviews, late enrollment in the course, and all other personal matters are to be treated as exceptions to the 100% attendance policy. Such exceptions cannot total more than 20% of the student’s overall attendance in the course or the student will be at risk of failing. Consequently, scheduling overlaps higher than 20% are not allowed. If students surpass the 20% limit, they must justify these absences with their academic offices. Failure to do so will translate into a failed class. This attendance policy is strictly enforced by each IEU academic office and the Global Experience Office cannot interfere in these matters. |

| Bilateral Exchange Spots Number of exchange seats for AY 26/27: To determine the number of students you may nominate through our bilateral exchange partnership for the current academic year, please refer to your previous correspondences with our team (alberto.garcia@ie.edu). Should you have more students show an interest than our agreed-upon numbers, kindly do not nominate them via our online form. Instead, you can nominate them through the Explorer Student Program (Fee-paying Partnership). See information below* Explorer Student Program (Fee-Paying Partnership)* This is a tuition-based, one-way mobility program that allows English Proficiency Requirements Partner Universities to send additional students outside of our agreed-upon exchange quota. The same processes and Key Dates apply to both the Fee-Paying Partnership and Exchange The possession of an English certificate is mandatory. Partnership. For more information on the process and tuition, you may contact geo.incoming@ie.edu IE University requires all applicants to demonstrate with GlobalAcademicPartnerships@ie.edu in copy. competence in the English language by providing one of the following official certificates taken within the last 2 years. TOEFL 100 (iBT)* IELTS 7 CAE (C1) / CPE (C2) Duolingo 130 pts *TOEFL scores as of January 2026 are reported on a 1-6 scale, and IE University accepts TOEFL 5. Native speakers do not need to submit test scores. Students will need to provide a valid passport from an English-speaking country during application. Students whose degree programs are entirely taught in English do not need to submit test scores. In the nomination form, coordinators must confirm that English is the medium of instruction at their home institution and their students consequently have sufficient proficiency in English to study at IEU. We cannot be flexible with these scores or validity dates, as these requirements apply to all IEU students. We cannot accept any other document besides the ones indicated above to fulfill this application requirement. Explorer Student Eligibility All students nominated to our Explorer Student Program must: Have successfully completed at least one-year of full- time study at the home institution. Be in good academic standing at the home institution. Be proficient in English (See English proficiency requirements) Kindly note that Fall and Full-Year students must both be nominated during the Fall nomination period. If a Fall student wishes to extend their exchange to Full Year, they must be nominated again during our Spring nomination period. We cannot consider any requests to extend a student’s exchange after the nomination period has finished. |

| Departments & Services Available for Explorer Students Once your student has been admitted to IE University, they will have access to many useful resources available on Campus. Find more information below about the different IEU departments that help students with immigration & relocation services, adjusting to life in Spain, and becoming part of the IEU Community. Student Services - Immigration & Relocation The IEU Student Services department supports students with immigration and relocation processes, to make the transition to Spain a bit smoother. To contact IEU Student Services office, email ieustudentservices@ie.edu or call at (+34) 91 568 98 96. IMMIGRATION EU CITIZENS: You will not need a visa if you are from Germany, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Croatia, Denmark, Slovakia, Slovenia, Estonia, Finland, France, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Czech Republic, Romania, Sweden, or Switzerland. *Residents of Monaco must request a visa in Marseilles. **Residents of Andorra do not need a visa, but have a different immigration process once here in Spain. ***Please be aware that the requirements for UK citizens changed after Brexit, as from January 1st, 2021. In this regard, UK nationals need to apply for a student visa in order to study in Spain. Remember to bring your passport and your EHIC (European Health Insurance Card) if it is available in your country. NON EU CITIZENS: If you are a non-European union citizen, you will need a student visa. Once you have been admitted as an Explorer Student at IE University, the Student Services department will provide NON EU students with their official admission letter (in Spanish) directed to their corresponding Spanish consulates. You will have to then contact the nearest Spanish consulate or embassy that corresponds to your place of legal residence. They should be able to give you an updated list of student visa requirements, as well as answer any questions you may have regarding the application process. Don’t forget to book your student visa appointment as soon as you receive your visa documents! Click HERE to see all the Spanish consulates and embassies around the world. HEALTH INSURANCE Health insurance coverage is necessary for all students in Spain but more so for international students, who apply for a student visa, as they will be asked to provide this during their visa application process. If you have any questions about health insurance as an EU or NON-EU student kindly contact Student Services to find out more information. LIVING IN MADRID & SEGOVIA Students are advised to start their accommodation search early as soon as they know what campus they are nominated to. Looking into housing options early will ensure a better fit for student’s needs and expectations. IEU ACOMMODATION | MADRID: There are several housing options in Madrid: Student residences, private flats, shared flats, and homestays with local families. Click HERE to learn about housing options in Madrid and see which one is best for you and HERE to see the estimated cost of living. IEU ACOMMODATION | SEGOVIA: There are several housing options in Segovia, a World Heritage city featuring cobblestones and a famous Roman aqueduct: Student residences, private flats, shared flats, homestays with local families and residence apartments. Click HERE to learn about housing options in Segovia and discover which one is best for you and HERE to see the estimated cost of living. |

| IEU Campus Life IEU Campus Life is the team that helps you leverage your learning experience outside the classroom during your IE journey. Campus Life fosters community engagement through debates, entrepreneurship competitions, art exhibitions, among many other interactive networking opportunities. With over 9,000 students from 130 different countries, 197 clubs, and around 1,500 yearly events, there is always something happening at IE University. Exchange students have the same rights and privileges as local IEU students, and this includes access to facilities and extracurricular activities. Pursue your interests and passions in parallel to your studies! IEU SPORTS & WELL-BEING IE University Sports & Well-Being offers the opportunity for self-care through sports and physical initiatives within the IE Community. We enhance the student experience by serving as a platform for the entire community to gather in a dynamic and supportive environment and help each other grow. Through our wide range of well-being, sports, fitness and adventure activities, we provide the opportunity to maximize well-being and achievement, whatever each student’s interest or skill level may be. IEU CLUBS No matter what piques your interest, we have you covered. IE clubs are instrumental to the IE experience. They are the engine to a unique and fun-filled time at IE. Click HERE to learn more and see which one is best for you. IEU TRADITIONS IE University’s contagious spirit and pride have grown tremendously over the years, bolstered by exciting campus-wide events and programs. Join in, have fun, and become a part of IE’s lively events and longstanding traditions. Click HERE to learn about the different IEU events and see which one is best for you. IEU Counseling The IEU Counseling department provides resources and support to help students achieve and maintain an equilibrium between their academic obligations, extracurricular activities and their personal and social lives. The IEU Counseling department aims to ensure undergraduate students’ well-being at every stage of their academic career. International students who experience distress or have issues adjusting to life in Spain can use this service to seek guidance and support. IEU Center for Health, Well-Being, and Happiness The mission of the IEU Center for Health, Well-Being, and Happiness is to give students, staff and IEU alumni the skills necessary to help them study, live and work at their very best. The Center takes a scientifically grounded and holistic approach to enhancing performance and happiness through simple, practical and sustainable educational programs. We can't wait to welcome the students on campus! |

Handbook for International Exchange Students accessible as a PDF file on the Purdue
Study Abroad website: http://www.studyabroad.purdue.edu/incoming/

Contact: Nancy J. Bennett
Assistant Director
njbennett@purdue.edu
1. Term dates and application deadlines
fall semester or academic year early August late December March 15
spring semester early January early May October 15
2. Exchange Program Application and required documents
a) download application from http://www.studyabroad.purdue.edu/incoming/
b) clear copy of passport
c) original signed letter from bank attesting to availability of $5,525
d) transcript (in English)
e) information about English language ability if language of instruction is not
English
3. Housing: see website above
application for campus housing form is downloadable from web site
deposit required
off-campus housing must be found by student; Purdue cannot offer assistance in
locating rooms, apartments or roommates

4. Courses:
see http://www.purdue.edu/Purdue/course_info/
students need to list requested courses on application
students must enroll in a minimum of 12 credit hours per semester
5. Orientation: Exchange students are required to participate in the International
Student Orientation organized by the Purdue Office of International Students and
Scholars. This takes place one week prior to the beginning of fall and spring semester.
6. Visa: The exchange student application and the supporting documents are
forwarded to the Purdue Office of International Students and Scholars for the
preparation of a DS 2019 visa document. With that document the student applies at the
closest U.S. consulate for a student visa.
7. Credits: Purdue uses the credit hour system. Since most courses at Purdue are
worth 3 or 4 credits, students generally take 4 to 5 courses per semester. Exchange
students in the past have commented that courses at Purdue involve a lot more work so
we do not recommend that they take more than five courses per semester.
8. Grades: Academic performance in each course is evaluated by the professor using
letter grades of “A” to “F” . The grading system used to evaluate a student’s academic
performance is based on a four-point scale. At the end of the semester you will receive
a number of credits corresponding to the courses you have successfully completed.
These credits are multiplied by your grades to determine your “grade-point average”
(G.P.A.). A G.P.A. provides a general indication of overall academic performance and is
used by graduate school admissions offices and employers interested in a student's
academic history. Generally, undergraduate students are expected to complete their
studies with a “C” average or better.
9. Costs and Budgets: Tuition is to be paid at your home university. Applicants must
show that they have a minimum of $5,525 to cover the following: housing and meals,
$5,030 and books and supplies, $ 495. these figures do not include costs for
entertainment or travel within the U.S.
10. The Purdue Office of International Students and Scholars organizes an
International Friendship Program. Please see http://www.iss.purdue.edu/Programs/IFP/

| --- | --- |

| PROGRAMMES & FACULTY | The Grande Ecole degree of SKEMA (Master in Management) is recognised by the French State as “Master“ level. The BBA degree of SKEMA (BBA in Global Management) is recognised by the French State as “Bachelor” level. There are more than 10,000 students present on our campuses in Asia, Europe, South Africa and America. The school itself is international in nature: - 45% international students - Ranked in the Financial Times - Eight campuses (France, Brazil, China, Africa, UAE and USA) Global BBA, Master, PhD programs and Executive MBA 100% taught in English Specialised in the Knowledge Economy in the following areas: Entrepreneurship, Technology and Innovation Management; Information and Knowledge Management; Risk Management: Industrial Dynamics, Sustainable Development, Globalisation. The faculty is organised in three cross-disciplinary academies: Globalisation, Digitalisation and Innovation. It is composed of both French and international professors of very high academic standards. |
| --- | --- |

International Office

Amanda NAGELE
International Office Manager

Incoming exchange student information
ACADEMIC CALENDAR

LANGUAGE REQUIREMENTS
Regular Exchange Students:
TOEFL (550 ITP, 80 iBT), TOEIC 850, IELTS 6,5, Duolingo 115, Cambridge English Qualification 175
MSc Dual Degree Exchange Students:
TOEFL (550 ITP, 80 iBT), TOEIC 850, IELTS 6,5, Duolingo 115, Cambridge English Qualification 175
PGE Dual Degree Exchange Students:

PROGRAMMES AVAILABLE FOR EXCHANGE STUDENTS
French as foreign language classes at different levels are offered to international students.
MASTER PROGRAMME (6 CAMPUSES) GLOBAL BBA PROGRAMME (4 CAMPUSES)
https://www.skema.edu/en/exchange-students https://www.skema.edu/en/exchange-students
Areas of concentration: Business and Management, Project Management, Marketing, Areas of concentration: Finance, Management, Marketing, Entrepreneurship,
Finance and Accounting, Strategy, Entrepreneurship, Tourism, Luxury Environmental Management, Global Business.
Grading system: From 0 to 20, 20 being the best mark. Passing grade: 10 with a Grading system: US based. Grading scale from 0 to 4. Passing grade : C (2.0)
corresponding GPA out of 4. Transcripts also show ECTS grades (A - E)
Students must choose courses within one specialisation only. Exchange students are expected to follow a minimum of 15 ECTS credits per semester.
Exchange students are expected to follow a minimum of 15 ECTS credits per semester. Students can take maximum 30 ECTS credits per semester.
Students can take maximum 21 ECTS credits per semester in MSc specialisations or
maximum 30 ECTS credits per semester for Master 1.
ORIENTATION
Incoming exchange students must participate in the Orientation Days which takes
place at the beginning of each semester.
The Orientation Days introduces international students to the various services and
systems in operation at SKEMA Business School. They will get all the academic and
practical information they need for their studies: confirmation of course choices,
class schedule, student card, computer account, campus tour, Residence Permit
information, presentation of student associations, icebreaker games.
VISA INFORMATION
Non EU students coming to SKEMA in France for more than 3 months need a long-stay student visa.
Once in France, students will be required to validate their visas. The International Office team will explain this procedure to students during Orientation.
International students studying in Raleigh, Suzhou, Belo Horizonte will also be assisted to prepare their student visas.
Sophia Antipolis , Lille, Paris : studentexchange.incoming@skema.edu | Raleigh, Suzhou, Belo Horizonte: international.campuses@skema.edu.
INTERNATIONAL STUDENT GUIDE
All practical information will be available on SKEMA’s online platform “SKEMA Compass”. After completing the online application, students accepted for an exchange will receive an email
with their login and password to access on SKEMA’s online platforms. Our 6 campuses are open to exchange students without extra fees.
2

SSKKEEMMAA CCAAMMPPUUSSEESS GGEENNEERRAALL IINNFFOORRMMAATTIIOONN
SOPHIA ANTIPOLIS - France MASTER PROGRAMME / GLOBAL BBA PROGRAMME
General background: The Sophia Antipolis campus is located on the French Riviera in Sophia Antipolis, a technology park which is
home to several renowned companies, research institutes and schools of higher education. Most of SKEMA’s students live either in
Antibes or Juan les Pins, coastal towns close to Sophia Antipolis, easily accessible by bus.
Food: Lunch can be bought at the cafeteria for ¤3.25 from Monday to Friday. Sandwiches and salad bar are also available as well as
microwave ovens for students’ use.
Transport: Most students fly to Nice Côte d’Azur Airport, which is 45 min’ drive from Sophia Antipolis campus. Students can park
in the campus. There is a bus line run by the General Council of the region that costs ¤1,50. All main locations around the campus are
accessible by bus. There are two kinds of monthly plans available for students: Under 26 years old: ¤20 - Over 26 years old: ¤30.
Campus facilities: Computer labs and wireless networks are available on campus. 2 Trading rooms, 6 Amphitheatres from
150 to 600 seats, 50 Lecture rooms from 20 to 80 seats. Multimedia library.
LILLE - France MASTER PROGRAMME / GLOBAL BBA PROGRAMME
General background: The Lille campus is located in the town centre between the two railway stations (Lille Flandres & Lille Europe),
next to the old town and the business centre. Lille is only 1 hour from Paris, 38 minutes from Brussels and 1h20mn from London by
train. Lille is the main student town after Paris. The region is well known for its dynamic economic activity: several companies have
set up their headquarters here in order to be logistically at the centre of Europe.
Food: Students can eat at the University Restaurant near the school. On the campus, a cafeteria offers quick snacks at reasonable
prices. The school is located above the shopping centre where you can find Carrefour supermarket.
Transport: Most students arrive either at the Lille Flandres station or the Lille Europe station. Ilévia is the company that runs all the
buses, tramways and metro. They offer low prices for students under 28.
Campus facilities: There are computer labs and wireless networks on the Lille campus, including the library and the common
facilities.
France MASTER PROGRAMME
GRAND PARIS -
General background: Paris continues to be one of the most alluring cities in the world for cultural and economic activities. SKEMA
Business School’s Grand Paris Campus in Suresnes is a central site 13 minutes by car from Les Champs Elysées. The campus is
spread across 14,000 m2, including 1,500 m2 of rooftop terrace with views of the Seine and the Eiffel Tower.
Food: Students have access to the cafeteria, which will serve a variety of international cuisine.
Transport: Most students arrive by Tram - line T2 (Les Coteaux) or by train - line L (Val d’Or) - or by bus - lines 175 (Clavel station),
263 Monge station) or 471 (Avenue de Suresnes station). They also can come by bicycle ( Vélib ) or by car (possibility to park in the
Grand Paris Campus parking lot).
Campus facilities: The knowledge Centre is a space serving three functions: “library” (documentation), “factory” (production
facility) and “academy” (research to train and educate). It is also virtual, via its data-rich resource portal that is accessible at all
times.
NC - USA MASTER PROGRAMME / GLOBAL BBA PROGRAMME
RALEIGH -
General background: The SKEMA US campus is situated in Raleigh, North Carolina, about 1h by plane from NYC.
The SKEMA building is located on the Centennial campus of our partner North Carolina State University and is surrounded by many
international companies.
Housing & Food: SKEMA provides students with a Raleigh Housing Guide which includes a number of student residences located
on and around campus. All apartments are close to the SKEMA campus (access by bus) and fully equipped. The housing usually
costs an average of ¤750/¤1100 per month. Students can eat at university dining halls (cafeterias) or at several small restaurants/
cafés on campus which serve breakfast, lunch and dinner.
Transport: The nearest airport to SKEMA US campus is Raleigh/Durham International Airport (RDU) which is about 24 km away.
Your student ID gives access to the free Wolfline bus transport to go anywhere on campus and in Raleigh.
Campus facilities: Students have access to all NCSU facilities including impressive sporting facilities and libraries, bus lines, health
centre, dining halls, and much more.
HOUSING ON FRENCH CAMPUSES:
SKEMA campuses in France do not have on-campus accommodation but we have agreements with a number of residences located in the campus area.
Housing usually costs an average of ¤650 up to ¤1000 per month. SKEMA provides a housing portal to assist students.
For further information: housing@skema.edu
HEALTH INSURANCE FOR THE FRENCH CAMPUSES:
Exchange students are required to arrange their own insurance covering illnesses and accidents during the period of their stay in France. All the international students attending
SKEMA on exchange must purchase health insurance before applying for their student visa. Non EU citizen students studying for more than three months at SKEMA, are required
to enroll in the French “Sécurité Sociale” once they arrive in France. All students must have repatriation coverage during their stay at the host country.
3

SSKKEEMMAA CCAAMMPPUUSSEESS GGEENNEERRAALL IINNFFOORRMMAATTIIOONN
SUZHOU - China MASTER PROGRAMME
General background: Suzhou has been called the Venice of the East because of its many canals, beautiful natural environment and
traditional gardens. Situated one hour from Shanghai (2nd industrial city of China) Suzhou is a well-known high-technology centre
with 118 of the top 500 companies in the world.
Housing & Food: SKEMA has negotiated a certain number of apartments close to the campus. The housing usually costs on
average ¤350 per month. On campus, students can eat at several small restaurants and fast food restaurants which are all
reasonably priced. Students can also prepare meals in their flats which are conveniently located to school.
Transport: To get from the airport to campus, students can go by taxi (2h30 mn cost 600-800 RmB), train (1h30mn- cost 120
RmB) or bus (2h30mn- cost 130 RmB). As a service to students, SKEMA will be organizing shuttle buses from Shanghai Pudong
Airport to Suzhou campus on selected dates at the beginning of each semester (cost 200 RmB).
Campus facilities: All essential services are available on campus: restaurants, laudromat, travel agent, phone card kiosk, buses,
taxis, etc. Nearby, there is a large library and sport facility.
BELO HORIZONTE - Brazil MASTER PROGRAMME / GLOBAL BBA PROGRAMME
General background: Belo Horizonte, Brazil’s third most important city for business, is 360km from Rio de Janeiro and 500km from
São Paulo. It is ranked among the 10 most dynamic cities for business in Latin America by the magazine América Economia and is
also considered the Brazilian Silicon Valley with more than 200 startups and 10 incubators.
Housing & Food: SKEMA has negotiated a certain number of apartments in hotel residences close to the campus. The housing
usually costs an average of ¤800 per month. SKEMA also provides a housing portal to assist students.
Students can eat in the dining halls (cafeterias) or at several small restaurants/cafés on campus.
Transport: Flights from Europe have a layover in Rio de Janeiro or São Paulo airports before taking a domestic flight to Belo
Horizonte. Students have access to the campus by public bus.
Campus facilities: Students have access to all facilities including impressive sporting facilities and libraries, computer labs, dining
halls, and much more.
UAE CURRENTLY NOT OPEN TO INCOMING EXCHANGE STUDENTS
DUBAI -
General background: At the crossroads of the Indo-Pacific, Asian and African regions, Dubai is now one of the world’s biggest
magnets for talent. Located at the heart of the Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC), this campus is a thriving hub for students
keen on making an active contribution to the world of tomorrow and the renewal of a region long defined by its dependence on oil.
In the United Arab Emirates, young people from around the world are eager to play a key role in a financial and economic centre of
influence.
South Africa CURRENTLY NOT OPEN TO INCOMING EXCHANGE STUDENTS
STELLENBOSCH -
General background: By joining forces with Stellenbosch University, SKEMA has chosen a prestigious partner to establish its
African campus near Cape Town, South Africa. Students benefit from the exceptional facilities offered by the university, including a
vast library, a music school with concert halls, and first-class sports facilities (stadiums, gymnasiums, Olympic pools, etc.).
Housing: Students are eligible for on-campus university housing and can also benefit from an extensive list of private
accommodations.
Campus facilities: SKEMA students and participants will benefit from the many facilities of the Stellenbosch University that
include an extensive library, a music school, concert halls, an athletics stadium, several Olympic swimming pools and sports fields
(rugby , football, tennis, hockey, cricket, squash…).
HEALTH INSURANCE FOR THE INTERNATIONAL CAMPUSES:
Exchange students are required to arrange their own insurance covering illnesses, accidents and repatriation during the period of their stay in the host country. All the international
students attending SKEMA on exchange must purchase health insurance before applying for their student visa.
TO PREPARE STUDENT’S DEPARTURE ONCE SELECTED, CONTACT:
Yana MENCHENKOVA, International Coordinator
international.campuses@skema.edu

| Fact Sheet 2026/2027 The School of Economics and Business was founded in 1987 as a reference quality institution. We focus on academic and research excellence, broad internationalization, and memorable student experience to cultivate "economics with a human face", as it was our first Dean's desire. Our program aims to prepare you for the challenges and opportunities of today's world. Your participation and involvement are essential to develop our mission. Accommodation: On campus housing is not available for exchange students. Exchange students
must make their own housing arrangements. The Office of Student Affairs provides
students with information related to rental accommodation outside CUHK campus:
https://lces.osa.cuhk.edu.hk/non-local-students-support/on-and-off-campus-
accommodation/#off-campus
Academic Expenses: Books and class reading materials around HK$5,000 per term
Living Costs: An estimated cost of living, not including housing, for an exchange student in Hong
Kong is around HK$33,100 for one term but the expenses vary greatly depending
on the lifestyle.
Others
Pre-arrival All exchange students are affiliated to International Asian Studies Programme
Information: (IASP). For pre-arrival information such as visa application and student
registration, please visit https://www.oal.cuhk.edu.hk/beforeyourexchange/.
Visa: All exchange students MUST apply for a Hong Kong student visa (not a China visa)
before arriving in Hong Kong. Applications should be sent directly to the Hong Kong
Immigration Department via the Office of Academic Links (OAL). OAL will send you
the application information and timeline in due course.
Health Insurance: Incoming exchange students holding a valid student visa with a stamp from the
Immigration officer when you enter Hong Kong are entitled to fees and charges for
"Eligible Persons" in Hospital Authority institutions within their duration of stay in
Hong Kong. This means they can enjoy discounted rates for public health services
and are exempted from surgical and hospital insurance. Please visit
https://www.oal.cuhk.edu.hk/duringyourexchange/ for details.
Apart from that, exchange students should also arrange at their own cost in the
accident and sickness insurance coverage with provisions for emergency
evacuation/rescuer's expenses and repatriation for the duration of their studies in
Hong Kong. If they have plans to travel outside Hong Kong, they should make sure
that their insurance policy covers those regions as well included in their parents'
health insurance policies, they should check the coverage before coming to Hong
Kong.
Exchange students are reminded to bring a copy of their insurance policy to Hong
Kong. When they report arrival at CUHK, they will be asked to submit a copy for
emergency use.

■Example 1: If students are living abroad without registering their birth in

obtain a Korean passport or proceed with the necessary steps

declaring a renunciation of Korean nationality, their child
automatically becomes a dual citizen. Although acquiring
foreign citizenship automatically results in the loss of Korean
nationality, it is essential to DECLARE a renunciation of
Korean nationality to an immigration office in Korea. Parents
who give birth to children after acquiring foreign citizenship
often assume that their child will not have dual citizenship.
However, they later realize that this is not the case. In such
situations, if a student wishes to obtain a Korean passport,
parents must complete the following steps: 1) declare their

Incoming Exchange Program Factsheet
Spring 2026
Thank you for your interest in the exchange programs of the School of Business, SYSU! Please review the
following fact sheet which contains the basic information for the programs for your reference.
School of Business, Sun Yat-sen University (SYSU)

2 / 10

1. INTRODUCTION TO SYSU
Sun Yat-sen University, founded by Dr. Sun Yat-sen，has an educational tradition spanning over 100 years,
is a preeminent research, academic and cultural center and the premier location for talent development in
South China.
The School of Business, Sun Yat-sen University (SYSU) is one of the oldest and most prestigious business
schools in China with a rich history. Established in 1985, SYSU is dedicated to sharing knowledge and best
practices that accelerate innovation in business education. Located in Guangdong, Hongkong, Macao
Greater Bay Area, SYSU actively engages in the region’s development by constantly contributing to the
region’s social advancement and economic growth. SYSU keeps holding ourselves accountable for
improving business practice through a commitment to strategic management, learner success, and impactful
thought leadership.
The School has risen to become a top business school in China, one of the first to be awarded triple
accreditations (AMBA in 2010, EQUIS in 2011, and AACSB in 2013). Since its establishment, the School
has always maintained its strength in Business Administration, which was selected into the list of “Double-
First Class” for Discipline Construction by the Ministry of Education in 2017, tied for first (A+) in the
fourth and fifth rounds of national discipline evaluation, and ranked No.1 in the Best Disciplines of China
by Shanghai Ranking in 2019, 2020 and 2021. In the first Times Higher Education China Subject Ratings
in 2020, Business Administration, Management Science, and Engineering in our school won the "A+"
ratings.
2. LOCATION
The school of business is situated in Guangzhou city, with two campuses, Guangzhou East Campus (Pan
Yu District, Guangzhou) and Guangzhou South campus (Hai Zhu District, Guangzhou).
3 / 10

Guangzhou is located in southern China in the middle of Guangdong Province, north of the Pearl River
Delta, with a population of over 10 million. The city also lies close to the South China Sea, Hong Kong,
and Macau. Because of its convenient geographical position, Guangzhou has been called "China's Southern
Gateway". As the capital of Guangdong Province, Guangzhou is the center of its politics, economy, science,
education. The city with long summer and no winter is always green with flowers in bloom all the year
round, hence reputed as "Flower City". Sui (Ears of Rice) is short for Guangzhou and the City of Ram
(Yang Cheng) is also an alias of Guangzhou. The Kapok is the city flower and the kapok tree is the city tree
of Guangzhou.
Guangzhou's industry covers machinery, shipbuilding, textiles, sugar-refinery, household electrical
appliances, computers, and petrochemicals, light industrial products for daily use, rubber products and
garments. It is South China's biggest national-and-foreign-oriented city with flourishing commerce, and
China's chief foreign trade center as well.
Guangzhou is historically both the start of the Maritime Silk Road and the center of Lingnan Culture. It is
also the cradle of the Chinese modern revolution and the foreland of China's reform and opening to the
outside world. Guangzhou has been a renowned commercial center since ancient times and is now the
economic hub of southern China. Chinese Import and Export Commodities Fair (Canton Fair) is widely
regarded as being "The No.1 Exhibition in China" and remains a magnet for foreign investors.
An ancient but dynamic city, Guangzhou impresses visitors with both its vivid modern ambiance and unique
traditional Lingnan indigenous culture. Reflecting the unique charm of a multicultural metropolis, the city's
cultural influences can be seen in all aspects of its social life. Specific examples include diet, lifestyle,
architecture, commerce, language, music, art, and customs.
3. ELIGIBILITY
Students who will be exchanged to SYSU must be attending an institution that has a currently active
Student Exchange Agreement with SYSU as an officially registered student.
*The orientation meetings for new incoming students will usually be provided within the 1st week after the
semester begins.
4 / 10

Step 3: Nominated students prepare and send the digital copies of application documents listed

(3) Certificate of Study or official Nomination Letter which shall be issued by students’ home

Once the application of nominated student is officially approved and accepted by SYSU, an admission

7. VISA
Students shall apply for X visa (single-entry student visa) with the admission package before they come
to SYSU for registration and study. The students with X1 visa MUST apply for a Residence Permit
(multi-entry visa) at the Guangzhou Municipal Public Security Bureau within 30dyas from their first
entry into China with the X1 visa. Residence Permit for students with X2 visa is optional. The
Admission Office SYSU is responsible to process the visa documents and application for all foreign
students.
8. INSURANCE
In addition to your personal insurance, all incoming students to SYSU are required to pay the insurance
fee for “Comprehensive Medical Insurance Plan for Foreign Students in China” (mandatory for
students study in SYSU) and the application fee of RMB400 (one-off payment) before the
registration at SYSU.
The insurance premium is:
➢ RMB400 for 1 semester
➢ RMB800 for 2 semesters
9. REGISTRATION
Upon arrival at SYSU, students must go to the Admission Office SYSU and School of Business, Sun Yat-
sen University, to complete the registration.
*Updated information regarding the registration will be sent to students via email once it is available.

text:
|  |
| --- |
| Student Exchange Program Fact Sheet 2026/27 School Address: International Team: KAIST College of Business Ms. Ju Young Park External Affairs Center, SUPEX 450 Program Manager (Incoming Exchange) 85 Hoegiro, Dongdaemun-gu, Email: jyp1017@kaist.ac.kr Seoul, Korea 02455 http://business.kaist.edu Ms. Yoon-Jung Cho Program Manager (Outgoing Exchange) Email: yj.cho@kaist.ac.kr |
|  |

Introduction to KAIST College of Business
KAIST College of Business (KCB), established in 1996, has been a pioneer in
advancing business education by integrating management and technology.
KCB is accredited by AACSB and is a member of GMAC, PIM, and AAPBS.
KCB comprises two schools: the School of Management Engineering (Seoul)
and the School of Business and Technology Management (Daejeon). The
School of Management Engineering, located on the Seoul campus, includes
the KAIST Graduate School of Business and the Graduate School of Finance.
Seoul, a vibrant city that embodies the economic dynamism of Northeast
Asia, allows students and faculty to maintain a global perspective while
staying rooted in Korea’s culture and innovation.

Academic Information
Eligibility
• Students must be enrolled in an MBA or Master’s program in business and
be able to take a minimum of 9 credits per semester, equivalent of full-
time enrollment at KAIST.
• Students must have an academic performance equivalent to a GPA of 3.0
or higher on a 4.3 scale (approximately 69%).
• Students must be able to stay for the full duration of the semester (16
weeks).
Language Requirements
• Minimum scores: TOEIC 720 / TOEFL iBT 83 / IELTS 6.5
or a confirmation letter from your home program coordinator.
• Not required if you are currently studying in a country where English is an
official language.
Course Information
• All exchange students will be enrolled in the general MBA program (KAIST
MBA).
• Students may take courses across various programs such as KAIST MBA,
Impact MBA, Finance MBA, and Management Engineering.
• It is strongly recommended to register for 9–12 credits per semester.
• Course offerings will be announced 1–2 months before the start of the
semester.
Course Structure
• Most courses are either 3 credits or 1.5 credits.
• One KAIST credit equals 16 contact hours.
• 3-credit courses run for 16 weeks, while 1.5-credit courses are offered in
half-semester formats (Weeks 1–8 or Weeks 9–16).
Class Format
• Attendance is mandatory. Grades are based on attendance, participation,
individual and group projects, assignments, presentation, and exams.
• Transcripts will be shared by email after the end of the semester.
KAIST Grading Scale
• A+ 4.3/A 4.0/A- 3.7/B+ 3.3/B 3.0/B- 2.7/C+2.3/C 2.0/C- 1.7/ D+ 1.3/D
1.0/D- 0.7

Nomination and application process
Students must be officially nominated by their home university.
Detailed application guidelines and procedures will be provided to nominated
students after the nomination period ends.
Nomination and Application Deadlines
Nomination Requirements
• Official nomination form from the home university (Excel format)
• Must be a graduate-level student to take MBA courses
• Minimum GPA: 3.0 on a 4.3 scale (equivalent to 69%)
• Must meet the English language requirement
Application Documents
• Application form
• Recommendation letter
• Curriculum Vitae
• Official Transcript from Current Institution
• Certificate of Enrollment (with Apostille or Korean consul confirmation)*
*If your home university is located in an OECD country, you may be exempted.
• Proof of Financial Ability : Bank Balance of $5,000
• Proof of English proficiency
• Passport scan
Academic Calendar

| Semester | 26 Fall | 27 Spring |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nomination Deadline | March 30 | Oct. 30 |
| Application Deadline | April 30 | Nov. 30 |

| Semester | 26 Fall | 27 Spring |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First Day of Classes | Aug.31(Mon) | Mar.2(Tue) |
| Course Add/Drop | Aug. 24(Mon) - Sept. 7(Mon) | Feb. 22(Mon) - Mar. 8(Mon) |
| Dorm Check-in (tentative) | Aug. 24(Mon) - Aug.31(Mon) | Feb. 22(Mon) - Mar.2(Tue) |
| Mandatory Orientation | Aug. 28(Fri) | Feb. 26(Fri) |
| Full Semester Period | Aug.31(Mon) - Dec. 18(Fri) | Mar. 2(Tue) - June 18(Fri) |
| Exam Period | Dec. 14(Mon) - Dec. 18(Fri) | June 14(Mon) - June 18(Fri) |
| Holidays (No classes) | Sept.24(Thurs)&25(Fri), Oct.5(Mon)&9(Fri) | Mar. 1(Mon), May 5(Wed)&13(Thurs) |

Student Life
On-campus Dormitory
The exchange program application includes a housing request section:
• Students who wish to live in the dormitory must select this option when
submitting their application.
• Students who do not wish to live in the dormitory are responsible for
arranging off-campus housing on their own.
• Single room with bed & mattress, desk, and closet
• Shared toilets & shared shower room in each wing (8 rooms)
• Dorm Fee: 270,000 KRW (approx. USD 200/EUR 180) per month
• Must pay dormitory fee for 4–4.5 months in total upon arrival (based on 15-
day rate, according to the academic schedule).
• Students are responsible for their own mattress covers, pillows, and blankets.
• Loud noise, music, and drinking in the dormitory is strictly prohibited.
Study Lab
Exchange students are also automatically assigned to a study lab - a room with 8-
10 personal desks. Each student will given a private desk to study and store
personal items.
Cafeterias
• Student Cafeteria: lunch & dinner
• Faculty Restaurant: lunch
• Atrium: light snacks & coffee
Sports Facilities
• Indoor gym & exercise room
• Indoor table-tennis room & golf zone
• Outdoor basketball & tennis court

Estimated Living Expenses
Alien Registration Card(ARC)
• This is your official ID in Korea and allows you to stay more than 90 days
and re-enter the country.
• Your ARC (Duration of Stay) shows your valid stay period, usually about a
month after semester ends — end of July for spring, end of January for fall.
• We will apply for it as a group during the exchange student orientation,
and detailed instructions will be provided later.
National Health Insurance Service (NHIS)*
• All exchange students(D2-6 visa holders) will automatically be signed up
to NHIS approximately 2-3 weeks after arrival.
• It is mandatory to pay the NHIS bill for the duration of your exchange.
• As the NHIS will start around mid or late March/September, you will be
charged with insurance fee for 3 months: April, May and June or Oct., Nov.
and Dec..
• You will need to pay around 76,390 KRW per month, a total amount of
around 230,000 KRW for 3 months. (2025)
• NHIS will cover approximately 70% of your medical expense when visiting
the hospital/doctor’s office.
• If you have private insurance with full and unlimited coverage, you can
apply for an exemption. The process must be handled directly by the
individual, please contact NHIS at 033-811-2000
Private Insurance for your first 1 month
• The National Health Insurance (NHI) will not take effect until your Alien
Registration Card (ARC) is issued, which is usually around mid to late
March/September. Therefore, you must purchase travel insurance that
covers the period from your arrival in Korea until at least late
March/September.

| Dormitory Fees 4~ 4.5 months | KRW 1,080,000 ~ 1,215,000 (KRW 270,000 per month) |
| --- | --- |
| National Health Insurance(mandatory)* | KRW 229,170 (76,390 per month(2025) X3 months) |
| Meals and Food | KRW 300,000 -500,000 per month |

After Application
1. Apply for a Visa
• You will receive your Certificate of Admission about 2 months before
the semester begins.
• Contact your nearest Korean Embassy and apply for an Exchange
Student Visa (D-2-6).
• All exchange students must obtain a D-2-6 visa before entering Korea —
it is not optional.
2. Prepare to Enter Korea
Prepare the following:
• Passport-sized photo (3.5cm × 4.5cm)for ARC.
• [Dormitory residents only] Health Certificate completed by a doctor
(form will be provided)
• Flight ticket
• Travel insurance that covers the first month of your stay
(The remaining months will be covered by the mandatory Korean
National Health Insurance.)
3. Start Packing
• Dorm rooms include an empty mattress only. Please bring or purchase
your own bedsheet, pillow, and blanket.
• The heating system is centrally controlled, and it can get quite cold at
night — please prepare accordingly.
• Average temperatures:
- Spring: March – Mid-June (15°C / 59°F)
- Summer: July – Mid-September (25°C / 77°F, August up to 30°C / 86°F)
- Fall: Mid-September – November (13°C / 55°F)
- Winter: December – February (5°C / 41°F)
• Other essentials:
- Bring your own laptop.
- Electricity: 220V / 60Hz
4. Upon Arrival
• Check in to the dormitory by visiting the guard’s office on the 1st floor
of the dormitory building. The guard will guide you to your room.
• Attend the mandatory orientation and apply for the Alien Registration
Card (ARC) as a group.
• Check your course registration: Online add/drop period begins one
week before classes start.

| Nomination and Application Procedure for Student Exchange Program |  | 1. Before the official nomination, program managers at partner universities MUST discuss the exchange quota for each academic year in advance with our KUBS exchange program manager. 2. Once the exchange quota is confirmed, KUBS’s Nomination Instruction will be distributed at the end of March (for Fall semester) and September (for Spring semester). 3. A link to KUBS’s online application will be given to the nominees after the nomination period ends. They MUST complete the online application by the specified deadline. Late application will not be accepted. 4. Starting in June (for Fall semester) and December (for Spring semester), the ‘Admission Package’ – which includes 1) the Letter of Admission, 2) the Certificate of Admission, and 3) Business License of Korea University – will be sent via email to students who completely submitted the application form and all required documents). Nominees must have a Gmail account (or 163.com for Chinese students). Please provide with the nominee’s Gmail address, not other email addresses such as a home institution email address. Important notices from our office may not be delivered to non-Gmail accounts. Other addresses may cause automated emails to be blocked or marked as spam. Therefore, please ensure that the nominee’s Gmail address is provided so they can receive all important communications. |

Due to the high demand for undergraduate business courses, it is highly possible that students will be unable to take the courses they need. We only accept students who can be flexible with their course selection and credit requirements during their exchange year. KUBS experiences extremely high demand for undergraduate business courses. Please be aware of the tight situation regarding the undergraduate course registration and to be flexible regarding your course selection. For these reasons, we do not accept the students who have strict credit requirements or who are in their final year of study or need specific courses for graduation are not recommended to participate in our exchange program. Please do not upload inappropriate photos. 3) Official Academic Transcript - A current transcript in English with a grading scale, demonstrating the equivalent to 2.5 (out of 4.0) and including grades for at least 2 full semesters (Transferred undergraduates/Graduates: 1 semester) 4) Letter of Academic Reference - MUST be completed by a professor or academic advisor familiar with the student’s academic work and is able to attest to his or her character, maturity and self-sufficiency - MUST include the recommender’s name, title, and the school’s official logo - If your professor or advisor prefers to send it directly to us, please let us know via email. 5) Health Certificate (The form can be downloaded from the application page) - MUST be completed by a physician/doctor only - All exchange students are required to complete this form and submit it within the application period. Incoming Students
You can also reach the International Relations Team at international@hhl.de.
TERM DATES (for 2025—26)
Winter 2025 January 6 - March 16, 2025 incl. exams and orientation (mandatory)
Spring 2025 March 10 - June 29, 2025 incl. exams and orientation (mandatory)
Summer 2025 June 30 - September 7, 2025 incl. exams and orientation (mandatory)
(MBA only)
Fall 2025 September 1 - December 21, 2025 incl. exams and orientation (mandatory)
Winter 2026 January 5 - March 15, 2026 incl. exams and orientation (mandatory)
Spring 2026 March 16 - June 28, 2026 incl. exams and orientation (mandatory)
We do not accept late arrivals or early departures! Students will need to stay for the whole term.
Open for incoming exchange students:
MBA: Fall I Winter I Spring I Summer
MSc Management: Fall I Winter I Spring
MSc Entrepreneurship: Fall I Winter I Spring
MSc Finance: Fall I Winter I Spring
EXCHANGE APPLICATION
Nomination by the exchange coordinator of the partner school via email at
friederike.solga@hhl.de is required!
Online application: apply.hhl.de After the successful online application, HHL will send out the
admission documents by email to the students. These documents will contain all information and
forms required for your exchange. It will also contain an official letter of acceptance (required
for issuing a student visa).
Application deadline: For non-EU-citizens: 4 months prior the requested start of the exchange
period (EU/US-citizens: 3 months).
HHL Leipzig Graduate School of Management | Jahnallee 59 | 04109 Leipzig | Germany
International Relations | Tel. +49 341 9851-745 | international@hhl.de

EXPECTED ARRIVAL DATE
Latest day of arrival should be 1 day prior to the start of the Orientation (incl. in the dates above).
We do not accept latecomers!
COURSE RESTRICTIONS
MBA-Students coming for an exchange term may take courses from the MBA-program and from
the MSc-Program. Courses in the MBA-program may be restricted to exchange students coming
from an MBA-program at their home institution. HHL reserves the right to decide individually
according to specific requirements such as pre-knowledge and work experience, whether
students from other programs are eligible for MBA courses as well. Students coming from
consecutive programs (usually a 4 or 5 years European program leading to an equivalent of a
Masters degree) are welcome in the MSc-Program if there are in the final year.
VISA
Student visa required; students coming with a tourist visa will be sent home. In addition, a
health insurance (unlimited coverage) is required – can be obtained in Germany. Processing
time for a visa can be up to three months at the German consulate!
HOUSING
HHL does not have student dormitories. Some dormitories are available on campus only through
the Student Union (Studentenwerk) Leipzig. If you are interested in renting a student dorm,
please contact the Student Union Leipzig directly (http://www.studentenwerk-
leipzig.de/en/housing). Please note that dormitory places are very popular and apply as soon as
possible.
Private Shared apartment: Leipzig has a lot of open living space available. Some apartments are
fully furnished, others come without furniture. You should possibly look for a place in the following
parts of the city: Zentrum, Zentrum Süd, Mitte, Lindenau, Südvorstadt, Plagwitz (these locations
are close to school). Addresses to contact via Internet:
www.wg-gesucht.de I www.easywg.de I www.studenten-wg.de
The first few nights: For the first few nights in Leipzig – especially if you arrive late in the day –
we recommend to stay in one of Leipzig’s hostels. Hostel “Sleepy Lion”: www.hostel-leipzig.de and
hostel “Central Globetrotter”: www.globetrotter-leipzig.de. You should make a reservation in
advance since the hostels are usually booked.
HEALTH INSURANCE
2

|  |
| --- |
| When enrolling, students are required to present proof of coverage by a German health |
| insurance carrier. Insurance coverage from outside Germany may fulfill requirements; a decision |
| about this is under responsibility of a German public insurance company. Students who are from |
| countries with which the Federal Republic of Germany has a social insurance agreement (the EU |
| member states, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia, Liechtenstein, Macedonia, Montenegro, Norway, |
| Switzerland, Tunisia and Turkey), and who are insured in their home country, should submit |
| their European Health Insurance Card (EHIC). |

APPROXIMATE LIVING COSTS
Around EUR 650 per month – non-EU students must show financial proof of EUR 934 per month
for living costs (together with the visa application).
▪ Housing: around EUR 280 – 600 per month
▪ Meals: lunch for students in the cafeteria between EUR 2,10 and 5,00
▪ Textbooks: around EUR 50 for the semester
▪ Entertainment: highly variable
▪ Student Union fee: around EUR 250 for the semester (required, subject to changes)
▪ Transportation: Included in the Student Union fee (public tram / bus)
▪ Tuition fees: students have to pay to the home university according to contracts
Codes for application:
▪ For US-students: HHL’s FAFSA-Code is G38183
HHL’s Facility Code at the US Dpt. of Veterans Affairs is 3-1-0003-80
▪ For EU Erasmus: HHL’s Erasmus Code is DLeipzig09
ACADEMIC REQUIREMENTS FOR EXCHANGE STUDENTS
▪ Exchange students are recommended to do 20 credits during a regular term. We require a
minimum of 15 credits and allow a maximum of 30 credits.
Only on request of the home university will exchange students be allowed to overload or
underload our minimum/maximum limits.
▪ German on survival level is recommended (not required).
German language courses will be offered to all incoming exchange students on three levels:
✓ A1/A2
✓ B1
✓ Business German
▪ Fluency in English to follow courses successfully and complete the coursework is mandatory!
✓ Language of Instruction is English only
✓ HHL requires a minimum TOEFL 90 or IELTS 7.0 (not older than 2 years)
✓ Exceptions: Native English speakers coming from Australia, Canada, New Zealand,
Singapore, South Africa, UK, USA or students having the undergraduate degree from
one of these countries
✓ Partner Universities having a sound internal testing system for English, that prefer to
use their internal testing methodology instead of the required TOEFL, please contact
Friederike Solga at friederike.solga@hhl.de by the nomination deadline.
3

COURSES
Your students are free to choose courses from three different degrees: Master in Management,
MBA and Master in Entrepreneurship.
HHL offers a variety of subjects in:
✓ Accounting
✓ Finance
✓ Strategy
✓ Marketing
✓ Logistics
✓ Entrepreneurship
✓ Internationalal Management
✓ Macroeconomics
✓ Microeconomics
CLASS SIZE
▪ Average class size: 23
▪ Ratio professor/students: 1:15
CLASS PROFILES
Fulltime MBA:
▪ Average age: 29
▪ Age range: 25 - 45
▪ Average work experience: 5,5 years
▪ Educational background: 26% Business Studies, 20% Engineering, 17% Economics, 14%
Liberal Arts, 10% Natural Arts, 8% Others, 5% Law
▪ Average GMAT: 640
▪ Number of international students: 70-80%
▪ Average number of countries represented: 15
Fulltime MSc:
▪ Average age: 24
▪ Age range: 21 - 27
▪ Average work experience: 1.5 years
▪ Educational background: 27% Business Studies, 22% Business Administration, 22%
International Business Studies/Management, 11% Economics, 6% Logistics Management,
6% Commerce, 6% Business Enginieering
▪ Average GMAT: 640
4

ASSESSMENT AND GRADING
All subjects include different forms of assessment, such as class exercises, assignments, quizzes,
tests or examinations. Individual students are, ultimately, responsible for meeting all course
requirements.
German System ECTS System Explanation
≤1,1 A (best 10%) outstanding
≤ 1,4 B (next 25%) very good
≤ 1,7 C (next 30%) good
≤ 2,3 D (next 25%) satisfactory
≤ 4,0 E (next 10%) pass
> 4,0 Fx fail (second exam allowed)
> 4,0 F fail (second exam not allowed)
P Grades not awarded
In order to assure all of our students the highest level of education, HHL requires all students to
sign an Honor Code, which addresses academic integrity, respectful conduct, amongst other
topics. HHL takes this code seriously and holds its students accountable to it.
KEY ATTRACTIONS OF HHL
▪ HHL has the right by the government to award the academic title PhD
▪ Accreditation by (one out of eleven universities in Germany)
▪ Member of gbsn, efmd, CLADEA and CEEMAN
▪ Rated No. 1 in Germany for Business Administration
▪ High standard with 30 to 40 students per semester out of more than 1,000 inquiries
▪ Highly international with 140 partners worldwide plus an international composition
of the student body and faculty
▪ Attractive environment in a dynamic student city
5

STUDENT SERVICES AVAILABLE
▪ ORIENTATION: Orientation is compulsory for all students coming on exchange (One week in
Fall, Spring and one day in Winter; dates included in the academic calendar above).
▪ COUNSELING: Counselling service and access to HHL’s Career service.
▪ STUDENT CLUBS: There are several student clubs run by the student body – have a look at
our website.
▪ ASSISTANCE: All incoming exchange students will have assistance by the International
Committee. This club organizes several activities, cultural events and tours within Germany
for the guest students.
▪ LOCKERS: are assigned to all students
▪ IT SERVICES: Exchange students will have access to all IT facilities including a personal HHL
e-mail address. All computer pools are open 24 hours / 7 days.
▪ LIBRARY: is open to students and staff 24 hours a day.
Containing some 15,000 volumes, it provides a wide range of basic literature and reference
works for your course as well as specialist literature on current research topics. In addition,
the library subscribes to some 200 national and international periodicals and newspapers.
The entire stock is catalogued on the Libero library system, which is known for its efficiency
and user friendliness. Research into the library’s catalogue can be carried out both within
and outside HHL’s network using a WEBOPAC.
In addition, our students have access to the library of the public university and to the
“Deutsche Bibliothek”. This library is unique in Germany, the collection consists of all what
was ever printed in German, starting in 1913.
▪ SPORTS CENTRE: Leipzig Graduate School of Management is sharing the campus with the
sport’s school of the public university. We have agreed that our students can use the full
range offered by the public university. For program details, please check at
http://www.uni-leipzig.de/sport/
▪ 24 HOUR UNIVERSITY: All facilities are accessible for students 24/7
