text:
EXCHANGE STUDENT SERVICES
UF FACT SHEET 2025-2026
CONTACT
University of Florida International Center
1765 Stadium Rd. 170 Hub
P.O. Box 113225
Gainesville, FL 32611
www.internationalcenter.ufl.edu
UF OUTBOUND
STUDY ABROAD SERVICES
John J. Mulligan
Interim Director, Study Abroad Sevices
jmulligan@ufic.ufl.edu
OUTGOING COORDINATORS
Advisors vary by region.
INBOUND TO UF
Amila Tica
Coordinator, Exchange Student Services
atica@ufic.ufl.edu
+1-352-294-3333
IMPORTANT DATES
Nomination Application
Fall Semester April 1 May 1
Spring Semester September 1 October 1
Summer Semester February 1 March 1
2025-2026 Academic Calendar
• Fall 2025: August 21 - December 12
• Spring 2026: January 12 - May 1
Please note that these dates are general semester dates. Graduate Business
school dates and Law school dates may be different than those listed above.
APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS
• Stage 1: Partner School Nomination; Partner school submits on-line nomination.
• Stage 2: UF International Center Online Application
• Stage 3: Post Acceptance Consecutive Processes
A. Student Visa application – apply at nearest US Embassy/Consulate
B. UF student account set-up and pre-registration requirments – process
internal to UF

ENGLISH PROFICIENCY
Per federal regulations, J1 Visa holders must verify they have proficient English
level to participate in their program. Partner schools should include appropriate
documentation at the time of the online nomination. Options for verification are:
1. Student is a passport holder of a country where English is an official
language. Listed here.
2. Student has attended a university in a country where English is an official
language. Listed here. Transcript required at the time of application
submission.
3. Student has achieved sufficient scores on English language competency
exam:
- IELTS Academic: 6.0 Overall
- MELAB: 77
- TOEFL iBT: 80
- TOEFL PBT: 550
- Verbal GRE: 140
- GATEWAY English Test: 425
- CEFR: B2
4. Home University can verify proficiency. Select this option at the time of
nomination. May submit additional documentation in support (for example,
letter of verification).
VISA INFORMATION
• The UF International Center online application covers meeting criteria for the
J1 visa status.
• Upon submission of a complete application and acceptance, Exchange
Student Services will issue a form of eligibility for J1 status sponsorship, DS-
2019 Form.
• Students then receive instructions to apply for their J1 visa.
ACCOMMODATIONS
• On-Campus Housing is limited and therefore not guaranteed to students.
• Students can indicate interest in living on-campus via their online application.
Upon submission of the complete application, students will be considered on
a first come, first serve basis until slots are filled.
• The on-campus dorm for exchange students is Weaver Hall. Weaver Hall
is part of the International Living Learning Community. Please note, to
increase the opportunity for exchange students to live on-campus, students
may be assigned to other dorms outside of Weaver Hall.
• UF Housing will contact students directly to begin the housing application
process.
• UF offers support for off-campus housing through the Off Campus Life office.
Ultimately, students are responsible for their own off campus housing.
International Center
UNIVERSITY of FLORIDA

HEALTH INSURANCE
All UF students are required to have health insurance that meets Affordable Care
Act (ACA) coverage standards. This coverage standard also fulfills international
student visa requirements. The UF Health Insurance policy is an “opt-out”
system. All UF students, including exchange students, will be automatically
enrolled in UF’s Health Insurance Plan. Students can either:
1. Stay enrolled in the UF Health Plan, OR
2. Submit a waiver to request approval for an outside policy by deadline
(outside policy must be comparable to ACA coverage).
NOTE: UF does not accept overseas or travel insurance plans. Students who do
not wish to purchase the UF plan should contact the UF Health Compliance Office
for more information. For additional questions, contact: insurance@ufic.ufl.edu.
ACADEMICS
Minimum credits required per semester
• Undergraduate Students: 12 (typically 4 courses worth 3 credits each)
• Graduate Students: 9 (typically 3 courses worth 3 credits each)
Important Considerations
• Students are allowed to enroll in one 100% on-line course per semester
• Students may not be eligible to participate in restricted enrollment programs
• Students must primarily choose courses from their hosting college. Students
may choose up to one course outside of their hosting college, unless
otherwise specified by their UF academic and exchange advisor.
BUDGETING & COSTS
Estimated Cost of Living:
https://internationalcenter.ufl.edu/j-1-studentscholar/partner-school-exchange-
students/estimated-costs-budgets
Application Funding Requirement: The U.S. government requires J-1 students
to prove sufficient funds for the duration of their program. To meet this
requirement, students must show they have a minimum USD $2300 per month of
the program.
STUDENT LIFE & RESOURCES
• Student Activities and Involvement – Check out student organizations and
daily campus events at this website: https://studentinvolvement.ufl.edu/get-
involved
• UF NaviGators International – Connects International Students with
American students through a unique mentorship program.
https://www.facebook.com/ufnavigatorsintl
• Counselling & Wellness Center (CWC) - https://www.counseling.ufl.edu/cwc
• Gainesville Regional Transit System (RTS) – Students can ride any
Gainesville RTS bus free with their Gator 1 ID card. www.go-rts.com
International Center • Disability Resource Center – https://disability.ufl.edu
UNIVERSITY of FLORIDA • COVID-19 Updates & Resources – https://coronavirus.ufhealth.org

title: SBS International Partner Factsheet 2016-17_0.pdf
text:
FACTSHEET 2016/17
International (non-Erasmus) Exchange Partners
Founded in 1947, Strathclyde Business School (SBS) is an enterprising, pioneering institution of global standing. It is a
triple-accredited business school, holding accreditation from the international bodies AMBA, AACSB and EQUIS and is
one of a small number of business schools worldwide to be triple accredited. SBS welcomes students from over 100
exchange and study abroad partners around the world making it a vibrant and cosmopolitan place to study.
Name of Institution University of Strathclyde (Strathclyde Business School)
Address Strathclyde Business School, Undergraduate Office, Duncan Wing Level 3, 199 Cathedral
Street, Glasgow G4 0QU, United Kingdom
Telephone +44 141 548 4114
Website www.strath.ac.uk and www.strath.ac.uk/business
Helen Templar International Partnerships Manager (Partner Agreements) sbs-exchange@strath.ac.uk
Lorna Bennet International Exchange Coordinator (Incoming/Outgoing Exchange) sbs-exchange@strath.ac.uk
Michele French Exchange Secretary sbs-exchange@strath.ac.uk
Christine Dodd Administrative Assistant (International) sbs-exchange@strath.ac.uk
Please note that dates are provisional and may be subject to change
Semester 1 Semester 2
Semester dates 19 September 2016 – 16 December 2016 16 January – 19 May 2017
(inc revision and exams)
Student housing opens 10 September 2016 – 7 January 2017 8 January – 10 June 2017
Orientation and Registration 12 – 16 September 2016 9 – 13 January 2017
Exchange Welcome Meeting 12 September 2016 9 January 2017
Classes begin 19 September 2016 16 January 2017
Exchange students are expected to remain at Strathclyde University until the end of
the examination period.
Key Dates http://www.strath.ac.uk/studying/currentstudent/keydates/

| ABOUT STRATHCLYDE BUSINESS SCHOOL |
| --- |

| GENERAL INFORMATION |
| --- |

| SBS EXCHANGE TEAM |
| --- |

| ACADEMIC CALENDAR |
| --- |

Nomination All nominations and applications must be made online via the University’s central application
portal (Mobility Online). Paper applications are no longer accepted.
Partners should nominate their students using the login instructions provided by the
Recruitment and International Office. Please contact international.exchange@strath.ac.uk if
you do not have a log-in
Further information on how to apply can be found at
http://www.strath.ac.uk/rio/howtoapply/
Application Students must first be nominated by the exchange coordinator at their home institution. Once
a nomination is approved, students will receive an email inviting them to register with Mobility
Online to enable them to submit a full exchange application.
Nomination Deadline Semester 1 (September entry) Semester 2 (January entry)
1st May 1st October
Application Deadline Semester 1 (September entry) Semester 2 (January entry)
15th May 15th October
Step by Step http://www.strath.ac.uk/media/ps/rio/exchange/pdfs/Student_Application_Guide.pdf
Application Guide
Application  Current academic transcript
Documents required  Academic reference
 Copy of the student’s passport information page.
Student Housing International exchange (non-Erasmus) students will normally be guaranteed campus housing
unless there are any extenuating circumstances in which case alternative arrangements will be
put in place and partner institutions will be notified.
Students can apply for campus housing as an integrated part of the online application process.
Deadlines are as noted above and students should ensure they submit their application prior
to the deadline in order to be considered for campus accommodation.
The Accommodation Office will email applicants in July/August (for applicants commencing
studies in September) and in December (for applicants commencing studies in January) with
further information concerning their accommodation arrangements.
Acceptance Acceptance documents will be sent by email from the University’s central Admissions Office
when applications have been approved. Please ensure that the email address provided in your
application has sufficient capacity to receive large files
Class Selection Details of classes offered in the Business School can be found in the SBS Class Catalogue at the
following link. Guidance is also provided on choosing classes at:
http://www.strath.ac.uk/business/undergraduate/international/incoming/informationaboutcl
asses
Classes Open to Exchange students take classes at Levels 1 to 3. Level 2 and 3 classes will require some
Exchange Students previous study in the subject.
Students registered in the Business faculty must take the majority of their classes with us. It
may be possible for students to take one class in another Faculty, subject to approval by the
relevant department.
Students should submit a list of provisional classes as part of their online application. Due to
potential timetable clashes or classes being cancelled or withdrawn, or high demand for
popular subjects, it is not possible to guarantee access to specific classes and applicants are
encouraged to identify some reserves which can be substituted as necessary. Students are
permitted to request curriculum changes during the first two weeks of the semester.

| APPLICATION PROCEDURE – UNDERGRADUATE NON-GRADUATING STUDENTS |
| --- |

Restricted Classes Level 4 classes at SBS are final year classes and assume extensive knowledge of the academic
subject, and are therefore not generally open to exchange students. In exceptional
circumstances, access to a Level 4 class may be considered if the student can provide evidence
of significant relevant study in the subject and can meet all prerequisite knowledge for that
class. Access to Level 4 classes is extremely limited and must be approved by the relevant
department.
Note: Level 4 classes are examined in the April/May diet only. Resits are not offered at Level 4.
Credits A full workload at Strathclyde University is 60 credits (30 ECTS) per semester. This normally
equates to 3 classes per semester. Students attending for a full academic year would normally
register for 120 credits (60 ECTS). Students are not usually permitted to exceed the maximum
workload of 60 credits (30 ECTS) per semester.
Academic Transcripts Once students’ marks have been validated by the Faculty Board of Examiners, 2 original
academic transcripts will be forwarded to the home University. For students who attend in
Semester 1, transcripts will normally be mailed by the end of February. For students who
attend in Semester 2 or for the full academic year, transcripts will normally be mailed by the
end of July.
UG Grading Scale Mark General Comment Equivalent Grade
70+ Excellent or Outstanding A
60-69 Comprehensively Good B
50-59 Generally Good C
45-49 Satisfactory D
40-44 Satisfactory E
<40 Weak - Fail FX/F
Student Health Service www.strath.ac.uk/studenthealth
Visa Requirements Information on Tier 4 visas and student visitor visas can be found at
http://www.strath.ac.uk/sees/infoint/visasandpbs/
Preparing to come to For more information on coming to the University of Strathclyde and the city of Glasgow,
Strathclyde our Welcome arrangements, cost of living, health matters and pre-arrival advice please
visit http://www.strath.ac.uk/sees/infoint
Only 1% of the world’s business schools are triple accredited: Strathclyde is one of them
http://www.strath.ac.uk/business/accreditations/
Like our Facebook page SBS Student Exchanges
Revised Feb 2016

text:
2026 Fall Semester Fact Sheet: Sungkyunkwan University (SKKU)
For Inbound Exchange & Visiting Students

| ○ List of Contents |
| --- |
| ① General & Contact Information ② Nomination Information ③ Application Information ④ Academic Calendar ⑤ Acceptance Package ⑥ Exchange/Visiting Student Orientation ⑦ Expected Arrival Date ⑧ SKKU Credit System ⑨ Maximum Credits & Credit Conversion ⑩ Course Information ⑪ IEC (International Exchange Course): Course Packet for Exchange/Visiting Student ⑫ Korean Language Program (RKP, IKP, BKP) ⑬ Accommodation (Dormitory) ⑭ Visa and Residence Card (formerly ARC, Alien Registration Card) ⑮ National Health Insurance System (NHIS) ⑯ Buddy Program: HI-Club & SG MAPLE ⓐ SKKU ISS (International Summer Semester) ⓑ SKKU WISE (Winter International Student Experience) |

| ① General & Contact Information |  |
| --- | --- |
| Office Name | Sungkyunkwan University, Office of International Relations (SKKU OIR) |
| Campuses | ■ Humanities and Social Sciences Campus (Seoul) ■ Natural Sciences Campus (Suwon) |
| Contact Information | ■ Office of International Relations Tel: +82-2-760-0156 / Fax: +82-2-760-0159 / Email: incoming@skku.edu ■ Dormitory Office Tel: +82-2-760-0163 / Fax: +82-2-760-0159 / Email: dorms@skku.edu |
| English Homepage | http://www.skku.edu/eng |
| Inbound Program | https://www.skku.edu/eng/International/StudySKKU/Introduction.do |
| Office Address | Office of International Relations (#90212), International Hall, Sungkyunkwan University, 25-2, Sungkyunkwan-ro, Jongno-gu, Seoul 03063, South Korea |

| ② Nomination Information |  |
| --- | --- |
| Home University’s Nomination Procedure | ■ Applicants must be officially nominated by their home institution to apply. ■ The sending institution's officer must notify the SKKU OIR by completing the provided form, which will be sent via email, and provide a list of nominated students. ■ Period of stay can be either 1 semester or 2 semesters, but extension is not allowed once nominated. |
| Nomination & Application Deadlines | ■ Exchange Students (Nomination) Spring Semester: October 15th Fall Semester: April 15th ■ Visiting students (Email Application) Spring Semester: October 15th Fall Semester: April 15th |
| Tuition Fees for Visiting Students (Not applicable to Exchange Students) | ■ Payment Visiting Students are required to pay the SKKU tuition fee. ■ Estimated Cost Approximately KRW 5,200,000~8,100,000 per semester, depending on the major. (USD Reference: Approximately USD 3,600~5,600 / Based on the exchange rates as of March 5, 2026) ※ Note: Tuition fees are subject to change based on the exchange rate.) |

| ③ Application Information |  |
| --- | --- |
| Online Application | ■ Website: https://kingoinfo.skku.edu/gaia/nxui/outdex.html?language=EN&menuId=NIBGG040301M ■ Browser Compatibility: Optimized for Microsoft Edge, Chrome, and Firefox. (It may not function properly on Safari) ■ Authentication Code · Exchange Students: Provided after SKKU OIR receives an official nomination. · Visiting Students: Provided upon receipt of an inquiry email from the applicant or a nomination from the home institution. |
| Application Guide | The Online Application Guide can be downloaded from the online application website. |
| Eligibility | All applicants must meet the following criteria: ■ Nomination: Must be officially nominated/recommended by the home or sending institution (applies ONLY to exchange students). ■ Academic Standing: Must have completed at least one year of study at the home institution by the application period. ■ Enrollment Status: Must be currently in the process of pursuing a degree at their home institution. ■ GPA Requirement: Must have a GPA above 2.5/4.0, 2.7/4.3, 3.0/4.5 or 3.3/5.0 1) When using a different GPA scale, students must provide an official letter from the institution confirming their GPA meets the specified criteria 2) Visiting students are not required to submit a GPA |
| Required Documents | ■ Formal photo (PNG or JPG format) ■ Valid passport (copy of the personal identification page) ■ Certificate of enrollment ■ Official Academic Transcript (showing cumulative records for all courses taken up to the application date) ■ Language Certificate (Applies ONLY to students choosing Business Administration at SKKU) ■ Participation Agreement (Available on the first page of the online application website) |
| Language Requirement | ■ Applicability: Applies ONLY to students who choose Business Administration majors at SKKU. Minimum Scores (Choose one): 1) TOEFL: iBT 80 / ITP 550 2) IELTS: 6.0 or above 3) English CEFR: B2 or above 4) CET: 4 or above 5) TOPIK: 3 or above 6) Duolingo English Test: 110 or above ■ Important Note: Proof of English proficiency certified by a home university (other than the official test scores listed above) is NOT accepted. Exemptions: Not required for students who meet at least one of the following 1) Native speakers 2) Students applying for majors other than Business Administration 3) Applicants from institutions where English is the primary language of instruction (A formal letter from the home university confirming this statement is required) |
| Online Application Period | ■ Spring Semester: October 1st ~ October 31st ■ Fall Semester: April 1st ~ April 30th ■ Late applications will NOT be accepted. ■ Application Confirmation: Please note that individual confirmation of application receipt will not be sent. ■ Follow-up Contact: The office will reach out only to those who require changes or additional document submissions after the application period has concluded |

| ④ Academic Calendar |  |
| --- | --- |
| Academic Semesters | ■ 2026 Spring Semester: March 3rd ~ June 22nd, 2026 (tentative) ■ 2026 Fall Semester: August 31st ~ December 18th, 2026 (tentative) |
| Academic Year | ■ 2026 AY: March 1st, 2026 ~ February 28th, 2027 (tentative) ■ 2027 AY: March 1st, 2027 ~ February 29th, 2028 (tentative) |

| ⑤ Acceptance Package |
| --- |
| ■ The SKKU OIR will provide each accepted exchange and visiting student with an Acceptance Package, which includes the Certificate of Admission (CoA) and a Letter of Acceptance (LoA) required for visa applications. ■ Timeline (Expected) Fall Semester: Late June to early July Spring Semester: Late December to early January ■ Important Condition for Issuance: Please be advised that the timeline above applies only to students who have successfully submitted all required documents in their complete and final form. ■ Warning on Delays: The issuance of the Acceptance Package is strictly contingent upon the verification of your documents. Any delay in submission or the submission of incomplete documents will directly result in a delay in the issuance of your package, which may subsequently affect your visa application schedule. |

| ⑥ Exchange/Visiting Student Orientation |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Date | August 28th(subject to change) | Venue | Humanities and Social Sciences Campus (Seoul) |

| ⑦ Expected Arrival Date |
| --- |
| ■ Early Arrival: It is highly recommended that students arrive at SKKU a few days earlier than the orientation date. ■ Deadline: If a student does not arrive in Korea by September 8th, his/her exchange program will automatically be cancelled. ■ Course Registration: Please note that no additional course registration sessions will be provided for late arrivals, as the registration process is conducted entirely online. |

| ⑧ SKKU Credit System |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SKKU Credit | Class Hours / semester | Self-Study Hours / semester | SKKU Credit | Class Hours / semester | Self-Study Hours / semester |
| 1 | 15 hrs | 30 hrs | 4 | 60 hrs | 120 hrs |
| 2 | 30 hrs | 60 hrs | 5 | 75 hrs | 150 hrs |
| 3 | 45 hrs | 90 hrs | 6 | 90 hrs | 180 hrs |
| ■ Credit Transferability: Students must consult with their home university regarding the compatibility and transferability of credits earned at SKKU, as the home institution holds the final authority over credit recognition. ■ Credit Definition: To earn one (1) SKKU credit per semester, students must complete a minimum of 45 hours of study, which includes 15 hours of in-class instruction and 30 hours of individual self-study. |  |  |  |  |  |

| ⑨ Maximum Credits & Credit Conversion |
| --- |
| ■ Maximum Credits: 18 SKKU credits (Approximately 6~7 courses) ■ Credit Conversion & Transfer: The credit transfer policy should be determined by the home institution. ■ SKKU can provide supporting information and references for credit conversion and transfer. ■ Important Policies 1) As all exchange and visiting students are classified as undergraduate (bachelor's degree) students in the SKKU system, they must follow a separate procedure for enrolling in graduate-level classes. 2) Details regarding graduate course enrollment will be announced during the course registration period. |

| ⑩ Course Information |  |
| --- | --- |
| Course Catalog | ■ Access: The Course Catalog is available on the official English website: http://www.skku.edu/eng ■ Navigation Path: Main > International > Study at SKKU > Inbound Exchange Program > Course Information > Course Catalog. ■ Syllabus Download: Course syllabi can be downloaded by double-clicking the specific course code within the catalog. |
| Course Registration | ■ Spring Semester: in February ■ Fall Semester: in August ■ Notification: Accepted students will be notified of the specific registration period and procedures via email. |
| □ The number of English-taught courses may be limited for undergraduate majors not listed below: Humanities and Social Sciences Natural Sciences and Engineering · Business Administration / Global Business Administration · Civil and Environmental Engineering · Economics / Global Economics · Software · Media & Communication · Systems Management Engineering · Political Science and Diplomacy · Mechanical Engineering · English Language and Literature · Architecture · Sociology · Psychology · Film, Television and Multimedia ■ Some courses in Global Business Administration and Global Economics may be restricted to exchange and visiting students. (Details regarding the above statement can be verified during the course registration period.) ■ Detailed restrictions for specific courses can be verified during the course registration period. □ The course restriction policy applies to various areas, including but not limited to the following programs: Graduate Programs Undergraduate Programs · Specialty Graduate Schools · School of Medicine - SKK Graduate School of Business · School of Pharmacy - SKK Graduate School of China · Public Affairs (course codes beginning with GLD) - Graduate School of Law · Law - Graduate School of Governance · College of Art - Graduate School of Education - Courses in the College of Art are open to exchange - Graduate School of TESOL/Translation and visiting students. However, please be advised that · Special Graduate Schools very few courses are conducted in English within this · Graduate School of Medicine college. · Graduate School of Pharmacy - The Theatre major is not open to exchange students. |  |

| Humanities and Social Sciences | Natural Sciences and Engineering |
| --- | --- |
| · Business Administration / Global Business Administration · Economics / Global Economics · Media & Communication · Political Science and Diplomacy · English Language and Literature · Sociology · Psychology · Film, Television and Multimedia | · Civil and Environmental Engineering · Software · Systems Management Engineering · Mechanical Engineering · Architecture |

| ⑭ Visa and Residence Card |
| --- |
| ■ Visa Requirements · Visa Types: Exchange students must apply for a D-2-6 visa, and visiting students must apply for a D-2-8 visa. Pre-entry Application: Students must secure their D-2 visa in their home country before entering Korea. · Important: SKKU is not responsible for any issues arising from entering Korea on a tourist visa (K-ETA). ■ Residence Card (formerly ARC) · Application Methods: You may apply for your Residence Card individually or through a group application managed by the university's designated agency (Hire Diversity). Please note that agency fees may apply. · Issuance Timeline: It typically takes about 45 days to receive the card. This timeline is subject to change by the Immigration Office and is the same for both individual and group applications. · Travel Restrictions: If you leave Korea after entering on a D-2 visa before your Residence Card is issued, your visa will be automatically invalidated. · International travel is only permitted after you have physically received your Residence Card. We strongly recommend planning trips after the midterm exams. ■ Visa Extensions · Personal Extensions: Requests for visa extensions for personal reasons after the semester ends must be handled individually. The university does not provide administrative assistance for post-program extensions. |

| ⑮ Mandatory Health Insurance: National Health Insurance Service (NHIS) |
| --- |
| ■ In accordance with Korean law, all international students holding a D-2 visa are required to subscribe to the National Health Insurance (NHI). ■ Automatic Enrollment: Enrollment occurs automatically once your Residence Card is issued. No separate application is required. ■ Monthly Premium: Approximately USD 60 per month. · Note: This fee is billed monthly. Students do not need to take any initial action for enrollment. ■ Visa Restrictions: Please be aware that failure to pay the monthly premiums may result in restrictions on visa extensions or other administrative disadvantages. ■ Supplemental Insurance: Since the NHI may not cover all medical contingencies (e.g., specific emergencies or private hospital room charges), we strongly recommend maintaining personal full-coverage insurance during your stay. |

| ⑯ Student Life & Buddy Program (SG MAPLE) |
| --- |
| ■ The SKKU OIR and HI-Club (a student group supporting international students) manage a dedicated buddy program called SG MAPLE. This program is designed to help you settle into Korean life and build lasting friendships with SKKU students. ■ Experience Korean Culture: Throughout the semester, you can participate in weekly or monthly cultural activities to experience various aspects of Korea. ■ Exciting Events & Field Trips: Enjoy your exchange period by joining field trips to famous tourist spots, participating in Sports Day, and engaging in diverse social events with your buddies. ■ Stay Connected: Follow the HI-Club on Instagram for the latest updates on events and matching schedules. ■ Instagram: @skku_hiclub |

and circumstances.

| ⓐ SKKU ISS (International Summer Semester) |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Description | The SKKU International Summer Semester (ISS) is an annual 4-week summer program hosted at Sungkyunkwan University. Details about this year’s program are available on the official website. Each year, the program brings together highly motivated students from partner universities around the world to study at SKKU’s Seoul campus and engage in a vibrant international learning environment. ISS offers a wide range of courses taught in English by renowned professors from leading universities worldwide, covering diverse academic fields. Some courses incorporate field trips and experiential learning activities, allowing students to connect classroom knowledge with real-world contexts in Seoul and beyond. In addition to regular academic courses, the program also offers a Research Internship Track, through which students can join research laboratories at SKKU and work closely with faculty members on academic research projects. Beyond the classroom, students participate in various cultural activities designed to introduce Korean history, traditions, and contemporary culture, creating opportunities to experience Korea while building friendships with peers from around the world. Exchange students are eligible for a 100% tuition scholarship, meaning that tuition fees are waived. (Please note that cultural activity fees may still apply.) |  |  |
| Official Website | https://summer.skku.edu (QuickLink) | Contact | issoffice@skku.edu / +82-2-760-0184 |

| ⓑ SKKU WISE (Winter International Student Experience) |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Description | The SKKU Winter International Student Experience (WISE) is an annual 3-week winter program held from late December to early January. Details about this year’s program are available on the official website. Similar to the summer program, WISE combines academic coursework with cultural experiences, offering students a unique opportunity to study in Korea during the winter season. Courses are delivered primarily by distinguished SKKU professors in an intensive 12-day format, allowing students to engage deeply with their subjects while experiencing campus life at SKKU. In addition to the academic program, students can participate in a range of cultural activities designed to introduce Korean history, traditions, and contemporary culture. Exchange students are eligible for a 100% tuition scholarship, meaning that tuition fees are waived. (Please note that cultural activity fees may still apply.) |  |  |
| Official Website | https://winter.skku.edu (QuickLink) | Contact | wiseoffice@skku.edu / +82-2-760-0184 |

General Eligibility
To be able to join our Exchange Program, students have to be nominated by their home university. Different
universities have different rules regarding credit transfer. To avoid any potential problems, we recommend that
students need to obtain the approval before joining the Exchange Program.
Application Process:
Step 1: Online Nomination by Partner University
The exchange coordinator of partner universities will receive an email regarding the online nomination
from the exchange coordinator of Chulalongkorn Business School. The nomination period and deadline will be
as follows:
Step 2: Online Application by Students
After nomination has been submitted, students will automatically receive instruction for application by
email. They are required to fill in an online form. The following supporting documents are required to upload
during:
2

1. Passport size color photo (with white background) taken no more than six months in polite attire
2. ID page of the student’s passport
3. Recent academic transcript (with English translation if applicable)
4. Proof of English proficiency (for a non-English native speaker only)

MBA Exchange 2026-27
The Schulich School of Business is locatedinToronto, the vibrant culturalandbusinessepicenterof Canada.
Renowned for its leadership in arts, finance andtechnology, Toronto is also celebrated as oneofthemostdiverse
cities in the world.At Schulich, we are thrilled to welcome your unique perspective, talentsandpresence,
enriching the diversefabricofour school community.

Nomination Information for Exchange Coordinators
Application Information for Students
Language Requirements
Students must demonstrate a high level of English proficiency. We assess proficiency through the following
methods:
Work Experience
It is strongly recommended that students have at least 2 years of full-time, post degree business-related
work experience. This experience is crucial as it provides a valuable reference point, enabling students to
actively contribute to class and group discussions.
Additionally, to the above, we trust that Exchange Coordinators will select suitable students to attend.

| IELTS – Academic | Minimum score: 7 |
| TOEIC (both required) | Minimum score: 850 |
| Post Secondary Classes Taught in English | Historical evidence that students have successfully pursued post- secondary studies in English |

Term Dates
Academic Information
Course Information
Graduate exchange students must have completed all master foundation (first year/core) courses and may only
enrol in MBA elective (upper level) courses at the Schulich School of Business. Elective courses feature small
class sizes and employ various teaching methods including lectures, case studies, individual and group
projects, term papers, presentations, exams and classroom discussions. Attendance is mandatory and class
participation contributes to the final grade.
A 3-credit course involves approximately 100 hours of work including 3 in-class hours per week over 12
weeks (36 in-class hours/course). A full course load for Schulich students is 5 courses (15 Schulich credits).
Exchange students are expected to enrol in a minimum of 3 courses (9 Schulich credits).
Elective courses may vary each term, and enrolment is not guaranteed so students should remain flexible.
Additional information can be found under Courses & Academics.
Exams
Final exams are scheduled for the week following the last day of classes. Students are advised not to make
travel plans before the end of the exam period however, students may leave early if all course requirements
are completed.
Grades & Transcripts
Students can view their grades online. Schulich uses a letter grade system: A+, A, A-, B+, B, B-, C+, C, C-, F.
An official transcript is sent to the home institution approximately 4-6 weeks after completion of the term.
Additional transcripts can be ordered online through the Registrar’s Office.
Code of Conduct
All students must adhere to the University’s code of conduct, which includes completing academic
integrity modules prior to the start of the term.

International Relations Support
Pre-Arrival Webinar
Before the start of each term, we provide information about arriving in Canada. This includes details on
required entry documents, housing, health insurance, transportation and other helpful resources.
Orientation
The mandatory Orientation offers valuable information and resources to help students prepare for their
journey and integrate into the Schulich community. During Orientation, students will meet the international
team as well as fellow Schulich and exchange students.
Visa Information & Immigration Support
Exchange students are responsible for obtaining the appropriate Canadian immigration documents to enter
Canada. Students studying for less than 6 months can enter and study as visitors but must apply for the
correct travel document (Temporary Resident Visa or electronic Travel Authorization) before arriving. A
Canadian study permit is not required. Please refer to the Visit Canada website to determine which document
is required (TRV or eTA). Students requiring a Temporary Resident Visa (TRV) should apply as early as possible
due to potentially lengthy processing times. Our team includes an immigration specialist to assist with any
questions or issues related to entry into Canada.
English Language Peer Support (ELPS) ADMISSIONS DEADLINES
The ELPS program offers students personalized English language assistance for assignments, cases, papers and
presentation skills. Students seeking support with English proficiency will collaborate with peer supporters,
who provide feedback on grammar, structure, citations and verbal presentation skills.
Health Services
University Health Insurance Plan (UHIP)
UHIP is mandatory for all exchange students and provides basic coverage for visits to doctors or hospitals.
York University administers UHIP registration before the start of the term. Students can opt for supplementary
insurance to cover additional costs not included in UHIP such as medications, dental and paramedical
services.
Student Accessibility Services (SAS)
Academic support and accommodation are available for students with disabilities including AD/HD, autism
spectrum disorders, mental health conditions, physical, sensory, medical and learning disabilities. Registration
and documentation are required and should be submitted once approved for exchange to ensure students receive
the necessary support.
Student Counselling & Development (SCD)
A professional and supportive environment ensures students have equitable access to a variety of services
that aid in their academic success.

Career Services
The Centre for Career Design (CCD) provides students with support to help them achieve their career goals.
Students have access to corporate information sessions, panel discussions, workshops, networking events,
individual counselling, resume reviews and mock interviews.
Student Life
Open Arms Committee (OAC)
The OAC connects exchange students with a
current MBA student to support their transition to
Schulich and Toronto.
Graduate Business Council (GBC)
The GBC advocates for the interests of all
graduate students to faculty and Schulich
administration. It organizes activities that foster
interactions with the business community,
recreational programs and social events.
Schulich’s clubs offer valuable opportunities for
students to explore business interests and develop
leadership skills. From Canadian mining to
investment banking to sustainable enterprise, the
variety of clubs allows students to pursue a broad
spectrum of interests. Exchange students are
encouraged to participate in these clubs during
the term.
Housing
York University’s Housing Services provides on-campus housing options. For information on both on-
campus and off-campus housing, refer to Schulich’s Student Housing Opportunities website. Students are
responsible for securing their own accommodations. On-campus housing is not guaranteed.

text:
NUCB Business School
International Programs
NUCB Business School offers two degree programs entirely in English: the MSc in Management and the MBA.
Starting in Fall 2025, we will also be launching our English-taught program in MSc in Business Analytics and AI. The
goal of our programs is to cultivate highly skilled professionals with a global perspective, a strong sense of ethics,
and the ability to lead and contribute positively to the international business community.
Nagoya University of Commerce and Business, founded by Dr. Yuichi Kurimoto in 1953, is a private university
operated by the Kurimoto Educational Institution and situated in Nisshin, just outside Japan’s third-largest city,
Nagoya. Animated by the “Frontier Spirit,” symbolizing the strong spirit of being at the frontier of knowledge and
communications, the NUCB family of schools includes the NUCB Undergraduate School and the Graduate School
of Management, NUCB Business School. Alongside the university’s strong commitment to excellence in case
method teaching and research are its internalization efforts, from which it has developed alliances with
international institutions in Asia, Europe, North America, and Latin America, and emerged as the first and currently
only Japanese business school to be accredited by AACSB in 2006, AMBA in 2009, and EQUIS in 2021, thus
achieving the renowned Triple Crown accreditation status in 15 years’ time.
NUCB Business School has partnerships with over one hundred leading business schools across more than fifty
countries, 86% of which are accredited by the international accreditation bodies. Dozens of students from leading
business schools around the world select NUCB Business School each year for their study exchange program, and,
with its induction into the Partnership in International Management Network as its 68th member in 2022, there will
surely be many more to come. As part of our commitment to excellence and ongoing contribution to international
management education, we are actively engaged with these partner schools through various types of programs
and initiatives. Collaborations with our partner schools include, but are not limited to, activity in the following areas:

Programs
Case Method Learning
The case method is at the core of our academic experience. The practice-oriented learning methodology built on
participant-centered learning aims to prepare students for strategic decision-making through the practice of real
business. This learning approach prepares you for the real world as a business leader better than any lecture-based
program ever could. Course materials consist of the latest business cases from renowned case publication
houses, such as Harvard Business Publishing, INSEAD, and Ivey Publishing.

text:
Waseda Business School
Graduate School of Business and Finance
WASEDA University
Exchange Programme Fact Sheet
Academic Year 2026
1

Actionable Knowledge
Unlock Your Potential
Mission Statement
WBS creates a dynamic learning community for all stakeholders as a
catalyst for developing insightful and responsible global leaders with
actionable management knowledge.
Choosing WASEDA Business School (WBS)
◼ One of the Best Business Schools in Japan
The WBS International MBA Programme has been ranked third in Japan
while the Master of Science in Finance Programme has been placed first
in Japan by the QS World University Rankings 2025.
◼ AACSB and EQUIS Accredited School
WBS is one of only two business schools in Japan that have been
accredited by AACSB and EQUIS.
◼ Dynamic Student Diversity
Students experience culturally diverse discussions and networking with
future international business leaders.
◼ Top-class Faculty
You are promised well-rounded learning from faculty members with
both high academic standards and extensive practical experience.
2

Mailing address Waseda Business School, Waseda University
3rd Floor, Building 11, Waseda Campus
1-6-1, Nishi-Waseda, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo 169-8050, JAPAN
Telephone +81-3-5286-8719
E-mail wbs-intl@list.waseda.jp
Website http://www.waseda.jp/fcom/wbs/en
*Completed at least one year of full-time study at the home institution by the time of
arrival at Waseda Business School.
*Must be nominated by the home institution.
*Level of Study for Incoming Students: Graduate Student / MBA Student
*Very strong command of English
Students are not required to submit an English Language score. If the student has a
test score (TOEFL/ IELTS), he/ she is encouraged to submit it. A high level of English
proficiency is required the courses are taught in English.
*Having at least three years of work experience (highly recommended).
https://www.waseda.jp/fcom/wbs/en/students-and-alumni/calendar
3

| General Information |
| --- |

| Applicant Qualifications | Applicant Qualifications |
| --- | --- |

| Academic Calendar &Class Schedule | Academic Calendar &Class Schedule |
| --- | --- |

| Fall Semester | Orientation (Online): Mid-September Class Starts: Early October Class Ends: Late January (including final exams) Fall Intensive: Early February (Optional) |
| --- | --- |
| Spring Semester | Orientation (Online): Late March Class Starts: Early April Class Ends: Late-July (including final exams) Spring Intensive: Early August (optional) |
| Holidays (Fall Semester) | Waseda Festival: First Week of November Winter Vacation: Late December to Early January Spring Vacation: Early February to Late March |
| Holidays (Spring Semester) | May Break: Subject to Annual Updates Summer Vacation: Early August to September 20 |

For Students: Students must be nominated by their home institutions. Nominated
students will be contacted by the WBS Office via email and requested to submit the
following documents, including the visa application documents.
1. Application Form for Exchange Program & Certificate of Eligibility (COE)
2. Academic Objectives, Research & Study Plan
3. Latest Transcript or Certificate of Academic Records from Home Institution
4. Statement of Financial Resources
5. Certification of Financial Resources to Cover Living Expenses while Living in Japan
6. Colored Scanned Copy of Applicant’s Passport (Page with Photograph)
*If there is a page indicating travel limitations and other important details, please
also include the page.
7. Digital File of Passport-Sized Photograph that will be used for Student ID Card and
Residence Card (Headshots with Plain Background; 3 x 4)
VISA Procedure
The Certificate of Eligibility (COE) is a necessary document for student visa issuance.
WBS will apply for the COE based on the information the student provides. As soon as
it is issued, an electronic version of the COE, Certificate of Admission and Letter of
Acceptance will be emailed to the student. Upon receipt, students are required to
apply for a student visa at the nearest Embassy of Japan or Consulate on his/ her own.
・When COEs are expected to be issued:
Fall Semester: Middle/ End of August to Early September
Spring Semester: Late February to Early March
http://www.mofa.go.jp/j_info/visit/visa/long/visa6.html
4

| Nomination/Application Periods and Required Documents |
| --- |
| Nomination Fall Semester: April 3 to April 30 / Spring Semester: October 3 to November 2 Application Fall Semester: April 3 to May 8 / Spring Semester: October 3 to November 9 Official Acceptance Announcement Fall Semester: Early July Spring Semester: Early January |

5

| Programme Information |  |
| --- | --- |
|  | Courses Available for Exchange Students |
| Credits and Workload of Courses Our class structure is 100 minutes per class with a 14-week workload of approximately 23.5 hours, equivalent to 2 credits, including lectures, classes, contact hours, assignments, examinations and independent study. The WBS strongly encourages at least three courses per quarter. Exchange students can enroll up to ten WBS courses (20 credits). The designated course list for exchange students will be shared one month before the commencement of each semester. The course registration will take place online during the registration period. Students are strongly advised to consult with the coordinator(s) at the home institution regarding the academic requirements of his/ her home institution. Reference Only: List of Courses (Spring 2025 Semester) https://waseda.box.com/s/w8amf7g8qh051dj29nk98mauwuu582c9 List of Courses (Fall 2025 Semester) https://waseda.box.com/s/nse9j6bzxaziyky2g2o8ajprx7h7ze0z List of Courses (Spring 2026 Semester) https://waseda.box.com/s/koyvtqn3meww6vpwr3p75ype3poei7dr *The course lists are subject to change every quarter/ semester. There is no guarantee that the courses will be offered in the subsequent quarters/ semesters. Syllabus Search https://www.wsl.waseda.jp/syllabus/JAA101.php?pLng=en MBA Programme Elective and bilingual courses offered at the MBA programme are open to the exchange students. Seminars, Core courses, IMBA Elective Core courses and overseas courses are not open to the exchange students. MSc in Finance Programme Elective core subjects are open to exchange students. |  |

|  | Other Courses |
| --- | --- |
| Japanese Language Courses offered by the Center for Japanese Language (CJL) Japanese language courses are available to the exchange students. Should the number of applicants exceed class capacity, a lottery system will be implemented where students are randomly selected for course enrolment. As of AY2025, exchange students do not need to pay extra fees. Please note that it is subject to change. http://www.waseda.jp/cjl/en/index.html |  |

Living & Personal Expenses
Approximately 150,000 Japanese Yen + per month, depending on one’s lifestyle and
the choice of accommodation (dormitory/ shared house/ private apartment, etc.).
When you submit your application, you must be able to show official proof (bank
statements, etc.) that you are able to allocate at least 150,000 Japanese Yen per month
as living expenses in Japan. Please note that the costs of living have raised in Japan.
Accommodation
Waseda University Dormitories
https://www.waseda.jp/inst/rlc/en/student_dormitory/
https://www.waseda.jp/inst/rlc/en/undergraduate/application/exchange/
Should you prefer to rent an apartment or stay in a shared house, etc., please refer
to the Waseda University Student Housing Centre website.
https://waseda-housing.com/international/
6

| Courses offered by the Other Graduate Schools at Waseda University Some courses offered by the other graduate schools are available to the exchange students. Most courses are offered on the Waseda or West Waseda campuses, but there are some courses in the areas of sports business and information analysis may be offered at the distant campuses. To learn more, please refer to the syllabus. These courses count toward the maximum number of courses (10) that WBS exchange students may take. More details, including a list of courses and the registration schedules for each semester, can be found on the following website. Course Registration – Global Education Center (GEC) (waseda.jp) |  |  |  |  |  |

| Other Important Information | Other Important Information |
| --- | --- |

Facilities
Each exchange student will receive a Waseda University student ID card. With the ID
card, students can access the various facilities on campus.
e.g., PC rooms, libraries, gymnasium*, swimming pool*, etc.
*A medical checkup (submission of medical reports/ certificates/ X-ray, etc.) and a pre-
registration are required to use these facilities. The Health Support Center can direct the
students to an external medical institution for the necessary health check-up or medical
examination.
Academic Calendar (AY2026)
*Subject to Change
Spring Semester (14 weeks): April 11 - July 22, 2026
(July 23 - 29 is the make-up class week)

| MBA Program International University of Japan (IUJ) Fact Sheet for Exchange Programs 2027/2028 |
| OUR LOCATION ACCESS TO IUJ Global Learning, From Tokyo Rooted in Japan Approx. 1 hr 45 min by Shinkansen IUJ is located in Minamiuonuma City, From Narita International Airport Niigata Prefecture, in the heart of Japan. Approx. 2 hr 30 min by train Surrounded by rich nature and four distinct seasons, IUJ offers the ideal environment for From Tokyo International Airport (Haneda) focused study, cross-cultural learning, and Approx. 2 hr 30 min by train personal growth. WHY STUDY AT IUJ RICH NATURAL SURROUNDINGS Study in a peaceful setting surrounded by mountains and nature. SAFE AND WELCOMING COMMUNITY Join a close-knit international community where students from around the world live and learn together. GATEWAY TO JAPAN Discover Japanese culture and daily life while staying connected to Tokyo and beyond. 1 |

| ACADEMIC FRAMEWORK Language of Instruction All courses are conducted entirely in English. Credit System 1 credit = 8 × 90-minute sessions (12 classroom hours). Grading System Grades are awarded on a scale from A (4.00) to F (0.00). Cross-Registration System Students are free to take courses from both the Graduate School of International Management (GSIM) and the Graduate School of International Relations (GSIR). Course Offerings A wide range of courses is available in Finance, Marketing, Management, Data Analytics, Sustainability, Innovation and Entrepreneurship, Digital Technology and Operations and Japanese-Style Management. Japanese Language Courses Variable credits are awarded according to proficiency level, with courses offered from beginner to advanced. ACADEMIC CALENDAR AND APPLICATION DEADLINES Fall 2027 Winter 2028 1st Module: Oct. 4 – Nov. 27 1st Module: Jan. 10 – Mar. 4 2nd Module: Nov. 29 – Dec. 11 2nd Module: Mar. 6 – Mar. 18 Exam Week: Dec. 13 – Dec. 17 Exam Week: Mar. 20 – Mar. 24 Deadline for Nomination: Apr. 12, 2027 Deadline for Nomination: Aug. 23, 2027 Deadline for Application: Apr. 29, 2027 Deadline for Application: Sep. 6, 2027 Spring 2028 Summer 2028 (intensive courses only) 1st Module: Apr. 3 – May 27 Mid June – Late July 2nd Module: May 29 – June 10 Deadline for Nomination: Feb. 14, 2028 Exam Week: June 12 – June 15 Deadline for Application: Feb. 28, 2028 Deadline for Nomination: Oct. 11, 2027 (Subject to change.) Deadline for Application: Oct. 25, 2027 REQUIRED APPLICATIONS DOCUMENTS Nominated students are required to submit the following documents via email at ofcintl@iuj.ac.jp by the designated deadline set for each term: • Exchange application form (available at www.iuj.ac.jp/im-info/exchange-programs/) • Latest resume (must be typed) • Latest official academic record (transcript at your home institution) • A copy of applicant’s passport clearly showing his/her name, birth date, passport number. |
| --- |
| 2 |

| HOUSING AND INTERNET CONNECTION IUJ guarantees on-campus housing for all exchange students in one of its three dormitories, each just a short walk from classrooms and campus facilities. Every room is fully equipped with free high-speed internet (wired and wireless), creating a convenient and supportive living environment from the very first day. More info: http://www.iuj.ac.jp/cs/. ESTIMATED MONTHLY LIVING EXPENSES • Dormitory fee: Up to JPY 39,000/month *10,000 JPY of a maintenance fee at check-in • Meals: JPY 30,000~ /month • Academic Materials: JPY 10,000~ /term • Miscellaneous: JPY 30,000~ /month VISA SUPPORT To support your entry to Japan, IUJ will apply for your Certificate of Eligibility (CoE) on your behalf and send it to you upon issuance. With this document, you can apply for a Student Visa at the Japanese embassy or consulate in your country. Full visa assistance is provided throughout the process. More info: https://www.iuj.ac.jp/admis/visa/ HEALTH INSURANCE Enrollment in Japan’s National Health Insurance (NHI) is mandatory for those who obtain a Student Visa. With NHI, students pay only 30% of medical costs at clinics or hospitals. The premium is about JPY 5,000 per term. However, as NHI does not cover car accident injuries, students are strongly advised to obtain additional travel insurance before arrival. ALUMNI NETWORK Your connection with IUJ doesn't end when your exchange does. As an exchange student, you are invited to become an Honorary IUJ Alum, giving you access to a vibrant global network of alumni and lifelong connections with the IUJ community. 3 |
| --- |

| VOICES FROM OUR EXCHANGE STUDENTS My exchange at IUJ offered unique insights into Japan’s business culture while immersing me in a diverse international community. It broadened my perspective, strengthened my cross-cultural skills, and made my time truly unforgettable. Edoardo from SDA Bocconi (Italy) My exchange at IUJ revealed how global strategies can be digitally driven yet locally adapted, while offering insights into technologies shaping industries worldwide. The experience expanded my leadership perspective and inspired me to embrace growth and new opportunities. Thembelihle from GIBS (South Africa) At IUJ, I built close friendships in a warm international community, learned from diverse cultures, and explored Japan. It is one of the few places where all of this comes together, making my experience truly unforgettable. Dean from Tuck (United States) |

General Eligibility
To be able to join our Exchange Program, students have to be nominated by their home university. Different
universities have different rules regarding credit transfer. To avoid any potential problems, we recommend that
students need to obtain the approval before joining the Exchange Program.
Application Process:
Step 1: Online Nomination by Partner University
The exchange coordinator of partner universities will receive an email regarding the online nomination
from the exchange coordinator of Chulalongkorn Business School. The nomination period and deadline will be
as follows:
Step 2: Online Application by Students
After nomination has been submitted, students will automatically receive instruction for application by
email. They are required to fill in an online form. The following supporting documents are required to upload
during:
2
Document required:
1. Passport size color photo (with white background) taken no more than six months in polite attire
2. ID page of the student’s passport
3. Recent academic transcript (with English translation if applicable)
4. Proof of English proficiency (for a non-English native speaker only)

5. A recent transcript from current institution (with English translation if applicable)
6. Proof of English proficiency (for a non-native speaker only)
- TOEFL 550 (paper-based) or 213 (computer-based) or 79 (ibt), or
- IELTS 6.5, or
- Common European Framework of Reference (CEFR) minimum B2
7. Resume
8. Two letters of recommendation from former/current instructors or former/current employers

to take the courses according to their field of study or specialization. Also, please be aware of the difference

ABOUT US
Thammasat Business School (TBS) was established in
1938. It offers a wide range of business and
management education in various fields from bachelor’s
to doctoral levels with the use of English language as a
medium of instruction. They include accounting, finance
and banking, marketing, management information
systems, entrepreneurship and human resource
management, operation management, international
business, logistics and transport management, and real
estate business.
Thammsat Business School was considered one of the
best business school in Thailand, and it was awarded
with the EQUIS Accreditation in 2012, the AACSB
Accreditation in 2017, and the AMBA Accreditation in
2018 respectively proven our outstanding standards of
academic curriculum, faculty, research, and innovation.
Thammasat Business School is the only business school
Center for International Affairs
in Thailand selected to join a prestigious community of
leading business schools – Partnership in International
Management (PIM), a consortium of top business schools
from around the world that exchanges top– quality
undergraduate and graduate students between
Thammasat Business School and top- tier partner
universities.

text:
Welcome
to
Sasin
Bangkok,Thailand
Enjoy your time in one of Asia’s most livable city
Fact Sheet
2026-2027

Why Bangkok?
Sasin School of Management is located in the heart
of Bangkok, Thailand: a modern, cosmopolitan
metropolis with a rich history and culture. As the most
visited city in the world, the logistics hub of ASEAN
and one of the most dynamic cities in Southeast
Asia, it is fun, exciting, vibrant and one of the most
international and livable cities in the region.
Established in 1917, Chulalongkorn University is Thailand's
oldest and most prestigious academic institution,
located on a spacious campus in Bangkok’s Central
Business District.
Sasin occupies a prime position on that campus,
combining a peaceful park-like setting with easy
access to major office and shopping centers.
Bangkok's modern and efficient skytrain and metro
systems are a 5-10 minute walk away - just a few
minutes by the university's free electric shuttle service.
Why Sasin?
Established through a partnership of
Thailand's first globally 1st BSIS Impact School
accredited business school in Southeast Asia
GLOBAL MBA RANKINGS 2026 #1in FINANCIAL TIMES EMBA RANKING
Thailand TOP100
TOP25 TOP10
for Employability, IN THE WORLD
Entrepreneurship & Alumni Outcomes,
Return on Investment TOP20
in Asia in Southeast Asia SCHOOLS IN ASIA
global partners
in 20+ countries
2

Nomination
The Sasin Exchange Coordinator will email all partner institutions to fill out a nomination form.
After we agree and/or accept your nomination, students will receive their online application
link to their email.
The deadline of the nomination is 3 months prior to the first preferred module date. Given the
example, if the preferred module is Module 1 (June - July 2026), the nomination then must be
completed by March 2026.
Student Register (Online Application)
Nominated students will receive an email containing detailed instructions guiding them
through the online application in our portal. They can expect to receive this email by 3
months prior to their first module start date.
Academic Dates
Module 1 June 8 - July 11, 2026
Module 2 July 13 - August 15, 2026
Module 3 August 24 - September 26, 2026
Module 4 September 28 - October 31, 2026
Module 5 November 9 - December 12, 2026
Module 6 January 4 - February 6, 2027
Module 7 February 8 - March 13, 2027
Module 8 March 29 - May 1, 2027
Module 9 May 3 - June 5, 2027
Sample Courses
Data Science and Accounting for
AI & Business
Visualization for Business Decision Making
Dr. Stefano Starita Dr. Mark Finn Dr. Pinnaree Tea-Makorn
Faculty, Management Clinical Associate Professor of Faculty, Management
Accounting and International Business
Kellogg School of Management
Visiting Professor
Academic Policies
Class Attendance
Sasin’s attendance rules follow Chulalongkorn University’s policies that students must
maintain a minimum of 80% attendance in order to complete a course.
Please note: class schedules may change.
3

Course Registration
The course registration email will be sent to students about 1-2 weeks before the module
starts. There are specific add/drop and withdrawal periods where course selections can be
adjusted, but may be subject to certain grade penalties.
Please note: course materials are non-refundable.
Course Load
There are 2–5 courses offered per module. Exchange students may register for up to 2
courses. Each course carries 3 credits and is equivalent to 30 - 33 contact hours (including
exam or presentation hours).
The course offerings for each module are expected to be available approximately 3 - 4
months before the first module of the academic year.
There is no minimum or maximum course load requirement from Sasin for exchange students
for the entire exchange period.
Please note: Students should manage their credit load carefully, as the maximum number of courses
allowed per module is 2 (6 credits).
Elective Courses
Exchange students are limited to the selection of elective courses exclusively. For more
information about electives courses https://www.sasin.edu/mba-elective-courses
Estimated Expenses
Typical expenses for a one-month period in Bangkok:
Expense Price (Baht)
Housing at CU-iHouse 14,000
Utilities-electricity, telephone, etc. (approximately) 900
Meals (three times a day) 3,000
Course materials and academic expenses 2,000
Personal spending money 10,000
Total 29,900
Note: Your total expenses will depend on your individual preferences and lifestyle.
4

Visa Information
After you’re accepted into the exchange program, the Sasin Exchange Coordinator will send
an official acceptance letter from Sasin. You will need to submit that letter to your nearest
Thai Embassy or consulate to obtain your visa. You can apply for a Non-immigrant visa
(Non-ED) for education purposes, valid for at least 3 months.
You may then do the visa extension to cover your entire exchange period after arriving
Thailand and start your first module. More information will be informed when you joined the
orientation on the first date at Sasin.
**** Please check with your Thai Embassy/Consulate for current entry procedures.****
Re-Entry Permits
If you plan to travel outside Thailand for a short period and you have single entry education
visa, you must apply for a “re-entry permit” at the Immigration Bureau or at the airport before
leaving the country. You can request a single entry or multiple entries.
Requirements:
• 1,000 Baht for single re-entry;
• 3,800 Baht for multiple re-entry;
• TM 8 application form
• Your passport
• Your photograph (4 x 6 cm)
Sasin Exchange Coordinator can give you more information or go to
https://www.immigration.go.th
*Note: Fees are subject to change.
Health Insurance (Required)
We require all exchange students to have international health insurance to cover accidents
and health/medical issues during their time at Sasin.
At Sasin
Your first day
Your first day will typically be an orientation day. You will
meet the Student Experience team at the reception,
receive your Sasin ID, and get an introduction to Sasin,
including a facility tour.
5

Accommodation
On-Campus Housing
Sasa International House, closest to Sasin is located within a three-minute walk. Rates
starts from 1,600 THB/room/night and 25,200THB /month, which includes room cleaning
service but excludes breakfast & electricity bill.
CU iHouse - Chulalongkorn University, is a short walk from Sasin, just off-campus. Daily rental
rate starts from 1,000 THB/room/night, and the monthly rate starts from14,000 THB/month.
Upon check in, you must pay the 1-month rental fee and 1-month room deposit for a total of
28,000 baht. Your 1-month deposit will be returned to you after checkout (provided you
have stayed to term and there is no damage to the room).
If the length of your stay changes, you will have to inform CU-iHouse 1-month in order to process
the return of your deposit.
Additional details for on-campus living:
www.chula.ac.th/en/prospective-student/accommodation
Note: Rates are subject to change. Please check the price and terms & conditions directly with the
accommodation.
6

Sasin Facilities
Toemsakdi Krishnamra Hall Sasa Commons
The ultimate social space where
members of the Sasin community
and guests can eat, hangout, or
have a casual meeting.
Toemsakdi Krishnamra Hall, the focal point of
Sasin’s newly-renovated space, is used for
talks, workshops, and other events, reflecting
Professor Toemsakdi’s legacy of blending
influential people and important ideas.
Workshops & Meeting Rooms

A perfect space for collaboration and lifelong learning!

Students can access the Chulalongkorn Health Center
(on campus) or Student Experience on the 6th floor
for over-the-counter medicines.
Recreational Facilities
Partnered with Chulalongkorn University
7

Getting Around Bangkok
Bangkok public transport is a cheaper and
more exciting option, giving you much more
local traveling experience. You can find
various means of transportation in Bang-
kok-city trains (metro, skytrains), buses,
canal boats, and river ferries.

Courseload & Credits
The MBA elective period (year 2) is divided into 4 modules (2 each in fall
and spring). A student must enroll in a minimum of 3 courses and 4.5
elective credits per module to be considered full-time.
For the semester exchange, this equals 9 elective credits and 6 courses.
A student cannot take 2 courses in one module and 4 in the other, as the
minimum course load is 3. We recommend that students not take more
than 5 courses per module. However, students can be approved to take 6
courses per module if they are required to do so by their home university.
Generally, a class consists of 20 in-class contact hours and 30 out-of-
class (study groups, case readings, etc.) hours.
Transcript
A digital transcript will automatically be sent to the international office
of the partner school that nominated their students. If the student has a
stop/hold on their academic account, a transcript cannot be released. Campus Health
UNC Campus Health requires all students to have health insurance.
Visiting exchange students can waive UNC’s insurance if their insurance
policy covers UNC’s minimum requirements.
Health insurance policies for international students need to meet these
minimum necessary requirements:
• A minimum medical benefit of $100,000 coverage for each specific
illness or injury.
• A deductible not to exceed $500 per accident or illness.
• Provide at least $25,000 in benefits for repatriation of remains to the
home country in case of death.
• Pay up to $50,000 for medical evacuation to the home country.
Immunizations are mandatory for all students entering the University.
Students attending one module only are exempted from submitting
immunization documents.
Exchange students have full access to campus health facilities and resources.

Onboarding
Orientation takes place at the beginning of each term. This is comprised
of two days of mandatory sessions covering legal services, health
insurance, academics, honor code, class attendance policy, and more.
Airport pick-up is available.
Students who wish to participate in the Buddy program will have a Full-
Time MBA student assigned to partner with them.

resume book, are not included.

text:
Better Business – Better Society
Aalto University School of Business is the leading business school in
Finland and ranks among the best in Europe. We offer our students
multidisciplinary, international learning experiences and opportunities to
solve real-world challenges in an international context. At the School of
Business, we work for better business and a better society.
Finland
Finland offers a great place for living with or without family. It is a safe, politically
stable and well-organized Nordic society where equality is esteemed very high and
corruption is very low. Finland’s free high quality education system is acknowledged
worlwide.
In Finland, a low level of hiearchy is considered a strong characteristic and that goes
to studying at the university as well - the professors are very approachable and they
can be addressed by their first name.
Housing
The main student housing organization in the Helsinki region is HOAS (Foundation
for Student Housing in the Helsinki Region). Another student housing organization is
AYY (Aalto University Student Union). Kindly note that AYY does not offer furnished
apartments. Student apartments typically consist of 3-5 bedrooms, a shared living
room, kitchen and bathroom. The apartments are situated around the Helsinki area
and students apply for housing directly through the above mentioned organizations.

Lectures and exams: Sept to mid-Dec Lectures and exams: Jan to May/June

Full academic calendar

and 4 finish their studies by beginning of May.

already before June.

to Lingnan’s classrooms.
Single, shared and well‐furnished apartments are available for students’

Volunteer buddies at Lingnan will assist exchange students on looking for a

Lingnan (University) College
Originating from Lingnan University, a private university established in the late 19th century, Lingnan
(University) College was reestablished in 1989 within Sun Yat‐sen University and is now one of the
leading schools in economics and management in China.
Guided by Lingnan’s motto “Education for Service”, the College provides high quality education and
research in economics, finance and management.
Lingnan offers a diversified portfolio of programs, including Undergraduate, Master’s, MBA, EMBA, and
PhD programs, together with international programs such as China Executive MBA, International MBA,
and Master’s in International Business. These programs, especially the Undergraduate and MBA
programs, are of the most popular and selective programs in South China.
Lingnan has an outstanding faculty with 100 members and a student population of around 3,000. As a
research‐active college, Lingnan is tirelessly striving for excellence in teaching and research,
advancement of knowledge, development of future leaders, and service to China and the global society.
Lingnan embraces a balance between liberal arts education and specialized education, with an emphasis
on the development of students with well-rounded personalities, critical skills, citizenship and global
vision.
Globalization is the trademark of Lingnan (University) College. The College is actively engaged in
international collaborations and has established extensive global partnerships with leading global
business schools through student exchanges, faculty exchanges, double degree programs, international
summer schools, study abroad trips, joint research, and academic seminars. Currently, Lingnan has
established exchange agreements with over 40 partner schools from 20 countries and regions in Europe,
Asian‐Pacific area and North America.
Lingnan is among the select few schools that have received all three international accreditations: AMBA,
EQUIS and AACSB.
For more information, please visit: http://lingnan.sysu.edu.cn/en

Life in Guangzhou
Located at the north of the Pearl River delta, Guangzhou is an important trading center as well as a busy
port and the capital city of the province of Guangdong. Guangzhou is one of the most important centers
of foreign commerce in South China. Guangzhou is also the host city for the 16th Asian Games which is
held in November, 2010
History
With a history of 2,200 years, Guangzhou is regarded as the earliest among international port cities in
the world. In ancient time, Guangzhou was the capital city for three Chinese dynasties: the Nan Yue
(South Yue), the Nan Han (South Han) and the Nanming (South Ming); the starting point of the Silk Road
on the sea which links China with Arabian and western countries in trade. It was China’s only foreign
trade port at sea before the Qing dynasty. The historic sights of Guangzhou include the Nan Yue King
Museum, the Zhenhai Tower and the Sun Yat‐sen Memorial Hall, which tell us the long history of
Guangzhou. Today, Guangzhou retains its ancient customs while developing steadfastly into a modern
and vigorous metropolitan city.
Food in Guangzhou
"Eating in Guangzhou" has become a popular saying both at home and abroad. Guangzhou ranks first in
the number of restaurants and tea‐houses in the country. Cantonese cuisine is good in color, fragrance,
taste and presentation. In addition, the delicate Cantonese pastry is also well‐known for its wide range
of varieties, delicious flavor and beautiful color. Cantonese cuisine is among the most famous four in the
country.
Tourist Attractions
Guangzhou is a beautiful city with ever-green scenery and flowers blooming all the year round.
The city boasts of many tourist attractions, among which highlights are the Canton Tower, a new
landmark of Guangzhou, the White Cloud Hill Scenic Spot, Yuexiu Park, Guangzhou Zoo, Six Banyan
Temple and Flowery Pagoda, Dr. Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall, etc. In the Suburbs, there are such scenic
spot on Conghua Hot Springs, Xiqiao Hill Scenic spot, Seven Star Crags, and Foshan City. Lots of tourists
to Guangzhou like to cover one or two of them for out-of-city pleasure.
Shopping in Guangzhou:
Guangzhou offers a wide range of shopping experiences ‐‐ from department store and fashion boutiques
to the strange world of traditional medicines and exotic foods.
Facts about Guangzhou
Population
12 million approximately
Geography

Guangzhou is the capital of Guangdong Province; it is very close to Hong Kong and Macau.
Size
Guangzhou covers an area of 1,444 square kilometers.
Main Language
Mandarin (formal language), Cantonese (dialect)
Climate
Guangzhou is located in a humid subtropical climate zone, with plenty of sunshine and rainfall, and no
snow in the last 100 years. Summers are long, humid and scorching, and winters are short, mild and
sunny. The yearly average temperature in Guangzhou is 22 °C (72 °F). The lowest temperatures are in
January when the average low temperature is 10 °C (54 °F), which will be chilly cold, and the record
highest temperature was 39 °C (102 °F) in July.

to the MITB office, SMU, by the above-agreed deadlines.
