Introduction: 

印度管理學院(Indian Institutes of Management，IIMs) 是由印度13所公立及自治校務的分校所組成，自2007年成立以來，於印度各大城市陸續設立分校，招收從事政治經濟研究及管理顧問的研究生，印度政府更於2014/7宣布，將再成立5所新的分校，以滿足國內外學生對於高等管理教育之需求。        

早在2007年，印度國家發展研究所就決定要成立一個研究人力資源管理的專門機構，直至2010年7月蘭契分校正式營運，為印度管理學院第9名成員，也是印度管理學院成員當中，唯一提供人力資源管理專門課程的學校，該校獨特的Post Graduate Diploma in Human Resource Management (PGDHRM)，在國際人力資源管理領域頗負盛名，更獲得印度政府人力資源發展部的全力支持。

Introduction: 

國立浙江大學前身為創立於1897年的求是書院，為中國最早創立的新式高等學校之ㄧ，於1946年正式更名為國立浙江大學。在超過115年的辦學歷程中，該校始終以造就卓越人才為己任，並貫徹「求是創新」的校訓。近年來亦致力於國際化發展，自國外聘請30位知名學者擔任講座教授，其中包含2位諾貝爾獲獎者，並與全球15所知名大學簽定姐妹校合作協議，前來交換或就學的外籍生人數也以每年10%的速度成長，至2013年校園已有超過3,000名外籍生，而薦外學生人數亦同步攀升，年增率逼近四成。

根據2013年泰晤士高等教育世界大學排名中，浙江大學高居全中國第5位，名列亞洲第45位；而由中國管理科學研究院武書連主持的中國大學平價當中，浙江大學自2011年開始已經連續三年蟬連榜首之位。

Introduction: 

印度管理學院為印度7所國立商學院的總稱，各自坐落於印度主要的7個城市，從2007年成立以來，為專攻政治經濟研究與管理顧問服務的頂尖學府。其中，位於科澤科德的分校創始於1996年，儘管成立時間不長，但不論課程品質或學生人數都快速成長，對於印度管理人才開發與新興領域的研究，占有舉足輕重的地位，並於2012年取得國際商管學院促進協會 (AACSB，The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business)之認證。此外，在國際學術交流方面，IIMK也和歐洲及東協地區多所頂尖管理學院締結合作，包括法國巴黎高等商學院 (ESCP Business School)、義大利博科尼大學 (Università Commerciale Luigi Bocconi )、澳洲昆士蘭大學 ( University of Queensland)等。政大和IIMK締結合作後，每學期將互相薦送2名研究所學生進行交換學習。

廣州中山大學嶺南學院擁有超過120年的悠久歷史，其在國際化的發展亦是高瞻遠矚，早在1999年就和美國麻省理工學院（MIT）合作開辦國際MBA課程，其後更與美國明尼蘇達大學卡爾森管理學院合作推出的中美EMBA，以及法國里昂第三大學、里昂商學院合辦中法MBA。統計該校在2011學年，就已有超過100名學生到海外各大姊妹校交換學習，學院目前也積極和加拿大、英國、澳洲等8所大學合作開發雙聯學位。

Introduction: 

華中科技大學創立於1953年，為中國教育部直屬的重點大學，亦是首批列入中國「211工程」和「985工程」重點建設的大學之一，校園內綠化覆蓋率72%，有「森林式大學」的美譽。

華中科技大學堅持開放式辦學理念，積極開展全方位、多層次的國際交流與合作，目前已與全球26國超過百所的大學建立良好的校際交流關係，包括美國南加州大學、英國伯明罕大學、新加坡南洋理工大學、日本東京大學等世界名校皆為其姐妹校；此外，每年也都會有超過1500人次交換教授前往華中科技大學任教、舉辦研討會以及進行其他的學術交流活動。

香港城市大學的前身為香港城市理工學院（City Polytechnic of Hong Kong），簡稱城市理工，創立於1984年，學校致力培育和拓展學生才能，創造實用知識，推動社會和經濟進步，矢志成為硏究優異、專業教育出眾的全球一流學府。 根據英國《泰晤士報高等教育特刊》年度全球200所頂尖大學排名顯示，城大連續6年躋身200大，並於2009年躍居第124位。在國際高等教育資訊機構Quacquarelli Symonds (QS)公佈的2010年度亞洲大學排名中，城大名列第15位。而城市大學的商學院更同時獲得了3項國際頂級認證AACSB、EQUIS、AMBA，直到目前為止，全球僅有不到百分之一的商學院獲得此3重認證的殊榮。

Introduction: 

朱拉隆功大學（Chulalongkorn University）是泰國最古老也是最頂尖的大學，被尊為「全國最有威望的大學」。學校名字取自朱拉隆功國王拉瑪五世，創始人是瓦吉拉伍德國王（H.M.Vajiravudh）拉瑪六世，拉瑪六世將該校發展成一所國家直屬的行政學院，並且增加了很多課程，早在1917年這所行政學院便具有現代綜合性大學的規模。該校悠遠的傳統也發展出特殊的「道德網絡」，該組織的主要工作為防止學生做出有為校譽的事情。為了因應全球市場對工程領域人才的缺乏，朱拉隆功大學在2005年更成立國際工程學院(ISE)，藉由全英文授課培育出能立足國際市場的高等工程人才。

Introduction: 

佛羅里達大學（UF）全美前五大的學校之—，為佛羅里達州最具規模的公立大學，座落在佛羅里達州北方Gainesville，城市裡的居民多半是UF 的學生，也可以說是一個大學城，曾被評選為全美最宜人居住的城市之一。該校為一所綜合、研究型大學，提供各種多元化的學術知識領域的學位，此外也擁有美國南部學府最大的電腦中心，廣闊的校園內擁有眾多設施。值得一提的是佛羅里達大學的農業研究相當知名，對於佛羅里達州的農業發展頗多助益。當然該校在商學領域的成就也不遜色，在最新出爐的《金融時報》2009年全球MBA排名當中位居63名（"Global MBA rankings in 2009" Financial Times shttp://rankings.ft.com/businessschoolrankings/global-mba-rankings）。

普渡大學（Purdue University）創立於1869年，為一所歷史悠久的研究性公立大學，向來以優良的教學質量和適中的收費標準聞名世界，且有「旅遊觀光界的哈佛」和「美國航太之母」的美譽。普渡大學雖以理工見長，但其管理專業在全世界享有很高的聲譽。此外該校也特別重視「教育國際化」，是美國國際學生最多的大學之一，在國際教育研究院（Institute of International Education）中爲國際學生最多的公立大學，在全美大學中排第四位。 在英國《金融時報》2008年的排名為第11名（http://rankings.ft.com/emba-rankings），其MBA學生更曾被華爾街日報評選「最受企業歡迎的人才」排名第四，美國普渡大學無論在學術和師資方面都有很好的評價。

Introduction: 

法國格勒諾貝爾管理學院成立於1984年，是由格勒諾貝爾工商協會所建立，創立之初便以成為法國工商管理高等教育標竿為旨，不論是在技術管理或跨文化管理領域都擁有獨特的精髓，並強調讓每位學生都懷著服務於全球企業的精神。格勒諾貝爾管理學院也是全球商管學院當中，少數同時通過國際商學院促進協會（AACSB）、國際工商管理碩士協會(AMBA)，以及歐洲品質發展認證體系（EQUIS）三重認證的頂尖學府；學校也在2010年英國《金融時報》全球商學管理碩士（Financial Times Masters in Management）排名中榮獲全球第5名的佳績。

Introduction: 

法國南特管理學院（Audencia Business School ）創辦於1990年，積極進取的辦學態度，讓該校在短短二十年之內就成為歐洲公認的管理學教學與研究中心，更成為全球少數獲得歐洲管理發展基金會（EQUIS）、高等商學院協會（AACSB）、MBA協會（AMBA）等三項頂尖國際認證的商學院之一；此外，南特管理學院在國際化之進程上也不斷創新努力，截至目前為止已經和全球百餘所頂尖的國際學術夥伴合作，在現有的3000名學生當中，就涵蓋來自全球50多個國家的同學，超過20％的外籍學生在此共同學習。該校在各方面優異的表現，也獲得英國金融時報（ Financial Times）2009年歐洲管理碩士學位排名（Masters in Management 2009）第13名的榮譽。

法國里昂高等管理學院（E.M. LYON），1872年成立於法國第二大都市-里昂。根據英國權威雜誌E的最新排名, E.M. LYON名列世界36，歐洲第10以及法國第3，也在《金融時報》2008年歐洲商業學校高居第8名 European Business school rankings 2008" Financial Times http://rankings.ft.com/businessschoolrankings/european-business-school-rankings）。E.M. LYON 擁有著高深資歷的師資陣容，培養出分布全球的卓越企業家和高層管理人才。為了順應全球化的浪潮，E.M. LYON和來自全球主要商業地區的五所學校：War¬wick Business School（英國）- HEC-Montreal（加拿大）Bel¬grano University（阿根廷）-- THUNDERBIRD（美國）成立了一個獨一無二的跨國商校聯盟—AEA聯盟，學生可獲得聯盟學校的雙文憑。

Introduction: 

法國諾歐商學院(NEOMA Business School)是由法國兩所歷史久遠且發展卓越的高等商學院合併而成，分別是成立於1982年的漢斯高等商業管理學院(Reims Management School)以及成立於1981年的盧昂商業學校(Rouen Business School)，該兩校先後獲得EQUIS、AMBA 及AACSB三項世界頂級商學院認證，為了整合兩校資源及姊妹校關係，攜手問鼎歐洲商學院之首的寶座，雙方決定深化長期合作關係，於2013年9月宣布合併為諾歐商學院(NEOMA)，「NEO」意為「新」，「MA」代表「Management」新校總部位於法國北部最大城市盧昂(Rouen)，共有三個校區，共有超過4萬名畢業生遍布全球。根據英國金融時報2013年歐洲商學院排名，這所新成立的學校目前位居第65名，由於排名評比對於新合併的學校並不有利，該校也將以全新的面貌，努力在2014年的金融時報四項排名中取得領先名次。

Introduction: 

里爾天主教大學是法國久負盛名的私立大學之一，其IESEG學院不但通過AACSB（國際商管學院促進協會）認證，也是歐洲管理學教學基金會的成員之一。該校相當重視國際化發展，合作姐妹院校共計139所，遍佈38個國家，該校有80％的學生都曾參與交流計畫到各國學習，而IESEG學院也有18.75%來自各地的國際學生，為了更積極和國際接軌，IESEG也是法國第一個開辦全英語碩士課程的學校，75％非法國背景的國際師資，也提供國際學生更多選擇。

斯德哥爾摩經濟學院成立於1909年，除了瑞典首都斯德哥爾摩市，並在拉脫維亞首都和俄羅斯聖彼得堡皆設有姊妹校區。該校不但是北歐最頂尖的商學院之一，作為諾貝爾經濟學獎的評選機構，更奉行菁英教育每年僅招收300名學生，優異的學術表現也成為兩大國際頂尖商學體系-國際商學管理聯盟「Partnership in International Management」(PIM)和「全球管理教育聯盟The Global Alliance in Management Education」(CEMS)的成員之一。該校在全球擁有70個合作的姊妹校，每學年都會薦送200名本校學生出國，並迎接180名來自各國的交換生。爾後，政大商學院每年也將提供大學部2名的交換名額。

Introduction:

ESSEC高等商業學院成立於1907年，為法國著名高等商業學院之一，擁有悠久的歷史傳統之餘，亦致力國際化的發展，全校有超過三分之一的國際師資，更有超過五分之一的國際學生來自於全球70餘國；在國際交流方面，ESSEC亦與多所國際知名大學建立合作關係，包含美國康乃爾大學、加州大學柏克萊分校、香港科技大學、韓國首爾大學等。

挪威經濟與商業管理學院在經濟和工商管理領域內高品質的教育和研究水準是每一個想從事於經濟管理的學生的理想選擇。截至目前為止，成立於1936年的挪威商 業學院已經培養出了一大批在商業界和公共生活中擔任要職的優秀畢業生。2005年挪威商業學院被《金融時代》評為歐洲最好的20個碩士管理課程之一，而經濟學位居第一，金融學位居第四。建校時間：1936年學校性質：公立 挪威管理學院和挪威經濟管理學院優秀的商科，也是莘莘學子們不錯的選擇。2004年諾貝爾經濟學獎的獲得者就是從挪威經濟管理學院畢業的。

Introduction: 

有義大利哈佛之稱的博科尼大學(Universita Commerciale Luigi Bocconi)於1902年創立，是義大利很有聲望、頂尖的私立大學，它是第一所在義大利教授經濟學高等教育的學院，亦是世界最重要的商學院之一，特別是在法律及管理學專業中是歐洲各名校中的佼佼者。目前公認為義大利最頂尖的經濟與商業領域大學，在最新出爐的2008年《金融時報》商管教育排名，高居全球第18名（Executive Education rankings 2008 http://rankings.ft.com/executive-education---open）。而全球排名不斷上升的SDA學院，也在金融時報FULL TIME MBA排名全球第四十八位（Global MBA 2008 http://www.ft.com/businesseducation/globalmba2008）。BOCCONI相當重視國際推廣，已在世界各地締結了超過200所姐妹校。近年來由於亞洲新興市場的崛起，博科尼大學日漸重視亞洲名校的關係經營，在亞洲地區已簽訂二十六所姐妹校，更和中國多所大學有交換學程，也有雙學位的學程，在亞洲地區非常的活躍。

法國諾歐商學院(NEOMA Business School)是由法國兩所歷史久遠且發展卓越的高等商學院合併而成，分別是成立於1982年的漢斯高等商業管理學院(Reims Management School)以及成立於1981年的盧昂商業學校(Rouen Business School)，該兩校先後獲得EQUIS、AMBA 及AACSB三項世界頂級商學院認證，為了整合兩校資源及姊妹校關係，攜手問鼎歐洲商學院之首的寶座，雙方決定深化長期合作關係，於2013年9月宣布合併為諾歐商學院(NEOMA)，「NEO」意為「新」，「MA」代表「Management」新校總部位於法國北部最大城市盧昂(Rouen)，共有三個校區，共有超過4萬名畢業生遍布全球。根據英國金融時報2013年歐洲商學院排名，這所新成立的學校目前位居第65名，由於排名評比對於新合併的學校並不有利，該校也將以全新的面貌，努力在2014年的金融時報四項排名中取得領先名次。

Introduction: 

法語魯汶大學源於現在的荷語魯汶大學。由於語系、文化背景的差異，在1970經政府立法年一分為二，將荷語魯汶大學留在魯汶(Leuven) ，並建立一個全新的校園給講法語的學生。法語魯汶大學的建校，促成了新魯汶（Louvain-la-Neuve）的誕生。該校繼承了比利時的傳統及原魯汶大學將近六百年悠久的歷史，同時也展現出活潑的現代化氣息。該校目前擁有十個學院、五十個科系以及 200 個研究單位。大致可分為三大類：人文科學、應用科學，另外還有戲劇學習中心以及語言中心，是一所相當完整的綜合性大學。

埃克塞特大學的歷史可遠溯自19世紀中期，前身為一所文學院，幾經沿革後於1955年定名為埃克塞特大學。該校位於英格蘭的西南方的城市埃克塞特（Exeter），是英國著名的傳統高等學府。該校的教學品質曾獲英國高等教育素質認證機構（Quality Assurance Agency for Higher Education）評譽有傑出表現，其它還獲得了The Times優良評價；而該校的研究水準則經由英國國家研究評鑑（Research Assessment Exercise， RAE）認證為具有國家暨國際級研究標準。 根據埃克塞特大學校方統計，目前約有將近一萬八千名學生就讀於此，其中包括了約1500名國際學生，分別來自海外100多個國家，且該校也與國際間的許多大學有頻繁密集的學術交流合作。值得一提的是，知名小說哈利波特的作者J•K•羅琳，也是出自於艾克斯特大學的校友。

設立於1963年的約克大學，在英國的學界來說是一所非常年輕的學校，但是該校所展現出的創意與爆發力卻讓牛津、劍橋等名校都望其項背，短時間內即發展成為全英國最成功、最受歡迎的大學之一，其研究成果的排名始終穩居全英國全10名，在2011年英國金融時報英國大學排名中位居第9名 ，其教學品質更被評估為全英國最佳之一。 約克大學本身無論是歷史還是名氣，事實上都與當地著名的大教學不相上下。儘管學生人數不少，仍有70%的學生居住在學校提供的宿舍，可見學校設施之完善。保持其高教學品質的傳統之餘，學校亦對越來越多的科目進行了改革，使之更加靈活而實用。

Introduction: 

葛洛寧恩大學創校於1614年，為歐洲最古老的研究型大學之一，長期深耕的學術成果享譽國際。該校坐落於荷蘭北方的葛洛寧恩市，為學生心目中理想 安全的城市，因此評選為荷蘭最友善的城市。在悠久的傳統之上，葛洛寧恩大學近來掌握全球化的潮流，積極向國際接軌，不論是學士、碩士、博士課程大都採用英語授課。 葛洛寧恩大學也是是歐洲COIMBRA集團的成員，COIMBRA集團是歐洲歷史最悠久的38所大學的合作組織，其成員包括英國劍橋大學與牛津大學。此外，該校也和遍佈世界的姊妹校締結合作，包括瑞典Uppsala University、比利時Ghent University，以及中國的北京大學、清華大學、復旦大學等建立長期的交流關係。 葛洛寧恩大學為政大商學院第90所姊妹院校，每年提供本校大學及研究生共4個交換名額，大學部申請標準為達到托福（TOEFL）新制79、舊制550，研究生則需要TOEFL新制92、舊制580。

Introduction: 

比利時荷語魯汶大學布魯塞爾校成立於1425年，其前身為天主教魯汶大學，不但是歐洲最古老且最知名的大學之一，更是現存最古老的天主教大學，在近600年的時間當中，一直在歐洲大學教育領域中扮演舉足輕重的角色，學校位於西歐歷史名城魯汶，為傳統的大學城，並擁有世界歷史文化遺產。

除了豐沛的歷史傳統，比利時荷語魯汶大學亦致力於區域化及全球化之發展，該校已是歐洲研究型大學聯盟（LERU）及歐洲古大學科英布拉集團及歐洲研究型大學聯盟（LERU）的創始成員之一，更是荷蘭語天主教魯汶大學聯盟（K.U.Leuven Association）的首席大學，與其他13所高校形成比利時荷蘭語區最大的教育聯合體，多年深耕國際化的結果，也讓該校獲得歐洲質量發展系統（European Quality Improvement System，EQUIS）之認證，並在2014年泰晤士高等教育世界大學排名中，榮獲世界第55位，歐洲第13位，比利時國內第1位之殊榮。

比利時荷語魯汶大學布魯塞爾校近年積極和亞洲建立連結，除了在中國和北京大學、清華大學及復旦大學等名校簽訂合作協議外，更成立中歐文化研究中心，如今，該校看中政大商學院在商學領域之卓越發展，雙方亦於2015年開啟合作，預計每學期將提供大學部及碩士各2名同學，互相交換學習一學期。

新里斯本大學商學院致力於成為國際頂尖的商學院之一，目前已加入管理碩士國際聯盟(CEMS)，和全球近30所頂尖商學院及50餘家企業締結合作，更於2009年在非洲成立分校Nova Angola Business School，並在巴西及東歐等地，積極推動針對有經驗商務人士的教育學程(Executive Education programs)管理碩士學程，獲得空前的成功，作為葡萄牙最頂尖學校當之無愧。

Introduction: 

德國漢堡大學(University of Hamburg)成立於1919年，實際上該校設立的起源可追朔至17世紀，初始設立的專業學科僅有法學及社會學、哲學、醫學及自然科學，經歷近一個世紀的發展，如今已有超過15個專業學科，並培育出4位諾貝爾物理學獎得主，學校更於2014年新設商學院，目前在校學生約4萬人，外籍生佔比近十分之一。 隨著全球化的潮流，近年來也積極進行國際化的發展，目前已和全球約265所菁英學校共569個學程締結交流合作外，合作對象包含美國UC Berkeley、上海復旦大學及丹麥根本哈根商學院等，對內則增設29個英語授課的碩士學程，當中有9個是和商管經濟等社會學科相關的學程，提供非德語系的學生，更暢通的學習管道。

Introduction: 

盧布爾雅那大學成立於1917年，坐落在斯洛維尼亞首都盧布爾雅那(Ljubljana)，為該國歷史最悠久、規模最大的大學，目前共有超過5萬名的學生在此學習，並有130項科系及專業可供選擇。隨著國家經濟發展突飛猛進，UL逐漸發展成一所國際化的綜合性大學，近十年來，UL積極參與國際性的學術研究計畫和教育專案，單是2013年UL就加入了421項的歐盟研究計畫，在斯洛維尼亞政府的建教合作專案中一樣沒有缺席。此外，UL也活躍於歐洲、澳洲、中美洲等區域教育聯盟，讓學生可透過這些聯盟和全球超過500個大專院校交流互動，並和歐美共100所名校建立合作，提供學生到各國交換學習的機會，同時也從世界各地迎來許多交換生，在豐富的交流經驗下，UL從課堂學習到住宿，皆為遠道而來的外籍同學設想周到，提供完善的生活措施，讓學生們可以無後顧之憂的在此地享受學術洗禮。

Introduction: 

羅浮堡大學的前身為1909年成立的小型技術學院，該學院在1963年由英國皇家認可，正式定名為羅浮堡大學，也是英國當時的第一所科技型大學。學校鄰近東米德蘭斯機場（East Midlands Airport），距倫敦火車車程約2小時，校園幅員遼闊為全英最大的學校之一。經過逾百年的努力，該校曾破紀錄獲得4項極具學術聲望的英國女皇年度獎（Queen’s Anniversary Prize），在歷年的泰晤士報英國大學排名中榜上有名 (2014泰晤士報英國大學排名中名列英國第21名)。尤其是商學院近年致力全球化布局，全校約有1/3外籍教授及學生，並先後獲得EQUIS、AACSB及AMBA三大國際認證，正式晉升全球1%商學名校之列。

政治大學商學院為羅浮堡大學在台灣簽訂的第一個姊妹校，每學年將會薦送4位同學來台交換，並提供4位大學部的交換機會給政大同學。

Introduction: 

Solvay商學院成立於1903年，並在2008年和布魯塞爾自由大學經濟學院合併，成為現今眾人熟知的SBS-EM，該校目前共擁有超過3,700名學生以及30個專業學程。在國際化發展方面，SBS-EM和全球40國超過100所頂尖的商學管理院校，建立了長久的合作關係，該校每年薦送約300名學生出國交換，並且有來自各地約200名國際交換生前來學習。值得一提的是，學校雖然位於比利時法語區，但學校提供了充足的英文授課課程，及基礎法語學習機會，讓外籍同學不論在校內外，只要具備英文能力就能夠暢行無阻。

Introduction: 

KEDGE高等商業學院是由法國兩所知名的商學院，波爾多高等商學院(BEM)和馬賽商學院(Euromed Management)合併而成，該校將於2013年9月正式對外招收第一批學生，並規畫至同年底在歐洲成立一個新的校區，到了2014年更將在歐洲以外成立一個國際校區，目標在5年內擠身歐洲前15大精英商管學院之列。

KEDGE高等商業學院不但承襲原有馬賽商學院獲得的AACSB、EQUIS以及AMBA三大頂尖商管認證，綜合既有兩校資源，目前已有近一萬名的學生分部在全球4個校區，而超過3萬5,000名的畢業生形成強勁的人脈網絡，加上300所遍布全球的姐妹院校，都為這所新竄起的法國高等商學教育機構，帶來堅強的後盾。

值得一提的是，「KEDGE」在英語中是指繫在繩上用於移動船隻的 「小錨」，也意味著一個全新的方向和指標，未來「KEDGE高等商業學院」也將成為全新的品牌，針對新興市場特別是亞洲執行發展策略，同時開發創新的教學課程，為全球高等商學教育樹立新的口碑和形象。

Introduction: 

阿姆斯特丹大學由阿姆斯特丹市議會於1632年成立學校的，是一所擁有豐富歷史的現代化大學，已成為一所世界級的研究與教學大學。其中的經濟計量學院成立於1922年，提供高水準的商業課程與卓越的學術研究，在荷蘭本地與世界各地皆擁有非常優異的學術知名度。阿姆斯特丹市可說是國際商業的源頭，舉凡全球第一個公開股票交易所，到全球第一個跨國公司皆設立於此，因此該校課程也反映了此城市的國際化、企業精神、學術風氣與社會責任等傳統。此外阿姆斯特丹大學也藉由與其他頂尖學術機構(如SEO經濟研究中心與Tinbergen經濟學院) 的密切合作，來促進並豐富研究成果與獨立專案的推行。

Introduction: 

馬茲垂克大學成立於1975年，是荷蘭最年輕的大學之一，獨創一格的教學方法、高品質的研究工作、極其廣闊的眼界在荷蘭大學中嶄露頭角，在國內外教學和研究評估中更擁有突出成績。超過一半以上的碩士學生都不是荷蘭本國學生，平均七名同學之中就有一人持有外國護照，組成相當多元；國際化的特點還反映在課程規劃上，多數碩士課程皆用英文授課。大學之下設有七個學院，四十四種專業領域可供選擇。此外該校也積極和世界各知名大學締結交流，每年提供上百個出國交換的機會，讓學生們周遊世界各地獲得大量的實踐經驗。

Introduction: 

聖加倫大學（University of St. Gallen）建立於1898年，以法律、經濟、管理與國際關係等學科為主的大學，雖然在亞洲沒沒無聞，但實際上在歐洲頗負盛名，以德語系國家尤然，甚至還有「德語區的哈佛」這個美名。聖加倫大學雖然是歐洲規模較小的大學，但卻擁有瑞士最大的經濟科學的師資力量。該校不但同時獲得EQUIS以及AACSB雙重高標準認證，另外也是兩大高等教育聯盟CEMS（(M.Sc. in International Management）和APSIA（Association of Professional Schools of Inter-national Affairs）的成員。

Introduction: 

西班牙企業學院（IE Business School）位於西班牙首都馬德里，成立至今雖然才三十餘年，卻已經獲得全球三大頂尖商學機構AMBA、AACSB和EQUIS的認可，值得一提的是，截至2011年11月為止，全球獲得三個頂尖機構會員資格的商學院，僅有55所商學院。不同於多數MBA課程著重在金融或管顧產業的訓練，西班牙企業學院旨在培養學生成為獨當一面的創業家。在2011年英國金融時報排行中，西班牙企業學院榮獲全歐洲商學院第四名、Global MBA全球排名第八的殊榮，同年也被富比士雜誌評選為全球第三的MBA學程。

Study program: Exchange students can join INCAE’s MBA in Spanish for with
simultaneous translation from August to October and courses
taught in English from October to December, 2025 with the
Global MBA. In 2026, students can take courses in English
with the Global MBA at any time from January to October. If
students speak Spanish and are comfortable taking courses
in Spanish, they are welcome to join courses in any of the
other programs (MBA in Spanish – Master of Analytics and
Information Technology) in 2025.

June and July

August to October (Module 8)

Language of instruction: Global MBA courses are all in English. Exchange students are
welcome to take courses in Spanish in other programs if they
are fluent enough.
Language courses: English (on campus) and Spanish (on campus). Not all levels
are offered at the same time. Tutors are available for a fee.
Language requirement: TOEFL score: 90 (iBT) or equivalent proficiency determined
by partner school. Students must be able to actively
participate in class discussions regardless of the language of
instruction of the course.
Methodology: 70% case study analysis and discussion, and 30% lecture.
The specific method depends on the nature of the course.
However, all courses are very demanding and students have
to be prepared for every single session. Class participation
can be 50% of the final grade in some cases. Students are
expected to read and prepare all the material assigned
individually and to check their e-mail regularly for last-minute
instructions from professors, even during weekends and/or
holidays.
Exams: Exams are scheduled during the last week of every module;
courses offered at the beginning of a module might have the
final evaluation earlier. However, you are advised to plan to
stay until the last day of the module. Professors have two
weeks to submit grades to the Registrar. Also, because
professors must use the grading curve, individual grades are
not available until all students have been assigned a grade.
Please book your return flight based on scheduled exam
dates.

Grading system: INCAE uses a highly competitive curve-grading system. The
curve is applied in all courses, but in second year, it is up to
the professor to assign failing grades. Letter grades are used
as follows:
A+ Outstanding (4.0)
A Excellent (3.75)
A- Very Good (3.45)
B+ Very Good (2.98)
B Good (2.80)
B- Satisfactory (2.65)
C Unsatisfactory (failing 2.0)
F Poor (0.0) equivalent to two failing grades (Note: the student will
receive notification of his/her grades; digital transcripts will be sent
to the home school without cost. Printed transcripts must be ordered
and paid for by the student).
Housing: Because living on campus is mandatory for all students,
availability is guaranteed. Single students must share a
house with 7 students and a room with one of them. There is
also married housing available for couples with or without
children. However, availability might be limited.
Facilities: We have a cafeteria, a convenience store, a bank office (No
ATM!) a swimming pool, gym, sauna, outdoor sporting areas,
library, wireless internet access, group study rooms, parking,
and laundry service for a fee (about $15 per load). Self-service
is now available! Students must purchase their own detergent
and other supplies (laundry basket, softener, etc.)
Services: The Student Affairs Department aids students with everyday
life, plus: visas, insurance, medical services, student clubs,
and so on. Student Affairs, in coordination with International
Programs, will pair exchange students with a “buddy” who will
guide them through their adaptation to life at INCAE.
Health insurance: All students are required to have health insurance from
their home country. It should cover any incidents while
traveling to and from INCAE as well as repatriation. We
strongly recommend that students also have liability insurance
as well as personal insurance covering theft, etc.
Career Services: The MBA Career Services office at INCAE will assist dual
degree students in their job search efforts while they are at
INCAE (only jobs in Latin America). All students will have
access to company presentations, job listings, interviews, and
career fairs, but priority will be given to INCAE and dual
degree students. Each student is responsible for writing and
translating their resumes and cover letters.

Visa requirements: Depending on their nationality, students may or may not need
a visa to enter the country. Students should check this link or
contact the nearest Costa Rica Consulate to make sure. Most
exchange students do not stay for more than 90 days at a time
(holidays, breaks), and get away with not having a student
visa, whose cost is currently around US$800. However, some
students have encountered trouble when trying to reenter
when they leave before the 90 days expire because they didn’t
have a return ticket every time. So, they ended up spending
more in an “emergency ticket” they couldn’t even use.
Travel requirements: https://www.visitcostarica.com/en/costa-rica/planning-
your-trip/entry-requirements
IMPORTANT!: INCAE requires full health insurance
coverage for the whole study period.
Yellow fever vaccine: If you're coming from Angola, Benin, Burkina Faso,
Cameroon, Congo, Gabon, Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Liberia,
Nigeria, Sierra Leone, Sudan, Bolivia, Venezuela, Brazil,
Peru, Ecuador, Colombia and French Guyana, you'll need to
get the yellow fever vaccine at least 10 days before entering
Costa Rica. It’s a one-time deal, so if you already have it, you
don’t need to get it again. Local Immigration authorities might
ask for it upon arrival.
Estimated Expenses*: Expenses for exchange students at INCAE include:
- Student fee US$390 per module (NOT tuition -
includes materials, housekeeping, medical attention on campus,
and other services)
- Housing (shared room) $25 per night if you bring your own
linens (approx. $750 per month)
- Meals $3 to $10 at the cafeteria
- Electricity $30 per month (approx.)
- Water $20 per month (approx.)
- Laundry Self-service (must provide your
own detergent) or pay $15 per load approx. for the service
(includes washing, drying and folding).
- Linens $100 per semester (includes
laundry service). We strongly recommend bringing your own.
- Transportation $200 per month (approx.)
- Recreation $300 per month (approx.)
- Miscellaneous $100 approx.
- Quarantine and PCR $275
Total per module: $4,000 approx.
*All costs subject to change without notice, especially outsourced services like meals and laundry.

Payment: Credit Card: If you plan to pay with a credit card, we’ll provide
a link to the shopping cart where you’ll find the different items
you must pay for.
Wire transfer: If you plan to pay via wire transfer, we’ll send
you the account information. All bank charges (sending,
receiving and correspondent fees) must be borne by the
student.
PLEASE, let me know how you’re planning to pay as the payment must be made
BEFORE you arrive. Thanks!

Frequently Asked Questions
Do I need a student visa?
You can check this link or contact your nearest Costa Rica Consulate to find out:
If you are and exchange or dual degree student staying for more than 90 days at a time
(most students don’t), a student visa is required. The process starts at the Costa Rica
consulate and continues once the student arrives in Costa Rica. The immigration office takes
about three months to issue the visa. The cost is approximately US$400. Students need 2
additional passport-size photographs.
How do I go about applying for housing?
You do not need to apply. If you’re single, you’ll be assigned a room in a house for single
students. If you’re married and your family is coming with you, let us know in advance, so
we can reserve a house for married couples with or without children. There’s no
housekeeping service for married student housing.
Will there be a telephone in my residence?
Yes. However, you cannot make off-campus calls. You can receive local and international
calls, but in order to make them, you must use your cell phone.

Can I use my cell phone to make calls in Costa Rica?
Yes, but if you’d like to use your home number, you’ll need International Roaming or an e-
SIM card. You can also get a local number (SIM card) at the airport (baggage claim area).
You can buy more minutes anywhere the service is available (convenience stores, for
example). Most people use Facetime or WhatsApp to make calls, where they have access
to free Wi-Fi all over campus.
When should I arrive for orientation?
Because INCAE is a small school, we don’t need a lot of time for orientation. Usually,
orientation takes place during the first week of class. Therefore, we ask students to arrive
the weekend before the term starts, so they are able to check in immediately. If you arrive
too early, chances are you will have to find a place to stay.
Will there be someone to meet me when I arrive?
If you are coming straight to campus from the airport, we can arrange airport pick-up with
one of our drivers for a fee. In case there’s a problem or if you miss our driver, please take
an orange cab at the airport. It’s safe and reliable and they know where INCAE is. They
charge around $20-30.
Do I have to bring towels and bed linens?
We’d rather you bring your own. However, if you don’t want to carry them, bed linens and
towels will be provided for a fee. Housing would change and wash them once a week.
Remember that you have to take care of and pay for the laundry service separately if you
bring your own. Single students have twin-size beds and married housing has a full-size
bed.
ABOUT COSTA RICA
Costa Rica is a small nation of about 5.18 million people, but it holds 5 percent of the world’s
total biodiversity, 3.5 percent of all marine life, and 30 percent of its territory is protected
natural land. In the last decades, renewable sources such as wind, geothermal, solar and
hydroelectric have been responsible for the production of nearly 93 percent of its energy.
Since the arrival of technology companies, such as Intel in the late 1990s and the rise of
free trade zones, Costa Rica has become an attractive place for big companies. These
factors resulted in a shift in employment, going from manufacturing to skilled professionals.
During your visit, you will have the opportunity to learn where Costa Rica’s reputation on
sustainable development comes from and why the nation has been considered one of the
happiest countries in the world in recent years.

ABOUT INCAE BUSINESS SCHOOL
INCAE Business School is a private, non-profit, multinational, higher-education
organization devoted to teaching and research endeavors in the fields of business and
economics aimed at training and instructing individuals capable of successfully holding top
management positions in Latin America.
In 1964, the business community and the governments of the Central American nations
founded INCAE Business School. Since its inception it has had the technical supervision
of the Harvard Business School.
INCAE Business School is now focused on three key activities:
* Masters programs in specific areas for Latin Americans development.
* Executive training programs and seminars.
* Research projects on competitiveness in the region.
INCAE's Research Centers engage in the analysis of issues highly meaningful to the
business community and the creation of proposals for the sustainable development of
Latin American countries. INCAE makes research findings available to different
governments, business sectors, and societies in an attempt to exert a positive influence on
them and to provide positive change drivers.
• Centro Latinoamericano para la Competitividad y Desarrollo Sostenible (CLACDS):
it is the main Think Tank and applied research center at INCAE. Its mission is to
promote sustainable development in the region through research and dialogue.
• Center for Collaborative and Women's Leadership: it is an extension of INCAE's
institutional belief that greater gender diversity in leadership has a positive impact
on the region’s progress. It has developed a successful three-pronged approach to
address this regional problem: research, leadership development and community
impact.
• Latin American Center for Entrepreneurs: it is the impact center responsible for
promoting entrepreneurship in the region, it provides the skills to educate and
develop an entrepreneurial mindset.
INCAE has two campuses: Walter Kissling Gam located in the province of Alajuela, Costa
Rica and Francisco de Sola Campus located in Montefresco, Nicaragua.

Safety
When traveling around the country, always keep an eye on your belongings, do not leave
your luggage unattended or with strangers.
Smoking
In general, it is prohibited to smoke in public places in Costa Rica. At INCAE, smoking is not
allowed in the rooms and facilities. We have a specific area for smokers outside the housing
units, you can use the green areas beyond the main parking lot. It is forbidden to smoke in
and around the main buildings, the soccer field and Hardbar.
Tipping
Restaurants: it is required by law to add a 13% tax and 10% tip to the bill, so you are not
expected to leave a separate tip.

Exchange students joining Aston for one or two terms, either in Term 1 (September to January)
or Term 2 (January to March) will be enrolled on the ABS Master Exchange Programme.
The number of modules that can be selected must be agreed in advance with the home
institution but students must register for at least two modules. The number of ECTS credit load
for each module can vary but students will be able to study up to four modules which will
represent a MAXIMUM of 60 Aston credits (30 ECTS credits) per academic term. This will
determine the total number of courses that can be selected. In some circumstances we may
exceptionally allow students to study up to five modules if required by the home institution.
Please note: some electives will assume knowledge of topics covered in other modules. If these
pre-requisites have not already been studied, students will not be able to register for that
module. Information on pre-requisites can be found in the Module Outlines. If any of the
modules selected have pre-requisites, students will need to note this on the “Module Choice /
Evidence of Prior Learning” form and attach evidence of prior learning. This form must be
signed and stamped by the home institution.
REGISTERING FOR MODULES
A Module Choice Form listing available modules and their scheduled running will be made
available before the start of each academic year. The provisional teaching schedule will be
made available in Autumn and the definitive teaching schedule as soon as possible. We will
endeavor to publish provisional module choices for Term 1 (September to December) as soon
as they become available.
Students will need to complete the form indicating their selection, and if appropriate providing
evidence of prior learning. The form will need to be signed and stamped by the home institution
and sent back to abs_exchange@aston.ac.uk before the start of term.
Please note that your selection of modules and these being granted will depend on no
clashes between each module on your timetable. You will be given a chance to select
alternative modules in this case.

ECTS Credits describe the student workload required to complete course units. They reflect
the quantity of work each course unit requires in relation to the total quantity of work
necessary to complete a full academic year, and therefore they are a relative rather than
an absolute measure. Please refer to the module outlines for details of the ECTS credit
values allocated for each module and the dissertation for a specific Masters course.
Please note that although partners should use the ECTS credit rating to work out the
workload of their students at Aston, they should NOT use ECTS grades. The Aston
local results are far more representative of students’ performance at Aston.
CONTACT HOURS & ASSESSMENT
Our Postgraduate Programmes are taught in Block Periods with most modules consisting of 5
weeks of study, varying from 3-6 hours per week. All modules are assessed at the end of the
teaching block either by a 2-hour or 3-hour examination and/or by the submission of
coursework.
All coursework is submitted online.
When making your module selections please be aware that some may contain written
assessments (coursework) which are due to be submitted after the official end of term. You
can view the submission deadlines on each module outline.
DISSERTATION (DOUBLE DEGREE STUDENTS ONLY)
All MSc Programmes include a dissertation which forms a substantial element of the course both
in terms of workload and assessment weighting. The dissertation (guideline 10-20,000 words
depending on MSc programme) is undertaken from the end of the second term and is submitted
in mid-September. However, work will begin during the first and second terms, when a topic for
the dissertation is identified, an academic supervisor is allocated, a work plan and dissertation
summary/proposal are produced and an ethical approval for the proposed research is obtained
in conjunction with the dissertation supervisor.

Students on the double-degree may be

with a mark of 45% or above

General Advice
Birmingham has a wide range of accommodation for students in the city centre. There is also
plenty of affordable accommodation outside the city that is well connected by bus, tram, and rail
links.
You can find out more information about some of the public transport services available in
Birmingham and a journey planner here.
ASH recommends that students search for accommodation in advance of arriving, but does not
recommend signing any contracts until you have viewed the property for yourself.
Because of this, it is advised that you arrive in the UK early to view properties and make these
arrangements in person. Please note, it is against the Law in the UK for an accommodation
agency to take fees in advance from prospective tenants in return for details of properties.
For tips on how to avoid rental scams please check out Action Fraud: Rental Scams.
It is your responsibility to secure accommodation and find out what options are available
to you.
Accommodation Types Explained;
• Private student halls—similar to university accommodation but run by commercial companies.
• Shared houses – sharing a house with other students in Birmingham.
• Private apartment or house—living on your own in Birmingham and the surrounding areas.

12
General Advice for Private Accommodation
Council Tax;
Please note that if you secure private accommodation, you may be required to
pay Council Tax.
Council Tax is a charge set by local authorities to pay for the local services that they
provide, for example rubbish collection, the Police and Fire Service. Council Tax is
based on the value of the property and the amount payable for the property can be
affected by who lives in it.
Generally, full-time students within Birmingham do not have to pay Council Tax if
they are studying a course that is for longer than 24 weeks per year.
If you are studying a course that is for less than 24 weeks, you are technically
liable to pay Council Tax, but local authorities I.E. Birmingham City Council will
consider exemption requests on a case-by-case basis.
You can find more information about council tax here.
If you are thinking of making a request for Council Tax exemption, please consult the
International Advice Team at astoninternational@aston.ac.uk for advice.
If you are deemed not to be exempt, then you must pay the Council Tax due.
If you have issues with accommodation or housing rights, whether you are living
on-campus or off-campus, you can contact the SU’s independent student advice service
(known as the Advice and Representation Centre (ARC)) via email advice@aston.ac.uk.

13
You will need a passport that is valid for the entire duration of your studies at Aston, including the
exam periods. If you do not already have a passport, or if you need to renew it before travelling,
please apply for it as soon as you receive your offer letter from us to ensure it has arrived before
you are due to travel.
Full Academic Year Exchange
Most students will require a student visa to study in the UK for a full academic year, including
EU and EEA nationals. Information about Student visas can be found on our website here.
One Semester Exchange
Most exchange students joining Aston for one semester (up to 6 months) will need visitor
immigration permission for the UK, including EU and EEA nationals (excluding Ireland), but
not everyone needs to apply for this before they travel. EU nationals, EEA nationals and
certain other nationalities can obtain visitor immigration permission at the UK border. You
can find information about applying for a visitor visa for short periods of study in the UK on
our website here:
Please be aware that Visitor immigration permission cannot be extended nor issued
consecutively, so be sure about your total length of exchange before proceeding. You also
will not be allowed to work in the UK and you will only have access to certain emergency
healthcare for free and should ensure that you have sufficient health insurance in place. If
you accept an offer to study with us, our team of qualified International Student Advisers will
be able to advise you on a range of visa and immigration issues, and help you to apply for the
appropriate visa. This is a free service, and the team can be contacted at
astoninternational@aston.ac.uk.
Health Care & Insurance
Students entering the UK with a Student Visa will need to pay the Immigration Health
Surcharge (IHS) as part of their visa application. Students coming for less than six months
are not required to pay this, but this does mean that you will be liable to pay for certain
healthcare services, such as hospital aftercare, if you require this during your stay in the UK.
There are no fees for Accident & Emergency Services and you do not need to have paid the
IHS to access them BUT you should only use the Accident & Emergency Department at
hospitals for emergency treatment for serious illness or injury.
We strongly advise students to arrange private health insurance to cover medical costs
should you require healthcare during your stay in the UK.
Information about the healthcare system in the UK, including how to register with a doctor,
accessing a dentist and more, can be found here;
Please ensure that you are looking at the information for England.

arrangements in person. Please note, it is against the Law in the UK for an accommodation
agency to take fees in advance from prospective tenants in return for details of properties.

Council Tax;
Please note that if you secure private accommodation, you may be required to pay
Council Tax.
Council Tax is a charge set by local authorities to pay for the local services that they
provide, for example rubbish collection, the Police and Fire Service. Council Tax is based
on the value of the property and the amount payable for the property can be affected by
who lives in it.
Generally, full-time students within Birmingham do not have to pay Council Tax if they
are studying a course that is for longer than 24 weeks per year.
If you are studying a course that is for less than 24 weeks, you are technically liable to
pay Council Tax, but local authorities I.E. Birmingham City Council will consider
exemption requests on a case-by-case basis.
You can find more information about council tax here.
If you are thinking of making a request for Council Tax exemption, please consult the
International Advice Team at astoninternational@aston.ac.uk for advice.
If you are deemed not to be exempt, then you must pay the Council Tax due.

accommodation or housing rights,
whether you are living on-campus or
off-campus, you can contact the SU’s
independent student advice service
(known as the Advice and

email advice@aston.ac.uk.

You will need a passport that is valid for the entire duration of your studies at Aston, including the
exam periods. If you do not already have a passport, or if you need to renew it before travelling,
(excluding Ireland). Information about Student visas can be found on our website here: www.aston.ac.uk/current-students/support-services/international/prospective-students/visa-application-overseas
please apply for it as soon as you receive your offer letter from us to ensure it has arrived before
you are due to travel.
Full Academic Year Exchange
Most students will require a student visa to study in the UK for a full academic year, including EU
and EEA nationals. Information about Student visas can be found on our website here.
One Semester Exchange
Most exchange students joining Aston for one semester (up to 6 months) will need visitor
immigration permission for the UK, including EU and EEA nationals (excluding Ireland), but not
everyone needs to apply for this before they travel.
EU nationals, EEA nationals and certain other nationalities can obtain visitor immigration
permission at the UK border. You can find information about applying for a visitor visa for short
periods of study in the UK on our website here:
Please be aware that Visitor immigration permission cannot be extended nor issued consecutively,
so be sure about your total length of exchange before proceeding. You also will not be allowed to
work in the UK and you will only have access to certain emergency healthcare for free and should
ensure that you have sufficient health insurance in place. If you accept an offer to study with us,
our team of qualified International Student Advisers will be able to advise you on a range of visa
and immigration issues, and help you to apply for the appropriate visa. This is a free service, and
the team can be contacted at astoninternational@aston.ac.uk.
Health Care & Insurance
Students entering the UK with a Student Visa will need to pay the Immigration Health Surcharge
(IHS) as part of their visa application. Students coming for less than six months are not required
to pay this, but this does mean that you will be liable to pay for certain healthcare services, such
as hospital aftercare, if you require this during your stay in the UK.
There are no fees for Accident & Emergency Services and you do not need to have paid the IHS
to access them BUT you should only use the Accident & Emergency Department at hospitals for
emergency treatment for serious illness or injury.
We strongly advise students to arrange private health insurance to cover medical costs should
you require healthcare during your stay in the UK.
Information about the healthcare system in the UK, including how to register with a doctor,
accessing a dentist and more, can be found here;
Please ensure that you are looking at the information for England.

| that comes with healthcare cover, so you can recover any costs that you incur. |

| have a European Health Insurance Card (EHIC). It is important that you apply for an EHIC in |

| Students that come to the UK to study for more than 6 months are entitled to free healthcare |
| --- |
| and they can register for a GP (family doctor) including the medical centre on campus. When |
| you apply for a visa, you will be asked to pay the Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS). This |
| costs £470 and will allow you to use most of the NHS services for free. However, services as |
| prescriptions, dental treatment and optical treatment are not included and need to be paid. |

| UNIVERSITY OF EXETER 2025-2026 FACTSHEET |
| --- |
| Global Opportunities Team Innovation Centre, Rennes Drive, Exeter, EX4 4RN, UK inbound@exeter.ac.uk https://www.exeter.ac.uk/study/studyabroadprogrammes/ Webpage for partners: https://www.exeter.ac.uk/study/studyabroadprogrammes/partners/ The University of Exeter has three campuses located in the South West of England: Streatham Campus, Exeter, Devon St Luke’s Campus, Exeter, Devon Penryn Campus, near Falmouth, Cornwall Students cannot study modules at both Devon and Cornwall campuses. Nomination Deadlines: Nomination 30th April (Semester 1) | 1st October (Semester 2) The home university should nominate their students using our online form, which will be emailed one month before the nomination deadline. If you are a Direct Enrol applicant please contact inbound@exeter.ac.uk directly. Application Deadlines: Application 31st May (Semester 1) | 31st October (Semester 2) Students must complete an online application, with copies of the following documents: Official Academic Transcript from the home university (English translation if applicable). Copy of their passport ID page. Evidence of English language level, where applicable. For more details check our website. Academic Reference (for Direct Enrol students only) Applications submitted without ALL supporting documents will not be processed. |
|  |

| UNIVERSITY OF EXETER 2025-2026 FACTSHEET |
| --- |
| Semester One Dates Semester Two Dates Suggested Arrival: 13- 15 September 2025 Suggested Arrival: 10 - 11 January 2026 Welcome Week: 15 - 20 September 2025 Orientation: 12 January 2026* Classes: 22 September - 12 December 2025 Classes: 12 January - 26 March 2026 Examinations: 5 - 10 January 2026 Examinations: 27 April - 1 June 2026 *Pre-Orientation available to early arrivals on 9 January 2025 Modules Students are expected to study 60 Exeter credits per semester (30 ECTS), students are able to take 45 credits with written permission from their home university. European exchange students must choose 75% of their modules from the department we have the agreement with their home university. Other students should take 50% of their modules within one subject area. Course Restrictions Psychology courses are only available for Psychology-specific exchange partners. Biomedical Science courses are only available for Biomedical Sciences-specific exchange partners. Graduate School of Education, Liberal Arts modules (LIB) and Degree Apprenticeship modules are not available. Where possible modules will be allocated pre-arrival, but will need to be finalised upon arrival and registration. There is a module change period during the first two weeks of each semester. Module Selection guidance will be updated in April 2025: https://www.exeter.ac.uk/study/studyabroadprogrammes/moduleselection/ Transcripts Semester 1 transcripts are sent out in March. Full Year and Semester 2 transcripts are sent out in July. A digital version will be sent directly to the home university and student. Finances Exchange students will have their tuition fee waived. Direct Enrol students can find information on tuition fees on the Inbound website. Living expenses vary depending on lifestyle choices. As a guide, students should budget around £1026 a month to cover expenses. |
|  |

| UNIVERSITY OF EXETER 2025-2026 FACTSHEET |
| --- |
| Accommodation Full Year Students Students are guaranteed University owned or managed student housing if they apply by 31st July. Single Semester Students Students are not guaranteed University housing, there are a limited number of rooms available. We recommend that they also research private housing. A list of privately-owned or managed accommodation can be found on the Accommodation webpage. More semester university accommodation is available in Semester 2. Immigration Students who are not British or Irish nationals must enter the UK with the appropriate immigration permission. FACTSHEET 2016/17
International (non-Erasmus) Exchange Partners
Founded in 1947, Strathclyde Business School (SBS) is an enterprising, pioneering institution of global standing. It is a
triple-accredited business school, holding accreditation from the international bodies AMBA, AACSB and EQUIS and is
one of a small number of business schools worldwide to be triple accredited. SBS welcomes students from over 100
exchange and study abroad partners around the world making it a vibrant and cosmopolitan place to study.
Name of Institution University of Strathclyde (Strathclyde Business School)
Address Strathclyde Business School, Undergraduate Office, Duncan Wing Level 3, 199 Cathedral
Street, Glasgow G4 0QU, United Kingdom
Telephone +44 141 548 4114
Website www.strath.ac.uk and www.strath.ac.uk/business
Helen Templar International Partnerships Manager (Partner Agreements) sbs-exchange@strath.ac.uk
Lorna Bennet International Exchange Coordinator (Incoming/Outgoing Exchange) sbs-exchange@strath.ac.uk
Michele French Exchange Secretary sbs-exchange@strath.ac.uk

(inc revision and exams)

the examination period.

Nomination All nominations and applications must be made online via the University’s central application
portal (Mobility Online). Paper applications are no longer accepted.
Partners should nominate their students using the login instructions provided by the
Recruitment and International Office. Please contact international.exchange@strath.ac.uk if
you do not have a log-in
Further information on how to apply can be found at
http://www.strath.ac.uk/rio/howtoapply/
Application Students must first be nominated by the exchange coordinator at their home institution. Once
a nomination is approved, students will receive an email inviting them to register with Mobility
Online to enable them to submit a full exchange application.
Nomination Deadline Semester 1 (September entry) Semester 2 (January entry)
1st May 1st October

Student Housing International exchange (non-Erasmus) students will normally be guaranteed campus housing
unless there are any extenuating circumstances in which case alternative arrangements will be
put in place and partner institutions will be notified.
Students can apply for campus housing as an integrated part of the online application process.
Deadlines are as noted above and students should ensure they submit their application prior
to the deadline in order to be considered for campus accommodation.
The Accommodation Office will email applicants in July/August (for applicants commencing
studies in September) and in December (for applicants commencing studies in January) with
further information concerning their accommodation arrangements.
Acceptance Acceptance documents will be sent by email from the University’s central Admissions Office
when applications have been approved. Please ensure that the email address provided in your
application has sufficient capacity to receive large files
Class Selection Details of classes offered in the Business School can be found in the SBS Class Catalogue at the
following link. Guidance is also provided on choosing classes at:
http://www.strath.ac.uk/business/undergraduate/international/incoming/informationaboutcl
asses
Classes Open to Exchange students take classes at Levels 1 to 3. Level 2 and 3 classes will require some
Exchange Students previous study in the subject.
Students registered in the Business faculty must take the majority of their classes with us. It
may be possible for students to take one class in another Faculty, subject to approval by the
relevant department.
Students should submit a list of provisional classes as part of their online application. Due to
potential timetable clashes or classes being cancelled or withdrawn, or high demand for
popular subjects, it is not possible to guarantee access to specific classes and applicants are
encouraged to identify some reserves which can be substituted as necessary. Students are
permitted to request curriculum changes during the first two weeks of the semester.

| APPLICATION PROCEDURE – UNDERGRADUATE NON-GRADUATING STUDENTS |
| --- |

Restricted Classes Level 4 classes at SBS are final year classes and assume extensive knowledge of the academic
subject, and are therefore not generally open to exchange students. In exceptional
circumstances, access to a Level 4 class may be considered if the student can provide evidence
of significant relevant study in the subject and can meet all prerequisite knowledge for that
class. Access to Level 4 classes is extremely limited and must be approved by the relevant
department.
Note: Level 4 classes are examined in the April/May diet only. Resits are not offered at Level 4.
Credits A full workload at Strathclyde University is 60 credits (30 ECTS) per semester. This normally
equates to 3 classes per semester. Students attending for a full academic year would normally
register for 120 credits (60 ECTS). Students are not usually permitted to exceed the maximum
workload of 60 credits (30 ECTS) per semester.
Academic Transcripts Once students’ marks have been validated by the Faculty Board of Examiners, 2 original
academic transcripts will be forwarded to the home University. For students who attend in
Semester 1, transcripts will normally be mailed by the end of February. For students who
attend in Semester 2 or for the full academic year, transcripts will normally be mailed by the
end of July.

Visiting Student Programme
Incoming Student Fact Sheet 2026/27
Next Stop York
York is an internationally recognised university with a reputation for quality, situated on a beautiful
parkland campus close to one of Britainʼs most historic cities, one of the best cities in the UK to live and
visit. We place an emphasis on small class sizes, personal attention and guidance, league tables
regularly place us as one of the top UK universities.
• Full integration in regular degree programme modules
• A personal academic supervisor to support you and your studies
• An academic transcript at the end of your studies
• A lively and stimulating environment
• Academic study in one or more departments (timetable allowing)
• Study periods of one semester or the full academic year
• Academic credit for modules to the equivalent of 60 credits per semester
• College membership and access to a wide range of extra-curricular activities
University of York campus
The University of York has a lively, cosmopolitan campus with its own shops, banks, bars and
restaurants, making it an exciting place to live and work, with everything you need close at hand. Our
campus is compact, easy to get around and close to the city centre and has a safe, friendly atmosphere.
The campus occupies two sites: Campus West and Campus East. Large lakes, landscaped parkland and
lots of student activity characterise these.
Our ongoing investment in new colleges, teaching and learning space, laboratories and research
facilities means it has never been a better time to join the University of York!
Application procedures
Students applying to York should have completed one year of undergraduate study and be of good
academic standing. Students can apply to study in up to two academic departments, but need to be
majoring or have a high proportion of their credits in the subject area of their main ‘homeʼ department at
York. We ask that students from partner universities are nominated by their home institution.
Please apply using the online application form for visiting students:
https://www.york.ac.uk/study/international/applying/visiting-students/applying/

Before you start your application, you should check:
● The availability of the module choices you wish to study at York, please discuss these with your
Department International Officer or Personal Academic Supervisor
york.ac.uk/study/international/applying/visiting-students/courses
● The prerequisites for studying in the UK English language requirements, visas, grades), paying
particular attention to the departmental requirements and prerequisites:
york.ac.uk/study/international/applying/visiting-students/courses
● The dates at which you wish to study at York. See semester dates below.
● It is also possible to study courses from our York Language Electives
(https://www.york.ac.uk/language/languages-at-york/york-language-electives/). These can be
as part of your allowed credits at York or as an extracurricular activity. Please discuss with the
Global Opportunities Manager Visiting Students). Extra-curricular classes must be paid for by
the student.

*Students with Korean heritage may encounter special requirements
concerning visa issuance due to dual nationality issues, particularly related to
military service for male students. Below are some typical examples to
consider. Given that this process usually takes more than two or three
months, it is crucial to confirm your status in advance with the Korean
embassy in your region and make necessary preparations for your visa
application.
■Example 1: If students are living abroad without registering their birth in
Korea, they must first register their birth in Korea to either
obtain a Korean passport or proceed with the necessary steps
to renounce their Korean nationality.
■Example 2: In cases where a parent acquires foreign citizenship without
declaring a renunciation of Korean nationality, their child
automatically becomes a dual citizen. Although acquiring
foreign citizenship automatically results in the loss of Korean
nationality, it is essential to DECLARE a renunciation of
Korean nationality to an immigration office in Korea. Parents
who give birth to children after acquiring foreign citizenship
often assume that their child will not have dual citizenship.
However, they later realize that this is not the case. In such
situations, if a student wishes to obtain a Korean passport,
parents must complete the following steps: 1) declare their
loss of Korean nationality, 2) register the birth of their
children in Korea.

| Nomination and Application Procedure for Student Exchange Program |  | 1. Before the official nomination, program managers at partner universities MUST discuss the exchange quota for each academic year in advance with our KUBS exchange program manager. 2. Once the exchange quota is confirmed, KUBS’s Nomination Instruction will be distributed at the end of March (for Fall semester) and September (for Spring semester). 3. A link to KUBS’s online application will be given to the nominees after the nomination period ends. They MUST complete the online application by the specified deadline. Late application will not be accepted. 4. Starting in June (for Fall semester) and December (for Spring semester), the ‘Admission Package’ – which includes 1) the Letter of Admission, 2) the Certificate of Admission, and 3) Business License of Korea University – will be sent via email to students who completely submitted the application form and all required documents). Nominees must have a Gmail account (or 163.com for Chinese students). Please provide with the nominee’s Gmail address, not other email addresses such as a home institution email address. Important notices from our office may not be delivered to non-Gmail accounts. Other addresses may cause automated emails to be blocked or marked as spam. Therefore, please ensure that the nominee’s Gmail address is provided so they can receive all important communications. |

| Entry Requirements |  Must be officially nominated by the home institution  A minimum GPA of 2.5 on a 4.0 scale (GPA by US standard)  Undergraduates must have completed at least 2 full semesters at their home institution before the Nomination/Application starts (Transferred undergraduates / graduates: 1 semester)  Fluency in either English or Korean (evidence of language proficiency not required)  Students who are in their final year of study and/or have required courses for graduation are not allowed to participate in our exchange program. Due to the high demand for undergraduate business courses, it is highly possible that students will be unable to take the courses they need. We only accept students who can be flexible with their course selection and credit requirements during their exchange year. KUBS experiences extremely high demand for undergraduate business courses. Please be aware of the tight situation regarding the undergraduate course registration and to be flexible regarding your course selection. For these reasons, we do not accept the students who have strict credit requirements or who are in their final year of study or need specific courses for graduation are not recommended to participate in our exchange program. KUBS cannot guarantee course registration. |

Please do not upload inappropriate photos. 3) Official Academic Transcript - A current transcript in English with a grading scale, demonstrating the equivalent to 2.5 (out of 4.0) and including grades for at least 2 full semesters (Transferred undergraduates/Graduates: 1 semester) 4) Letter of Academic Reference - MUST be completed by a professor or academic advisor familiar with the student’s academic work and is able to attest to his or her character, maturity and self-sufficiency - MUST include the recommender’s name, title, and the school’s official logo - If your professor or advisor prefers to send it directly to us, please let us know via email. 5) Health Certificate (The form can be downloaded from the application page) - MUST be completed by a physician/doctor only - All exchange students are required to complete this form and submit it within the application period. Those who do not submit the form will not be accepted to Korea University Business School. - The examination must be conducted no later than May (for Fall semester) and November (for Spring semester). 6) Statement of purpose and goals - Describe the purpose and goals of your exchange semester in 1 or 2 pages of word file (A4 size) - Students should write the reason why they chose KUBS as a study abroad destination and what they hope to achieve. 7) Copy of Passport Identification Page (file size under 50kb) - A clear copy of a valid passport that includes a student’s photo, name, and passport number. - MUST be valid for at least 6 months beyond your intended stay in Korea. (If you plan to apply for a new passport, you should inform us in advance.) * If you have two passports (multiple nationalities), you must provide us with the passport you will use to get the visa and the student must enter Korea with the same passport. - If you renew or obtain a new passport after submitting your application, you must immediately submit a copy of the new passport to our office. 8) Letter of confirmation for private insurance/travel insurance - MUST cover the entire study abroad period - MUST state the name, coverage period, and benefits in ENGLISH - Insurance can be submitted via email even after submission of the online application, as students usually enroll right before their departure. - Submission deadline: July 31 (Fall) / January 31 (Spring) to our office via email. * For Korean passport holders, you can submit a Health Insurance Qualification Certificate issued by NHIS or Government 24 instead. 9) Pledge (can be downloaded from the application link) - Must be handwritten (only for the blanks of the form) |

text:
GENERAL INFORMATION
The Student Exchange Programme (STEP) is currently open for masters
students. This fact sheet is for inbound students.
Academic Information
Course Choices and Registration
IIM Ranchi offers electives in multiple domains of management. All courses are of the post
graduate level.
Exchange students have the same freedom in course selection as regular students. The students
are encouraged to go through the detailed course outlines and make a selection of the courses.
The student has to pre-register for the elective courses of his/her choice from a list of courses
updated every year. An elective course is offered if it meets the minimum subscription
condition during the bidding process, which normally takes place in the last week of June or 1st
week of July. In case any of the courses chosen by the exchange student is not offered due to
less-than-required subscription, the student can choose other courses(s) offered in that term,
depending on the result of the bidding process. Nonetheless, IRO tries its best to allot the courses
based on the choices provided by the student.
After obtaining confirmation from the student regarding the course allotment, IRO freezes the
same, and any further requests for a change of courses are not entertained.
They can take whatever courses the institute offers to Master of Business Administration
(MBA) students.

Attendance
Class attendance is mandatory. A shortfall in attendance may lead to a grade fall. Students must
maintain regular and punctual attendance in courses. Instructors have the authority to mandate
procedures to monitor attendance, penalize students for non-attendance, and ensure that
student behavior is conducive to teaching and learning. Latecomers will not be given attendance
in the class. No student is permitted to go on leave during the Term.
To accommodate elective courses, sometimes, classes may be scheduled until late evenings and
during weekends. Therefore, the students must spend time on the campus during the term.
All leave of absence, unless and until the absence is warranted by a medical emergency, must be
authorized in advance and in writing by the Administrative Officer (AO) - Programme in the
prescribed format. Then it should be submitted to the Academic Programme Office (APO).
2

Credit System
All courses offered are either 3-credit or 1.5-credit. 1 credit is equivalent to 10 class contact hours
with the addition of 30 hours of preparation and post-class work by the students.
A 3-credit course is equivalent to 120 hours including 30 class contact hours, and
A 1.5-credit course is equivalent to 60 hours including 15 class contact hours.
Participation: Class participation is part of a student’s final grade in courses.
Workload for Exchange Students: The students should take courses (credits) as per the
requirement of their home Institute.
The Entrance @IIMR
3

Grading System
Grading System
IIM Ranchi follows a grading scheme of 8 levels ranging from A+ to F as given in the following
table:
Evaluation Criterion: In addition to class participation and continuous evaluation the following
format is followed for evaluation:
For 3 credit course: Minimum 4 components of evaluations comprising of mid-term exam
(compulsory), end-term exam (compulsory), and at least two from the following components –
Quizzes, Class Participation, Assignment, Project, Case Analysis, etc.
For 1.5 credit course: Minimum 3 components of evaluations comprising of end-term exam
(compulsory), and at least two from the following components – Mid-Term Exam, Quizzes, Class
Participation, Assignment, Project, Case Analysis, etc.
Examinations
The format of the examination varies. Final examinations are generally held in the last week of
the term.
Exchange students are expected to take exams along with regular students. No permission is
given for a change of exam date(s).
Students have the responsibility to stay at IIM Ranchi until they have completed all examinations.
Transcript of Records
The hard copy of the transcript will be sent to the International Relations Office of the respective
partnering institute by February 15.
4

The Academic Blocks @IIMR
Practical Information
Application Procedure
Step 1: Nomination for Exchange Programme
Incoming students need to apply for the Student Exchange Programme (STEP) through their
International Relations Office in the prescribed application form of IIM Ranchi. Detailed
application form will be emailed to the partner institute after receiving nomination of students.
Step 2: Acceptance of Nomination
Once nominations along with the filled-in application and supporting documents are received
through email, the partner institute will be informed about the acceptance of nomination
approximately two weeks after the application deadline (tentatively: 30 April every year). A
scanned copy of the Letter of Admission will be sent to the student through e-mail and the
original will be sent by courier.
Step 3: Enrollment
Exchange students get enrolled in the Post Graduate level courses.
Important Dates
Expected Arrival Date: Three days before the start of the term.
Orientation Dates: Two days before the start of the term.
5

Visa Details
It is mandatory for all incoming students to arrive in India on a Student Visa. Students need to
ensure they have a visa when they reach India.
Refer to the link below for more details on Indian Visa regulations and requirements:
http://indianvisaonline.gov.in/visa/
Legal Formalities
The incoming exchange students must submit a copy of their Passport and Visa to the Foreign
Regional Registration Office (FRRO), with a letter giving details of their arrival and departure.
The Soul Bridge and Lawns @IIMR
6

Documentation
Electronic Submission
1. Duly filled-in IIM Ranchi registration form received by the candidate by email after his
nomination by his/her home institution.
2.Scanned copy of passport pages showing date of birth, nationality, and address.
3. Official transcripts of all the courses completed to date by the candidate in his/her current
program.
4.English Language Proficiency certificate from the concerned authority of the Institute.
During Enrollment
1.Filled-in Personal Data Form with passport size photograph affixed
2.Photocopy of the Invitation Letter – duly signed by the incoming student
3.Original filled-in application
4.Six passport-size photographs
5.One Photocopy of Passport, Visa & Health Insurance (copy of vaccinations taken)
6.Certificate from notary/competent authority stating no legal cases pending against the student
7.Medical & Travel Insurance
7

The Campus Dog, Jimmy @IIMR
Fee Structure
Tuition Fee
No tuition fee is charged to the students of partner institutions coming on exchange to IIM Ranchi.
The Tuition Fee is to be paid at the home institute. A student on exchange has to pay INR 2,000/-
towards course materials for each course they subscribe to during the term. Thus, if the student
registers for four courses, the total amount would be INR 8,000/-
Food and Lodging
It is mandatory for all students to stay on campus. Exchange students are expected to vacate
their rooms within 3 days from the last date of their examination.
Students pay INR 25,000/- a month towards food and lodging. The amount is pro-rated based on
the duration of the student's actual stay in the campus. Students pay the charges for three
months (3 X 25,000 = INR 75,000) in advance by international wire transfer at the time of
enrollment. Dues for additional days of stay may be cleared at the time of vacating the room.
8

Other Living Costs
Medical/Health Insurance: To be purchased if the student is not covered by his/her medical
insurance (purchased in home country). All exchange students are strongly encouraged to avail
health insurance from their home country, which covers medical repatriation for the full Term.
They may also be required to take preventive vaccination(s).
All payments are to be completed at the time of enrollment, and preferably before the arrival of
the student on the campus.
Beautiful Sunsets @IIMR
Good to Know
General Code of Conduct
It is expected that the students are conformed to strict norms of integrity, honesty and good
conduct in all their dealings and are willing to bear individual responsibility for their work.
The students are expected to obey the rules of the Institute both in letter and spirit.
9

Any work (written or otherwise) submitted to fulfill an academic requirement must represent a
student’s original work. Any act of academic dishonesty, such as cheating or plagiarism will
attract disqualification from the program.
Students are advised to be appropriately attired in a manner befitting the status and the
occasion. Wearing transparent clothes and attire bearing vulgar, obscene, or offensive prints or
language is discouraged.
IIM Ranchi adheres to the federal and state laws which prohibit unlawful possession, use, or
distribution of alcohol and illicit drugs by students on the College premises, or in conjunction with
any college-sponsored activity or event, whether on- or off-campus.
Absence from the Campus
Whenever exchange students plan to go out of the city during vacations, they need to inform the
AO - Programme through email and get his/her approval. After getting the approval, the mail will
be forwarded to the Students’ Engagement and Development Chair (SEDC), Faculty Coordinator
(International Relations), AP Office & International Relations Office.
Other Useful Information
Computer Services: Each student is given an e-mail account after he/she has been admitted.
Computer facilities with wireless internet access are available for students.
On-campus Facilities: Exchange students will obtain a student identity card during international
student orientation. This card provides access to facilities on campus such as a library, IIM Ranchi
bus service, gym, etc.
Transport: Transport is arranged by the Institute for commuting between the Institute campus to
the nearest city center/market free of charge.
Arrival Pick-up Service: On prior intimation to the International Relations Office, pick-up service
from Ranchi Airport can be arranged.
Student Support Services: The IRO provides all assistance to international students and/or
students from abroad already studying at IIM Ranchi.
Library: The IIM Ranchi library is known as “The Learning Resource Centre”. The library has a
mixed collection of both print and electronic formats, which include books, journals, databases,
CDs/DVDs, e-journals, reports, etc. The library timings are 8:00 am-10:30 pm.
General Profile of Students: The post-graduate student batch consists of a healthy mix of
freshers and students with prior work experience in diverse industries like public sectors, NGOs,
consulting, and IT firms.
10

Medical Facility: The Institute has a Medical Consultant with fixed office timings. The Institute
also has a tie-up with local hospitals.
Student Committees and Clubs
IIM Ranchi also has various Committees like the Academic Committee, Alumni Committee,
Corporate Relations & Placement Committee, Cultural Committee, International Relations
Committee, Infrastructure Committee, Media & Digital Communications Committee, Social Impact
Committee, and Sports Committee. IIM Ranchi also has various clubs formed by the students.
Multiple events are held throughout the year. For details, please visit- https://iimranchi.ac.in/life-
iim-ranchi/#clubs
Ranchi City
The city of Ranchi is located at an altitude of 654 meters above sea level on the plateau of
Ranchi. As part of Bihar, it used to be the summer capital from the time of the British Raj because
of its cool and salubrious climate. Temperature ranges from 20°C - 37°C in the summer and 6°C -
22°C in winter. The Subarnarekha river flows by the side of the city.
Reaching IIM Ranchi Campus
1. Airport: Birsa Munda International Airport is around 12 km from the Institute. Daily flights
connect to domestic destinations like Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Mumbai and
New Delhi and international destinations like Abu Dhabi, Colombo, Doha, Dubai, and
Singapore. Pre-paid taxi service is available at the airport, and it would cost approximately
INR 600 to reach the IIM Ranchi campus.
2. Railway Station: Ranchi is well connected by rail with different parts of the country, and the
campus is about 12 km away from the railway station.
3. Click on the link for directions: https://maps.app.goo.gl/1L6Ej9UBT8y43DzQ6
Local Transport: Taxi and Auto Rickshaws are available in Ranchi city.
General operating hours of banks in Ranchi:
Monday – Saturday: From 10:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. (Closed on 2nd & 4th Saturdays)
Sunday: Closed

Exchange Programme Expectations
Academic/Experience Requirements
Exchange students are encouraged to complete core courses and have at least two years
of professional experience prior to their exchange term. Course-specific prerequisites will
be detailed in the syllabus.
Workload
Exchange students can enroll in a minimum of 2 to maximum of 4 or 5 courses per term,
each consisting of 10 sessions of two hours, resulting in 20 contact hours per course.
Additionally, students have the option to take Block Weeks, which are intensive courses
designed to be completed within a week. Each Block Week consists of 5 consecutive days
of instruction, with 4 hours per day, amounting to 20 contact hours per one-credit course.
Attendance
ISB mandates 100% attendance. Students must arrive on campus at least two days before
the term begins (ideally a week prior) and stay through the term's completion, including
exams. Attendance for all sessions of enrolled courses is compulsory, and adherence to
International Exchange Office rules is required. Exam schedules are fixed and non-negotiable.
Mode and Language of Instruction
All classes are conducted in-person and in English. Exchange students must demonstrate
proficiency in English to actively participate in discussions and coursework.

Vaccination

Visa Requirements
