Courses and Programs of Interest to Incoming Exchange Students
Africa and Black Diaspora Studies (Faculty of Humanities)
Africa and Black Diaspora Studies is made up of courses spanning across more than a dozen departments. These
courses provide students with in-depth understanding of Black and African-diaspora peoples and societies around
the world.
https://aads.humanities.mcmaster.ca/
Globalization Studies (Faculty of Social Sciences)
Globalization Studies provides students with the opportunity to explore the complex idea of globalization from a multi-
disciplinary perspective. In particular, the course ‘GLOBALZN 1A03 - Global Citizenship’ will offer an interdisciplinary
introduction to globalization through a critical engagement with the idea of "global citizenship" in the contemporary
context. The political, economic, and cultural dimensions of globalization will be examined, and students will reflect
upon what it means to be a "global citizen" considering how such dynamics shape questions of identity, agency,
power and resistance.
https://socialsciences.mcmaster.ca/globalization
Indigenous Studies Department (Faculty of Social Sciences)
The Indigenous Studies Department is home to the Indigenous Studies undergraduate program, a planned graduate
program, and research and community-focused activities. The Indigenous Studies undergraduate program, one of
the longest-standing programs of its kind in Canada, incorporates a very unique teaching structure of Indigenous
knowledge which involves many Indigenous peoples and Elders. This unique perspective assists all students from
various cultures and background in learning about the history and lives of Indigenous people within an Indigenous
perspective.
https://indigenous.socsci.mcmaster.ca/
Movement and Integration - ARTSSCI 4MN2 (Arts & Science Program)
This two-unit undergraduate course, which brings together Arts & Science students and international exchange
students, prompts critical reflection on the experience of studying in unfamiliar terrain and challenges students to
imagine ways of integrating their experiential learning into their lives. The course aims to help students develop an
ongoing practice of reflective, lifelong learning.
https://artsci.mcmaster.ca/courses-faculty/artssci-4mn2-movement-and-integration/
Sustainable Future Program (Office of Sustainability)
The Sustainable Future Program (SFP) consists of a suite of undergraduate courses focused on providing students
with the opportunity for interdisciplinary, student-led, community-based and experiential education focused on
sustainability. Courses in the program are open to students from all Faculties.
https://asp.mcmaster.ca/academic-programs/sustain-courses/

Term Dates
Academic Information
Course Information
Graduate exchange students must have completed all master foundation (first year/core) courses and may only
enrol in MBA elective (upper level) courses at the Schulich School of Business. Elective courses feature small
class sizes and employ various teaching methods including lectures, case studies, individual and group
projects, term papers, presentations, exams and classroom discussions. Attendance is mandatory and class
participation contributes to the final grade.
A 3-credit course involves approximately 100 hours of work including 3 in-class hours per week over 12
weeks (36 in-class hours/course). A full course load for Schulich students is 5 courses (15 Schulich credits).
Exchange students are expected to enrol in a minimum of 3 courses (9 Schulich credits).
Elective courses may vary each term, and enrolment is not guaranteed so students should remain flexible.
Additional information can be found under Courses & Academics.
Exams
Final exams are scheduled for the week following the last day of classes. Students are advised not to make
travel plans before the end of the exam period however, students may leave early if all course requirements
are completed.
Grades & Transcripts
Students can view their grades online. Schulich uses a letter grade system: A+, A, A-, B+, B, B-, C+, C, C-, F.
An official transcript is sent to the home institution approximately 4-6 weeks after completion of the term.
Additional transcripts can be ordered online through the Registrar’s Office.
Code of Conduct
All students must adhere to the University’s code of conduct, which includes completing academic
integrity modules prior to the start of the term.

International Relations Support
Pre-Arrival Webinar
Before the start of each term, we provide information about arriving in Canada. This includes details on
required entry documents, housing, health insurance, transportation and other helpful resources.
Orientation
The mandatory Orientation offers valuable information and resources to help students prepare for their
journey and integrate into the Schulich community. During Orientation, students will meet the international
team as well as fellow Schulich and exchange students.
Visa Information & Immigration Support
Exchange students are responsible for obtaining the appropriate Canadian immigration documents to enter
Canada. Students studying for less than 6 months can enter and study as visitors but must apply for the
correct travel document (Temporary Resident Visa or electronic Travel Authorization) before arriving. A
Canadian study permit is not required. Please refer to the Visit Canada website to determine which document
is required (TRV or eTA). Students requiring a Temporary Resident Visa (TRV) should apply as early as possible
due to potentially lengthy processing times. Our team includes an immigration specialist to assist with any
questions or issues related to entry into Canada.
English Language Peer Support (ELPS) ADMISSIONS DEADLINES
The ELPS program offers students personalized English language assistance for assignments, cases, papers and
presentation skills. Students seeking support with English proficiency will collaborate with peer supporters,
who provide feedback on grammar, structure, citations and verbal presentation skills.
Health Services
University Health Insurance Plan (UHIP)
UHIP is mandatory for all exchange students and provides basic coverage for visits to doctors or hospitals.
York University administers UHIP registration before the start of the term. Students can opt for supplementary
insurance to cover additional costs not included in UHIP such as medications, dental and paramedical
services.
Student Accessibility Services (SAS)
Academic support and accommodation are available for students with disabilities including AD/HD, autism
spectrum disorders, mental health conditions, physical, sensory, medical and learning disabilities. Registration
and documentation are required and should be submitted once approved for exchange to ensure students receive
the necessary support.
Student Counselling & Development (SCD)
A professional and supportive environment ensures students have equitable access to a variety of services
that aid in their academic success.

Career Services
The Centre for Career Design (CCD) provides students with support to help them achieve their career goals.
Students have access to corporate information sessions, panel discussions, workshops, networking events,
individual counselling, resume reviews and mock interviews.
Student Life
Open Arms Committee (OAC)
The OAC connects exchange students with a
current MBA student to support their transition to
Schulich and Toronto.
Graduate Business Council (GBC)
The GBC advocates for the interests of all
graduate students to faculty and Schulich
administration. It organizes activities that foster
interactions with the business community,
recreational programs and social events.
Schulich’s clubs offer valuable opportunities for
students to explore business interests and develop
leadership skills. From Canadian mining to
investment banking to sustainable enterprise, the
variety of clubs allows students to pursue a broad
spectrum of interests. Exchange students are
encouraged to participate in these clubs during
the term.
Housing
York University’s Housing Services provides on-campus housing options. For information on both on-
campus and off-campus housing, refer to Schulich’s Student Housing Opportunities website. Students are
responsible for securing their own accommodations. On-campus housing is not guaranteed.

About SFU
Simon Fraser University (SFU) is a globally engaged institution known for excellence in research,
innovation, and sustainability. Ranked among Canada’s top comprehensive universities SFU is a leader
in interdisciplinary education, offering programs that integrate diverse fields of study to foster innovation,
critical thinking, and global collaboration.
Born in 1965, SFU has grown into a leading institution with vibrant campuses in British Columbia's largest
municipalities — Vancouver, Burnaby and Surrey — and deep roots in partner communities throughout
the province and around the world.

FACT SHEET 2026/2027
Nomination & Application Procedures
Nomination: Partner institutions will receive an email with a link to the online nomination system when
nominations are open for the upcoming year. Please complete the nomination form by the appropriate
deadline noted above. (Note partners can nominate Winter term students as soon as their selection
process is complete.)
Application: After nominations have been received and processed, students will be emailed directly
with instructions and the incoming exchange application form.
Supporting Documentation:
• Official transcripts (applications without a transcript attached will not be processed)
• Proof of English Language Proficiency (ELP) (if required)
o For applicants required to prove present proficiency in English, a minimum TOEFL
(Internet-based) score of 97 with no section less than 20 (Internet-based test), or an
IELTS score of 7.0 with no section less than 6.0 or a CAEL overall score of 70.
• Current resume (maximum 2 pages)
Students are asked to send their completed application and supporting documentation to us at
mba.exchange@haskayne.ucalgary.ca by the deadlines noted above. Please copy the home institution
coordinator on the email.
Academic Information
Students are asked to provide a list of up to 4 courses on their application; current timetable is online
here: csprd.my.ucalgary.ca/psp/csprd/?cmd=login&public=class-search&. Once the application has been
processed, students will be contacted with instructions for the course enrollment process. Students
cannot register for business courses without permission.
Most graduate courses offered by the Haskayne School of Business are permitted for incoming exchange
students to register in, provided the students have the course prerequisites.
Note there are sometimes courses offered that are not open to incoming exchange students, typically
special topic courses.
Course levels:
• 600- and 700-level courses are graduate level courses
• Anything numbered 200 through 500 are for undergraduate students and not available to
incoming graduate exchange students.
Incoming exchange students must meet minimum full-time enrollment in Fall and Winter semesters
and adhere to minimum enrollment requirements for the study visa (if applicable). Each course is
worth 3 units, equal to 3 class hours per week per course, approximately 30-36 lecture hours total per
2

HASKAYNE SCHOOL OF BUSINESS
INTERNATIONAL EXCHANGE PROGRAM
FACT SHEET 2026/2027
term. Labs and tutorials are in addition to the mandatory lectures; labs and tutorials are sometimes
mandatory, sometimes optional, depending on the course and instructor.
Time conflicts or overlaps are not permitted for any student at the University of Calgary; please
ensure the classes selected for registration do not have any time conflicts between any of the
lectures, labs, tutorials, and/or seminars.
Many courses have a registrar-scheduled final examination, held during the exam period (see Important
Dates above). If students register in classes with registrar-scheduled final examinations, they are
required to be available for the entire exam period. The exam schedule is typically released one month
after classes have started, and exams can be scheduled until 10:00pm on the last day of the exam
period. Incoming exchange students should not plan any travel until after the last possible day for
final exams.
At the end of the exchange term, incoming exchange students are responsible for ordering official
transcripts to be sent to their home institution. Instructions for ordering transcripts are online here:
ucalgary.ca/registrar/student-centre/transcripts.
Study Visa & Insurance
As an exchange student, you are expected to have comprehensive travel and medical insurance. It's
best to buy insurance from your home country and bring it with you. UCalgary does not sell insurance
plans for exchange students, but International Student Services can give some advice if you choose
to buy insurance in Canada.
Depending on what country you are coming from and how long you are staying for, you may require
different documents (ex: study visa) to study in Canada. International Student Services is an office at
UCalgary that provides all information about immigration documents to students. If you have any
questions about your specific circumstances, please contact an immigration advisor.

FACT SHEET 2026/2027
Student Services & Housing
On-Campus housing is organized through Residence Services: ucalgary.ca/residence/.
All incoming exchange students are required to obtain a UPASS upon arrival for each exchange
semester, as well as pay the Campus Recreation fee. This allows students unlimited access to public
transportation (busses and c-trains) for the duration of their exchange term. Transcripts will not be
released to students with outstanding fees. Current fees are listed here:
calendar.ucalgary.ca/pages/d80b6ce5a431469ba19a6ef032fd1672
International Student Services (ucalgary.ca/iss/) offers events for international and incoming exchange
students and can advise on Immigration questions (including study visa/permit and working during the
exchange term). They also often organize the international orientation
(ucalgary.ca/iss/resources/orientation), recommended for all incoming exchange students to attend;
there are also virtual events students can attend prior to arrival in Canada.

deadline noted above. (Note partners can nominate Winter term students as soon as their selection
process is complete.)
Application: After nominations have been received and processed, students will be emailed directly
with an individualized link to the online application. A separate email will be sent with instructions for
completing the application.
Supporting Documentation:

please visit: calendar.ucalgary.ca/pages/e9845c2c03e84596bcaf892d52666fbf
Academic Information
Students are asked to provide a list of 6 to 8 courses on their application; current timetable is online
here: csprd.my.ucalgary.ca/psp/csprd/?cmd=login&public=class-search&. Once the application has been
processed, students will be emailed with instructions for completing registration. Students cannot
register for business courses, and other faculty courses with course pre-requisites, without permission.
Most undergraduate courses offered by the Haskayne School of Business are permitted for incoming
exchange students to register in, provided the students have the course prerequisites. The following
courses are not permitted for incoming exchange students to take:
• Block Week courses (lectures end before regular term begins)
• ENTI 317 – Entrepreneurship and Innovation
• FNCE 449 – Trading and Market Data Management
• FNCE 469 – UCeed Haskayne Student Fund
• FNCE 471 – The Calgary Portfolio Management Trust
• FNCE 559.09 – Decentralized Finance
• LEAD 401 – Foundations in Ethical Leadership
• LEAD 501 – Leadership Studies Capstone
• MGST 217 – Introduction to Business Analytics
• MGST 301 – Research Methodologies
• MGST 501 – Capstone Applied Research project I
• MGST 503 – Capstone Applied Research project II

HASKAYNE SCHOOL OF BUSINESS
INTERNATIONAL EXCHANGE PROGRAM
FACT SHEET 2026/2027
• OBHR 519 – Leadership Expedition
• SGMA 217- Intro Business Skills
• SGMA 303 –Career Strategies
• SGMA 505 -Consulting for impact
• SGMA 591 – Strategic Management
Note there are sometimes other courses offered that are not open to incoming exchange students,
typically special topic courses.
Students may be allowed to take courses from other faculties on campus, depending on prerequisites
and space availability. Please note that economics is not part of the business faculty here. Permission to
take non-business courses must be sought from the department offering the course.
Course levels:
• 200-level: junior level, intended for students in 1st and/or 2nd year
• 300-level: senior level, intended for students in 2nd and/or 3rd year
• 400-level: senior level, intended for students in 3rd and/or 4th year
• 500-level: senior level, intended for students in 4th and/or 5th year
• 600-level & 700-level: graduate level courses, not open to incoming undergraduate exchange
students
Incoming exchange students must take a minimum of 2 business courses (6 units) and a minimum of 3
courses (9 units) total per semester. The maximum course load is 5 courses (15 units) per semester.
Each course is worth 3 units, equal to 3 class hours per week per course, for 12 weeks total
(approximately 30-36 lecture hours total per term). Labs and tutorials are in addition to the mandatory
lectures; labs and tutorials are sometimes mandatory, sometimes optional, depending on the course
and instructor.
Time conflicts or overlaps are not permitted for any student at the University of Calgary; please
ensure the classes selected for registration do not have any time conflicts between any of the
lectures, labs, tutorials, and/or seminars.
Many courses have a registrar-scheduled final examination, held during the exam period (see Important
Dates above). If students register in classes with registrar-scheduled final examinations, they are
required to be available for the entire exam period. The exam schedule is typically released one month
after classes have started, and exams can be scheduled until 10:00pm on the last day of the exam
period. Incoming exchange students should not plan any travel until after the last possible day for
final exams.
At the end of the exchange term, incoming exchange students are responsible for ordering official
transcripts to be sent to their home institution. Instructions for ordering transcripts are online here:
ucalgary.ca/registrar/student-centre/transcripts.

Student Services & Housing
On-Campus housing is organized through Residence Services: ucalgary.ca/residence/.
All incoming exchange students are required to obtain a UPASS upon arrival for each exchange
semester, as well as pay the Campus Recreation fee. This allows students unlimited access to public
transportation (busses and c-trains) for the duration of their exchange term. Transcripts will not be
released to students with outstanding fees. Current fees are listed here:
calendar.ucalgary.ca/pages/d80b6ce5a431469ba19a6ef032fd1672
International Student Services (ucalgary.ca/iss/) offers events for international and incoming exchange
students and can advise on Immigration questions (including study visa/permit and working during the
exchange term). They also often organize the international orientation
(ucalgary.ca/iss/resources/orientation), recommended for all incoming exchange students to attend;
there are also virtual events students can attend prior to arrival in Canada.
If students require academic accommodations (example: extended exam time), please advise your
student(s) to connect with Student Accessibility Services (ucalgary.ca/student-
services/access/prospective-students/how-to-register) as soon as the student has been accepted as an
incoming exchange student.

About the Prague University of Economics and Business (VSE)
The Prague University of Economics and Business (VSE) is the biggest public university of
economics in the Czech Republic.
The 6 VSE faculties offer a broad spectrum of study
fields and branches in Bachelor’s, Master’s and
Doctoral degree study programmes.
5 faculties are located in the center of Prague:
Faculty of Finance and Accounting
Faculty of International Relations
Faculty of Business Administration
Faculty of Informatics and Statistics
Faculty of Economics
1 faculty is located in the town of Jindřichův Hradec:
Faculty of Management
Studies at VSE meet the European Credit Transfer and Accumulation System (ECTS)
requirements.
Currently, VSE has about 15.000 students
and more than 500 academic staff. Two
thirds of VSE teachers hold doctoral
degrees in their field.
VSE graduates occupy important
positions in both the private and the
public sector. Most of them are active in
different branches of industry and
services, business, marketing, banking,
public management, accounting,
auditing, tourist trade and information
technologies.

The VSE’s honourable title of doctor
oeconomiae honoris causa has been
awarded to many important Czech and
international economists, e.g. the Nobel Prize
laureates Prof. Gary S. Becker, Prof. Dr.
Douglass North, Prof. Milton Friedman or
Prof. Robert A. Mundell.
Each semester approx. 1000 international students from all over the world study at VSE
in non-degree and degree programmes. VSE also offers several master (double/joint) and
bachelor (double/joint) degree programmes taught completely in English and many
doctoral programmes in English. VSE has more than 240 partners worldwide involved in
its Exchange Programme.
All Exchange Students study in the one of the three
university campuses which is situated near the centre of
Prague. The courses offered in the Exchange Programme
are given by lecturers from different faculties and
departments. Intensive courses given by international
visiting professors enrich the academic offer.
For more information and news about our school please
refer to VSE website.
VSE is highly appraised both in the Czech Republic and abroad.
Thanks to correct implementation of the credit system, VSE was
certified with the “ECTS label” and “DS Label” by the European
Commission from 2014 to 2018. Both certificates confirm the
credibility of VSE in terms of partnerships with universities abroad.
VSE is ranked by the Financial Times annually and has already
been appraised by the Eduniversal Ranking project as one of the
best “business schools” in Central and Eastern Europe during the
past couple of years. VSE is the first university in the Czech
Republic to be accredited by the Association to Advance
Collegiate Schools of Business “AACSB”, confirming its
membership in a small group of elite global economic universities.
Two Master’s degree programs have been certified with EPAS
accreditation by the European Foundation for Management
Development (EFMD). The Faculty of Business Administration has
successfully completed the EQUIS re-accreditation process and is
still the only Czech faculty with this most prestigious international
accreditation in the field of management.

| --- |
| Fact Sheet 2025/26 |
| Experience a unique study environment at the University of Mannheim. Our centrally situated campus is mainly located in a baroque palace, merely a few steps away from Mannheim's shopping district and the intercity train station. Become part of our vibrant student life and enjoy high-class education at Germany's leading business school, which is known as a breeding ground for future managers. |
| The Campus and the City of Mannheim |
| Online Campus Tour You are curious about getting to know our campus? You can explore it via our online campus tour. Mannheim Studying in Mannheim means studying in the heart of Germany, close to Heidelberg, Frankfurt, Munich, and Paris. Together with its neighboring cities Heidelberg and Ludwigshafen, Mannheim is part of the Rhine- Neckar metropolitan region. About 2.4 million inhabitants, a great infrastructure and several companies form one of the most attractive business hubs in Germany. Next to its industrial charm, Mannheim has many green areas running along its two rivers. It also offers a great variety of shopping, nightlife, restaurants, museums, and cafés. Another local gem is the close-by Palatinate, a well-known wine growing region ideal for hiking trips. |

Please note that the housing situation in Mannheim tends to be a lot more relaxed in the spring semester. Thus, if students have the option between fall and spring, we recommend students come during the springsemester. |

After the nominations have been submitted by our partner institutions, we will contact the students with instructions onhow to complete theonlineapplication. |

Orientation Mandatory orientation sessions take place during the Welcome Week. EUR970–EUR1000*permonth (including rent) Fees By law, every student must pay a semester fee to obtain the enrollment status. The fee currently amounts to EUR 85* per semester. Kindly note that all exchange students need to pay this feeinorder to beenrolled. Services Exchangestudentscan accessthesamefacilities asregular degree- seeking students, such as libraries, computer centers, sports facilities andcafeterias. Further information and services may be found in our central international office’s fact sheet *subject to change |

Business exchange students may also take courses offered by other schools (restrictions might apply) but are required to attend the majority of their courses at the Business School. There is no minimum/maximum required amount of credits on our end, but we Course load recommend not taking on a course load of more than 30 ECTS (credit points) per semester (which we consider a full semester workload). Course registration varies, however, by when and how students need to register Course registration will be stated clearly in the course description in the online course catalog. At the Business School, most of our courses are taught in English. Some courses Language are taught in German. Four-week intensive German language courses are offered in January and in August (special rates for exchange students). The German language courses German language offered during the semester are free apart from a registration fee of 15 EUR per courses course. Each exchange student can take up to three courses per semester. text:
Department International Relations
Julia Brodacki
Tel.: +49 (341) 985 1746
Director International
j.brodacki@hhl.de
Relations
hhl.de/international
Partnerships, Outgoing
Students and Staff Mobility
Friederike Solga
Manager International Tel.: +49 (341) 985 1745
Relations friederike.solga@hhl.de
hhl.de/international/incomings
Incoming Students
You can also reach the International Relations Team at international@hhl.de.
TERM DATES (for 2025—26)
Winter 2025 January 6 - March 16, 2025 incl. exams and orientation (mandatory)
Spring 2025 March 10 - June 29, 2025 incl. exams and orientation (mandatory)
Summer 2025 June 30 - September 7, 2025 incl. exams and orientation (mandatory)
(MBA only)
Fall 2025 September 1 - December 21, 2025 incl. exams and orientation (mandatory)
Winter 2026 January 5 - March 15, 2026 incl. exams and orientation (mandatory)
Spring 2026 March 16 - June 28, 2026 incl. exams and orientation (mandatory)
We do not accept late arrivals or early departures! Students will need to stay for the whole term.
Open for incoming exchange students:
MBA: Fall I Winter I Spring I Summer
MSc Management: Fall I Winter I Spring
MSc Entrepreneurship: Fall I Winter I Spring
MSc Finance: Fall I Winter I Spring
EXCHANGE APPLICATION
Nomination by the exchange coordinator of the partner school via email at
friederike.solga@hhl.de is required!
Online application: apply.hhl.de After the successful online application, HHL will send out the
admission documents by email to the students. These documents will contain all information and
forms required for your exchange. It will also contain an official letter of acceptance (required
for issuing a student visa).
Application deadline: For non-EU-citizens: 4 months prior the requested start of the exchange
period (EU/US-citizens: 3 months).
HHL Leipzig Graduate School of Management | Jahnallee 59 | 04109 Leipzig | Germany
International Relations | Tel. +49 341 9851-745 | international@hhl.de

EXPECTED ARRIVAL DATE
Latest day of arrival should be 1 day prior to the start of the Orientation (incl. in the dates above).
We do not accept latecomers!
COURSE RESTRICTIONS
MBA-Students coming for an exchange term may take courses from the MBA-program and from
the MSc-Program. Courses in the MBA-program may be restricted to exchange students coming
from an MBA-program at their home institution. HHL reserves the right to decide individually
according to specific requirements such as pre-knowledge and work experience, whether
students from other programs are eligible for MBA courses as well. Students coming from
consecutive programs (usually a 4 or 5 years European program leading to an equivalent of a
Masters degree) are welcome in the MSc-Program if there are in the final year.
VISA
Student visa required; students coming with a tourist visa will be sent home. In addition, a
health insurance (unlimited coverage) is required – can be obtained in Germany. Processing
time for a visa can be up to three months at the German consulate!
HOUSING
HHL does not have student dormitories. Some dormitories are available on campus only through
the Student Union (Studentenwerk) Leipzig. If you are interested in renting a student dorm,
please contact the Student Union Leipzig directly (http://www.studentenwerk-
leipzig.de/en/housing). Please note that dormitory places are very popular and apply as soon as
possible.
Private Shared apartment: Leipzig has a lot of open living space available. Some apartments are
fully furnished, others come without furniture. You should possibly look for a place in the following
parts of the city: Zentrum, Zentrum Süd, Mitte, Lindenau, Südvorstadt, Plagwitz (these locations
are close to school). Addresses to contact via Internet:
www.wg-gesucht.de I www.easywg.de I www.studenten-wg.de
The first few nights: For the first few nights in Leipzig – especially if you arrive late in the day –
we recommend to stay in one of Leipzig’s hostels. Hostel “Sleepy Lion”: www.hostel-leipzig.de and
hostel “Central Globetrotter”: www.globetrotter-leipzig.de. You should make a reservation in
advance since the hostels are usually booked.
HEALTH INSURANCE
2

|  |
| --- |
| When enrolling, students are required to present proof of coverage by a German health |
| insurance carrier. Insurance coverage from outside Germany may fulfill requirements; a decision |
| about this is under responsibility of a German public insurance company. Students who are from |
| countries with which the Federal Republic of Germany has a social insurance agreement (the EU |
| member states, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia, Liechtenstein, Macedonia, Montenegro, Norway, |
| Switzerland, Tunisia and Turkey), and who are insured in their home country, should submit |
| their European Health Insurance Card (EHIC). |

APPROXIMATE LIVING COSTS
Around EUR 650 per month – non-EU students must show financial proof of EUR 934 per month
for living costs (together with the visa application).
▪ Housing: around EUR 280 – 600 per month
▪ Meals: lunch for students in the cafeteria between EUR 2,10 and 5,00
▪ Textbooks: around EUR 50 for the semester
▪ Entertainment: highly variable
▪ Student Union fee: around EUR 250 for the semester (required, subject to changes)
▪ Transportation: Included in the Student Union fee (public tram / bus)
▪ Tuition fees: students have to pay to the home university according to contracts
Codes for application:
▪ For US-students: HHL’s FAFSA-Code is G38183
HHL’s Facility Code at the US Dpt. of Veterans Affairs is 3-1-0003-80
▪ For EU Erasmus: HHL’s Erasmus Code is DLeipzig09
ACADEMIC REQUIREMENTS FOR EXCHANGE STUDENTS
▪ Exchange students are recommended to do 20 credits during a regular term. We require a
minimum of 15 credits and allow a maximum of 30 credits.
Only on request of the home university will exchange students be allowed to overload or
underload our minimum/maximum limits.
▪ German on survival level is recommended (not required).
German language courses will be offered to all incoming exchange students on three levels:
✓ A1/A2
✓ B1
✓ Business German
▪ Fluency in English to follow courses successfully and complete the coursework is mandatory!
✓ Language of Instruction is English only
✓ HHL requires a minimum TOEFL 90 or IELTS 7.0 (not older than 2 years)
✓ Exceptions: Native English speakers coming from Australia, Canada, New Zealand,
Singapore, South Africa, UK, USA or students having the undergraduate degree from
one of these countries
✓ Partner Universities having a sound internal testing system for English, that prefer to
use their internal testing methodology instead of the required TOEFL, please contact
Friederike Solga at friederike.solga@hhl.de by the nomination deadline.
3

COURSES
Your students are free to choose courses from three different degrees: Master in Management,
MBA and Master in Entrepreneurship.
HHL offers a variety of subjects in:
✓ Accounting
✓ Finance
✓ Strategy
✓ Marketing
✓ Logistics
✓ Entrepreneurship
✓ Internationalal Management
✓ Macroeconomics
✓ Microeconomics
CLASS SIZE
▪ Average class size: 23
▪ Ratio professor/students: 1:15
CLASS PROFILES
Fulltime MBA:
▪ Average age: 29
▪ Age range: 25 - 45
▪ Average work experience: 5,5 years
▪ Educational background: 26% Business Studies, 20% Engineering, 17% Economics, 14%
Liberal Arts, 10% Natural Arts, 8% Others, 5% Law
▪ Average GMAT: 640
▪ Number of international students: 70-80%
▪ Average number of countries represented: 15
Fulltime MSc:
▪ Average age: 24
▪ Age range: 21 - 27
▪ Average work experience: 1.5 years
▪ Educational background: 27% Business Studies, 22% Business Administration, 22%
International Business Studies/Management, 11% Economics, 6% Logistics Management,
6% Commerce, 6% Business Enginieering
▪ Average GMAT: 640
4

ASSESSMENT AND GRADING
All subjects include different forms of assessment, such as class exercises, assignments, quizzes,
tests or examinations. Individual students are, ultimately, responsible for meeting all course
requirements.
German System ECTS System Explanation
≤1,1 A (best 10%) outstanding
≤ 1,4 B (next 25%) very good
≤ 1,7 C (next 30%) good
≤ 2,3 D (next 25%) satisfactory
≤ 4,0 E (next 10%) pass
> 4,0 Fx fail (second exam allowed)
> 4,0 F fail (second exam not allowed)
P Grades not awarded
In order to assure all of our students the highest level of education, HHL requires all students to
sign an Honor Code, which addresses academic integrity, respectful conduct, amongst other
topics. HHL takes this code seriously and holds its students accountable to it.
KEY ATTRACTIONS OF HHL
▪ HHL has the right by the government to award the academic title PhD
▪ Accreditation by (one out of eleven universities in Germany)
▪ Member of gbsn, efmd, CLADEA and CEEMAN
▪ Rated No. 1 in Germany for Business Administration
▪ High standard with 30 to 40 students per semester out of more than 1,000 inquiries
▪ Highly international with 140 partners worldwide plus an international composition
of the student body and faculty
▪ Attractive environment in a dynamic student city
5

STUDENT SERVICES AVAILABLE
▪ ORIENTATION: Orientation is compulsory for all students coming on exchange (One week in
Fall, Spring and one day in Winter; dates included in the academic calendar above).
▪ COUNSELING: Counselling service and access to HHL’s Career service.
▪ STUDENT CLUBS: There are several student clubs run by the student body – have a look at
our website.
▪ ASSISTANCE: All incoming exchange students will have assistance by the International
Committee. This club organizes several activities, cultural events and tours within Germany
for the guest students.
▪ LOCKERS: are assigned to all students
▪ IT SERVICES: Exchange students will have access to all IT facilities including a personal HHL
e-mail address. All computer pools are open 24 hours / 7 days.
▪ LIBRARY: is open to students and staff 24 hours a day.
Containing some 15,000 volumes, it provides a wide range of basic literature and reference
works for your course as well as specialist literature on current research topics. In addition,
the library subscribes to some 200 national and international periodicals and newspapers.
The entire stock is catalogued on the Libero library system, which is known for its efficiency
and user friendliness. Research into the library’s catalogue can be carried out both within
and outside HHL’s network using a WEBOPAC.
In addition, our students have access to the library of the public university and to the
“Deutsche Bibliothek”. This library is unique in Germany, the collection consists of all what
was ever printed in German, starting in 1913.
▪ SPORTS CENTRE: Leipzig Graduate School of Management is sharing the campus with the
sport’s school of the public university. We have agreed that our students can use the full
range offered by the public university. For program details, please check at
http://www.uni-leipzig.de/sport/
▪ 24 HOUR UNIVERSITY: All facilities are accessible for students 24/7
6

Situated in the heart of Germany’s beautiful Rheingau wine

Frankfurt – one of Europe’s most important financial and
cultural hubs.
Whether you are looking to challenge yourself academically, grow your international network, or
explore Germany’s history and lifestyle, EBS offers the ideal setting for a truly enriching exchange
experience.
About Us
Founded in 1971 by Prof. Dr. Klaus Evard in an empty shoe
factory in Paris, EBS Universität began as Germany’s first
private business university.
The vision: an international, practice-oriented education
closely connected to corporate partners - unlike anything
seen in Germany at the time.
We do this with state-of-the-art didactic methods, with a
coaching and leadership hub dedicated to strengthening
leadership skills and with our teaching approach of
Challenge Based Learning - together with many partners
from the field. This enables our students to bring out their
best and equip themselves to change the world.
EBS aims to develop a new leadership elite guided by
values such as courage, responsibility, and integrity.
Today, around 2,200 students from around the world study on the Oestrich-Winkel campus, supported
by 44 professors and more than 250 staff members.

NOMINATION AND APPLICATION PROCEDURES
Nomination Deadline From 1 April to 8 May for both First (Fall) and/or Second (Spring) semester
Nomination Procedure All exchange students must be nominated by their home university.
The home coordinator must email our nomination spreadsheet (shared via
email) to in_erasmusexchange@luiss.it
Application Period Students are contacted shortly after their nomination and can submit their
application until 15 May for both First (Fall) and/or Second (Spring)
semesters.
Application Deadline for Second Semester Luiss does not accept a second round of selected students for the Second
(Spring) semester after the summer. Exceptions are very rare and have been
pre-arranged with the partners involved.
Application Procedure Online Application System
Application Steps for Incoming Students:
After being nominated by their home university, exchange students will
receive an email with an access code (token) and instructions to register on
our online Web Self-Service platform.
Registration
Students must register on the Web Self-Service platform by entering the
access code, first name, last name, and date of birth. The information
entered must match the data provided by the home university.
If registration is successful, students will be granted access to the system
using their newly assigned username and password. We recommend
saving this page or noting down the credentials for future use (a copy will
also be sent to the student’s e-mail address).
Once logged into the system, students can proceed to the next step.
Application
From the Web Self-Service user page, students should click on Study
abroad > Application Form for Incoming students (Erasmus/Exchange)
located on the right-hand side of the page.
Students will have to upload the following scanned documents:
• A recent photograph (35 x 40 mm, max 5MB, in JPG, BMP, or PJPEG) *
• ID card (for Schengen countries) or passport (for non-EU students) *
• Updated transcript of records in English *
• Language certificates (if required, check with your home university)
* Compulsory attachments
Lastly, students are required to create their Luiss email account, which will
allow them to access their institutional email and most Luiss services.

students should be in good academic standing.
Language Requirements With most of our partners we have agreed that language

As a result, students will not be required to submit an official
an official language test result for the exchange program.

to study at Luiss.

the list. The most up-to-date list of courses is available here.

Course Descriptions Course descriptions can be found here.
If you do not find some course descriptions, it means they are
new subjects and have yet to be published.

Enrolment Guidelines Exchange students will have access to courses across all
disciplines, academic years, and levels (both bachelor and
master), provided they meet the necessary prerequisites

The more they mix areas and levels, the greater the risk of

have the required background and strong language
competences.

June/July, and for the Spring semester in
November/December.
An add/drop period will take place at the beginning of each
semester. Students will have one week to change courses if
necessary.
Most courses have limited capacity, and places will be allocated

Elective Courses Elective courses in all areas will be offered only if enough
students enroll. The final list will be available in late July.
Italian Language Course Luiss offers extensive Italian language courses in both semesters
for exchange students who have been admitted to study at Luiss,
under an exchange program (Erasmus+ or Bilateral Agreement).
The courses are offered at three levels: beginners, intermediate,
and advanced, and are free of charge for students.
Students who attend the courses and meet the requirements will
receive a certificate and earn 3 ECTS credits per semester.
University Structure 3 + 2 - according to the Bologna system
Undergraduate and Graduate Schools
Three-year Bachelor’s Degree Programs (180 ECTS credits)
Two-year Master’s Degree Programs (120 ECTS credits)
Five-year Single Cycle Graduate Programs (300 ECTS credits).
The courses in the fourth and fifth years are more advanced and
equivalent to master’s level.
ECTS Credits Luiss University credits are based on ECTS (European Credit
Transfer and Accumulation System).
1 ECTS is equivalent to 25 hours of study.
Average Workload The average workload for students at Luiss is 24 to 30 ECTS
credits per semester, including Italian language courses.
Typically, full-time students enroll in four or five courses per
semester, depending on the year of study and academic level.
Minimum Workload Requirements Exchange students must take at least one course.
Incoming mobility for thesis research is not permitted.
Maximum Workload Limit Exchange students are permitted to enroll in up to 40 ECTS
credits per semester. However, they are strongly advised not to
exceed 33 credits per semester (excluding the Italian language
course).
Attendance Certificates Attendance certificates will be issued by Luiss and sent directly
to students. The arrival date will correspond to the mandatory
Orientation Day, and the departure date will be the day of the
student’s final exam.

LUISS EDUCATIONAL MODELS
Undergraduate School Educational Model – Engaged An experiential and interactive education split into six phases:
Learning 1. Acquisition - The professor imparts knowledge that
restructures the student’s conceptual framework.
2. Investigation - The student independently investigates the
topics covered.
3. Discussion -Discussion with peers and faculty stimulates
critical thinking.
4. Collaboration - Teamwork generates shared results and
cooperative learning.
5. Practice -Knowledge is applied to real contexts.
6. Production - The student develops original ideas and
produces content.
The aim is to provide not only theoretical knowledge, but a
transferable and lasting learning method, capable of adapting to
new and changing issues.
For those enrolling in bachelor’s degree programs from the
2025-2026 academic year, a compulsory midterm exam will be
introduced. Students can decline the midterm grade and
choose to take the entire test in the exam session, but it will no
longer be possible to decline a grade obtained in a final exam.
Click here and find out more!
Graduate School Educational Model – SMART An education approach to tackle the challenges of the future is
split into five distinctive factors, which define its pedagogical
framework and educational efficacy:
1. Student-Centricity - Customisable education programs
built around the specific needs of the student.
2. Multidisciplinarity - Integration of expertise from different
areas of knowledge.
Fact and Information Sheets 2026-2027 8 of 12

Luiss
International Student Mobility
3. Academic Rigor - Solid theoretical preparation with
advanced teaching methods.
4. Readiness - Focus on the practical application of skills in
the world of work.
5. Tech-Enhancement - Targeted use of digital technologies
to enhance learning.
Graduate School students must actively participate in at least
70% of the lectures. A lecture attendance tracking system is in
place. Those who do not reach this threshold are considered
noncompliant. The student evaluation system adopted by the
Graduate School consists of continuous assessment, designed to
monitor progressive learning during the semester, where
assessments count for 1/3 of the final grade, and a final exam
which counts for 2/3 of the final grade. Continuous assessment is
mandatory and ongoing evaluations cannot be refused. For
those enrolling in master’s degree programs in their first year in
the 2025/2026 academic year, it will not be possible to decline
continuous assessment or exam results.
Click here to find out more!
Examination Periods Exams are held after the teaching period and can be oral,
written, or a combination of both.
Undergraduate and Graduate courses offer two exam
opportunities at the end of each teaching semester (three in
case of Law courses).
Every semester, exam dates are published around one month
after classes start.
Final Exams Exams can only be taken on the official dates.
Exchange students will take their exams under the same
conditions as regular students.
Proctored Exams
Luiss cannot offer proctored Exams.

Exceptional performances may be awarded 30 cum laude (30 e
lode).
30 e lode = excellent
29-30 = very good The minimum passing grade is 18. Grades below 18 are
27-28 = good considered a failure and will not be recorded.
24-26 = satisfactory
18-23 = sufficient Grades below 18 will not appear and cannot appear on the
< 18 = fail transcript of records, as such grades do not exist in Italy.

ACCOMMODATION
Housing for Erasmus and Exchange Students Luiss University, through its Accommodation Office, assists incoming
Erasmus and Exchange students in their search for accommodation during
their stay in Rome.
The following accommodation arrangements are available:
• Luiss halls of residence (run directly by the University) and affiliated
halls of residence (run by a private institution with an agreement with
the University).
To apply for accommodation at one of the halls of residence, students
are required to apply through an automated online booking system.
The system will process applications in chronological order contingent
upon the availability of the desired accommodation.
• Private rooms and apartments
Luiss University has signed agreements with some online property
rental platforms and local real estate agencies for the selection of
private apartments to share with other students.
As spots are limited, accommodation is not guaranteed.
Applying for Luiss and Affiliated Halls of Incoming students must apply online until all accommodation is booked.
Residence Different click days will be arranged according to the semester of mobility.
To participate in the online booking process, students are required to
register in advance, via the link that will be published on the
Accommodation Office webpage.
Please note that additional “click days” might be added based on further

The second examination period officially marks the end of the academic semester. However, many exchange students choose to
complete their exams earlier, typically during the first examination period. Students may take all exams in the first period, all in
the second, or split them between the two — this is the most common approach among Luiss students.
Please note that during the First Examination Period, only one exam opportunity is offered per course.
Considering that exam dates and times may overlap — especially across different years, programs, or levels — students might be
unable to sit all required exams during the first examination period and may need to take the remaining exams during the
second examination period.
The date of the final exam taken will be recorded to verify attendance for certification purposes.

Course Descriptions Course descriptions can be found here.
If you do not find some course descriptions, it means they are

Enrolment Guidelines Exchange students will have access to courses across all
disciplines, academic years, and levels (both bachelor and
master), provided they meet the necessary prerequisites
outlined in the syllabi and there are no major timetable clashes.
The more they mix areas and levels, the greater the risk of

have the required background and strong language
competences.

for exchange students who have been admitted to study at Luiss,

The courses are offered at three levels: beginners, intermediate,

Students who attend the courses and meet the requirements will

ECTS Credits Luiss University credits are based on ECTS (European Credit

1 ECTS is equivalent to 25 hours of study.
Average Workload The average workload for students at Luiss is 24 to 30 ECTS
credits per semester, including Italian language courses.
Typically, full-time students enroll in four or five courses per
semester, depending on the year of study and academic level.
Minimum Workload Requirements Exchange students must take at least one course.
Incoming mobility for thesis research is not permitted.
Maximum Workload Limit Exchange students are permitted to enroll in up to 40 ECTS
credits per semester. However, they are strongly advised not to
exceed 33 credits per semester (excluding the Italian language

LUISS EDUCATIONAL MODELS
Undergraduate School Educational Model – Engaged An experiential and interactive education split into six phases:
Learning 1. Acquisition - The professor imparts knowledge that
restructures the student’s conceptual framework.
2. Investigation - The student independently investigates the
topics covered.
3. Discussion -Discussion with peers and faculty stimulates
critical thinking.
4. Collaboration - Teamwork generates shared results and
cooperative learning.
5. Practice -Knowledge is applied to real contexts.
6. Production - The student develops original ideas and
produces content.
The aim is to provide not only theoretical knowledge, but a
transferable and lasting learning method, capable of adapting to
new and changing issues.
For those enrolling in bachelor’s degree programs from the
2025-2026 academic year, a compulsory midterm exam will be
introduced. Students can decline the midterm grade and
choose to take the entire test in the exam session, but it will no
longer be possible to decline a grade obtained in a final exam.
Click here and find out more!
Graduate School Educational Model – SMART An education approach to tackle the challenges of the future is
split into five distinctive factors, which define its pedagogical
framework and educational efficacy:
1. Student-Centricity - Customisable education programs
built around the specific needs of the student.
2. Multidisciplinarity - Integration of expertise from different
areas of knowledge.
Fact and Information Sheets 2026-2027 8 of 12

Luiss
International Student Mobility
3. Academic Rigor - Solid theoretical preparation with
advanced teaching methods.
4. Readiness - Focus on the practical application of skills in
the world of work.
5. Tech-Enhancement - Targeted use of digital technologies
to enhance learning.
Graduate School students must actively participate in at least
70% of the lectures. A lecture attendance tracking system is in
place. Those who do not reach this threshold are considered
noncompliant. The student evaluation system adopted by the
Graduate School consists of continuous assessment, designed to
monitor progressive learning during the semester, where
assessments count for 1/3 of the final grade, and a final exam
which counts for 2/3 of the final grade. Continuous assessment is
mandatory and ongoing evaluations cannot be refused. For
those enrolling in master’s degree programs in their first year in
the 2025/2026 academic year, it will not be possible to decline
continuous assessment or exam results.
Click here to find out more!
Examination Periods Exams are held after the teaching period and can be oral,
written, or a combination of both.
Undergraduate and Graduate courses offer two exam
opportunities at the end of each teaching semester (three in
case of Law courses).
Every semester, exam dates are published around one month
after classes start.
Final Exams Exams can only be taken on the official dates.
Exchange students will take their exams under the same
conditions as regular students.
Proctored Exams
Luiss cannot offer proctored Exams.

Transcript of Records Transcripts of records will be sent digitally to Partner Institutions
according to the following timeline:

Grading System Individual courses are graded on a scale of 18 to 30/30.
Exceptional performances may be awarded 30 cum laude (30 e
lode).
30 e lode = excellent
29-30 = very good The minimum passing grade is 18. Grades below 18 are
27-28 = good considered a failure and will not be recorded.
24-26 = satisfactory
18-23 = sufficient Grades below 18 will not appear and cannot appear on the
< 18 = fail transcript of records, as such grades do not exist in Italy.
Exceptions cannot be made.

ACCOMMODATION
Housing for Erasmus and Exchange Students Luiss University, through its Accommodation Office, assists incoming
Erasmus and Exchange students in their search for accommodation during
their stay in Rome.
The following accommodation arrangements are available:
• Luiss halls of residence (run directly by the University) and affiliated
halls of residence (run by a private institution with an agreement with

To apply for accommodation at one of the halls of residence, students
are required to apply through an automated online booking system.
The system will process applications in chronological order contingent
upon the availability of the desired accommodation.
• Private rooms and apartments
Luiss University has signed agreements with some online property
rental platforms and local real estate agencies for the selection of
private apartments to share with other students.
As spots are limited, accommodation is not guaranteed.
Applying for Luiss and Affiliated Halls of Incoming students must apply online until all accommodation is booked.
Residence Different click days will be arranged according to the semester of mobility.
To participate in the online booking process, students are required to
register in advance, via the link that will be published on the

Please note that additional “click days” might be added based on further

VISA AND INSURANCE
Health Insurance Non-EU students must hold a health insurance policy to obtain a
study Visa and, once in Italy, to apply for a residence permit. The
health insurance must cover the entire residence permit duration.
To be valid:
• It must cover any case of accident and hospital treatment in Italy
and in the Schengen Area.
• It must cover the entire duration of your stay in Italy.
• It must have a minimum coverage of 30.000.
• It must guarantee the policy−holder's return to their own country
in case of serious illness.
• It must be translated into English or Italian.
Please visit the dedicated webpage for more detail.
EU students must bring their European Health Insurance Card
(EIHC) which entitles the holder to get necessary treatments at the
same cost as an Italian citizen.
It does not necessarily guarantee free services and is not an
alternative to travel insurance (it does not cover private healthcare,
return flights or lost/stolen properties).
For more information, please visit: European Health Insurance Card -
European Commission.
3T

for all exchange students.

Introduction to KAIST College of Business
KAIST College of Business (KCB), established in 1996, has been a pioneer in
advancing business education by integrating management and technology.
KCB is accredited by AACSB and is a member of GMAC, PIM, and AAPBS.
KCB comprises two schools: the School of Management Engineering (Seoul)
and the School of Business and Technology Management (Daejeon). The
School of Management Engineering, located on the Seoul campus, includes
the KAIST Graduate School of Business and the Graduate School of Finance.
Seoul, a vibrant city that embodies the economic dynamism of Northeast
Asia, allows students and faculty to maintain a global perspective while
staying rooted in Korea’s culture and innovation.

Academic Information
Eligibility
• Students must be enrolled in an MBA or Master’s program in business and
be able to take a minimum of 9 credits per semester, equivalent of full-
time enrollment at KAIST.
• Students must have an academic performance equivalent to a GPA of 3.0
or higher on a 4.3 scale (approximately 69%).
• Students must be able to stay for the full duration of the semester (16
weeks).
Language Requirements
• Minimum scores: TOEIC 720 / TOEFL iBT 83 / IELTS 6.5
or a confirmation letter from your home program coordinator.
• Not required if you are currently studying in a country where English is an
official language.
Course Information
• All exchange students will be enrolled in the general MBA program (KAIST
MBA).
• Students may take courses across various programs such as KAIST MBA,
Impact MBA, Finance MBA, and Management Engineering.
• It is strongly recommended to register for 9–12 credits per semester.
• Course offerings will be announced 1–2 months before the start of the
semester.
Course Structure
• Most courses are either 3 credits or 1.5 credits.
• One KAIST credit equals 16 contact hours.
• 3-credit courses run for 16 weeks, while 1.5-credit courses are offered in
half-semester formats (Weeks 1–8 or Weeks 9–16).
Class Format
• Attendance is mandatory. Grades are based on attendance, participation,
individual and group projects, assignments, presentation, and exams.
• Transcripts will be shared by email after the end of the semester.
KAIST Grading Scale
• A+ 4.3/A 4.0/A- 3.7/B+ 3.3/B 3.0/B- 2.7/C+2.3/C 2.0/C- 1.7/ D+ 1.3/D
1.0/D- 0.7

Nomination and application process
Students must be officially nominated by their home university.
Detailed application guidelines and procedures will be provided to nominated
students after the nomination period ends.
Nomination and Application Deadlines
Nomination Requirements
• Official nomination form from the home university (Excel format)
• Must be a graduate-level student to take MBA courses
• Minimum GPA: 3.0 on a 4.3 scale (equivalent to 69%)
• Must meet the English language requirement
Application Documents
• Application form
• Recommendation letter
• Curriculum Vitae
• Official Transcript from Current Institution
• Certificate of Enrollment (with Apostille or Korean consul confirmation)*
*If your home university is located in an OECD country, you may be exempted.
• Proof of Financial Ability : Bank Balance of $5,000
• Proof of English proficiency
• Passport scan

On-campus Dormitory
The exchange program application includes a housing request section:
• Students who wish to live in the dormitory must select this option when

arranging off-campus housing on their own.
• Single room with bed & mattress, desk, and closet
• Shared toilets & shared shower room in each wing (8 rooms)
• Dorm Fee: 270,000 KRW (approx. USD 200/EUR 180) per month
• Must pay dormitory fee for 4–4.5 months in total upon arrival (based on 15-
day rate, according to the academic schedule).
• Students are responsible for their own mattress covers, pillows, and blankets.
• Loud noise, music, and drinking in the dormitory is strictly prohibited.
Study Lab
Exchange students are also automatically assigned to a study lab - a room with 8-
10 personal desks. Each student will given a private desk to study and store
personal items.
Cafeterias
• Student Cafeteria: lunch & dinner
• Faculty Restaurant: lunch
• Atrium: light snacks & coffee
Sports Facilities
• Indoor gym & exercise room
• Indoor table-tennis room & golf zone
• Outdoor basketball & tennis court

Estimated Living Expenses
Alien Registration Card(ARC)
• This is your official ID in Korea and allows you to stay more than 90 days
and re-enter the country.
• Your ARC (Duration of Stay) shows your valid stay period, usually about a
month after semester ends — end of July for spring, end of January for fall.
• We will apply for it as a group during the exchange student orientation,
and detailed instructions will be provided later.
National Health Insurance Service (NHIS)*
• All exchange students(D2-6 visa holders) will automatically be signed up
to NHIS approximately 2-3 weeks after arrival.
• It is mandatory to pay the NHIS bill for the duration of your exchange.
• As the NHIS will start around mid or late March/September, you will be
charged with insurance fee for 3 months: April, May and June or Oct., Nov.
and Dec..
• You will need to pay around 76,390 KRW per month, a total amount of
around 230,000 KRW for 3 months. (2025)
• NHIS will cover approximately 70% of your medical expense when visiting
the hospital/doctor’s office.
• If you have private insurance with full and unlimited coverage, you can
apply for an exemption. The process must be handled directly by the
individual, please contact NHIS at 033-811-2000
Private Insurance for your first 1 month
• The National Health Insurance (NHI) will not take effect until your Alien
Registration Card (ARC) is issued, which is usually around mid to late
March/September. Therefore, you must purchase travel insurance that
covers the period from your arrival in Korea until at least late
March/September.

| Dormitory Fees 4~ 4.5 months | KRW 1,080,000 ~ 1,215,000 (KRW 270,000 per month) |
| --- | --- |
| National Health Insurance(mandatory)* | KRW 229,170 (76,390 per month(2025) X3 months) |
| Meals and Food | KRW 300,000 -500,000 per month |

After Application
1. Apply for a Visa
• You will receive your Certificate of Admission about 2 months before
the semester begins.
• Contact your nearest Korean Embassy and apply for an Exchange
Student Visa (D-2-6).
• All exchange students must obtain a D-2-6 visa before entering Korea —
it is not optional.
2. Prepare to Enter Korea
Prepare the following:
• Passport-sized photo (3.5cm × 4.5cm)for ARC.
• [Dormitory residents only] Health Certificate completed by a doctor
(form will be provided)
• Flight ticket
• Travel insurance that covers the first month of your stay
(The remaining months will be covered by the mandatory Korean
National Health Insurance.)
3. Start Packing
• Dorm rooms include an empty mattress only. Please bring or purchase
your own bedsheet, pillow, and blanket.
• The heating system is centrally controlled, and it can get quite cold at
night — please prepare accordingly.
• Average temperatures:
- Spring: March – Mid-June (15°C / 59°F)
- Summer: July – Mid-September (25°C / 77°F, August up to 30°C / 86°F)
- Fall: Mid-September – November (13°C / 55°F)
- Winter: December – February (5°C / 41°F)
• Other essentials:
- Bring your own laptop.
- Electricity: 220V / 60Hz
4. Upon Arrival
• Check in to the dormitory by visiting the guard’s office on the 1st floor
of the dormitory building. The guard will guide you to your room.
• Attend the mandatory orientation and apply for the Alien Registration
Card (ARC) as a group.
• Check your course registration: Online add/drop period begins one
week before classes start.

2026 Fall Semester Fact Sheet: Sungkyunkwan University (SKKU)
For Inbound Exchange & Visiting Students

| ① General & Contact Information ② Nomination Information ③ Application Information ④ Academic Calendar ⑤ Acceptance Package ⑥ Exchange/Visiting Student Orientation ⑦ Expected Arrival Date ⑧ SKKU Credit System ⑨ Maximum Credits & Credit Conversion ⑩ Course Information ⑪ IEC (International Exchange Course): Course Packet for Exchange/Visiting Student ⑫ Korean Language Program (RKP, IKP, BKP) ⑬ Accommodation (Dormitory) ⑭ Visa and Residence Card (formerly ARC, Alien Registration Card) ⑮ National Health Insurance System (NHIS) ⑯ Buddy Program: HI-Club & SG MAPLE ⓐ SKKU ISS (International Summer Semester) ⓑ SKKU WISE (Winter International Student Experience) |

| ① General & Contact Information |  |
| --- | --- |
| Office Name | Sungkyunkwan University, Office of International Relations (SKKU OIR) |
| Campuses | ■ Humanities and Social Sciences Campus (Seoul) ■ Natural Sciences Campus (Suwon) |
| Contact Information | ■ Office of International Relations Tel: +82-2-760-0156 / Fax: +82-2-760-0159 / Email: incoming@skku.edu ■ Dormitory Office Tel: +82-2-760-0163 / Fax: +82-2-760-0159 / Email: dorms@skku.edu |
| English Homepage | http://www.skku.edu/eng |
| Inbound Program | https://www.skku.edu/eng/International/StudySKKU/Introduction.do |
| Office Address | Office of International Relations (#90212), International Hall, Sungkyunkwan University, 25-2, Sungkyunkwan-ro, Jongno-gu, Seoul 03063, South Korea |

| ② Nomination Information |  |
| --- | --- |
| Home University’s Nomination Procedure | ■ Applicants must be officially nominated by their home institution to apply. ■ The sending institution's officer must notify the SKKU OIR by completing the provided form, which will be sent via email, and provide a list of nominated students. ■ Period of stay can be either 1 semester or 2 semesters, but extension is not allowed once nominated. |
| Nomination & Application Deadlines | ■ Exchange Students (Nomination) Spring Semester: October 15th Fall Semester: April 15th ■ Visiting students (Email Application) Spring Semester: October 15th Fall Semester: April 15th |
| Tuition Fees for Visiting Students (Not applicable to Exchange Students) | ■ Payment Visiting Students are required to pay the SKKU tuition fee. ■ Estimated Cost Approximately KRW 5,200,000~8,100,000 per semester, depending on the major. (USD Reference: Approximately USD 3,600~5,600 / Based on the exchange rates as of March 5, 2026) ※ Note: Tuition fees are subject to change based on the exchange rate.) |

| ③ Application Information |  |
| --- | --- |
| Online Application | ■ Website: https://kingoinfo.skku.edu/gaia/nxui/outdex.html?language=EN&menuId=NIBGG040301M ■ Browser Compatibility: Optimized for Microsoft Edge, Chrome, and Firefox. (It may not function properly on Safari) ■ Authentication Code · Exchange Students: Provided after SKKU OIR receives an official nomination. · Visiting Students: Provided upon receipt of an inquiry email from the applicant or a nomination from the home institution. |
| Application Guide | The Online Application Guide can be downloaded from the online application website. |
| Eligibility | All applicants must meet the following criteria: ■ Nomination: Must be officially nominated/recommended by the home or sending institution (applies ONLY to exchange students). ■ Academic Standing: Must have completed at least one year of study at the home institution by the application period. ■ Enrollment Status: Must be currently in the process of pursuing a degree at their home institution. ■ GPA Requirement: Must have a GPA above 2.5/4.0, 2.7/4.3, 3.0/4.5 or 3.3/5.0 1) When using a different GPA scale, students must provide an official letter from the institution confirming their GPA meets the specified criteria 2) Visiting students are not required to submit a GPA |
| Required Documents | ■ Formal photo (PNG or JPG format) ■ Valid passport (copy of the personal identification page) ■ Certificate of enrollment ■ Official Academic Transcript (showing cumulative records for all courses taken up to the application date) ■ Language Certificate (Applies ONLY to students choosing Business Administration at SKKU) ■ Participation Agreement (Available on the first page of the online application website) |
| Language Requirement | ■ Applicability: Applies ONLY to students who choose Business Administration majors at SKKU. Minimum Scores (Choose one): 1) TOEFL: iBT 80 / ITP 550 2) IELTS: 6.0 or above 3) English CEFR: B2 or above 4) CET: 4 or above 5) TOPIK: 3 or above 6) Duolingo English Test: 110 or above ■ Important Note: Proof of English proficiency certified by a home university (other than the official test scores listed above) is NOT accepted. Exemptions: Not required for students who meet at least one of the following 1) Native speakers 2) Students applying for majors other than Business Administration 3) Applicants from institutions where English is the primary language of instruction (A formal letter from the home university confirming this statement is required) |
| Online Application Period | ■ Spring Semester: October 1st ~ October 31st ■ Fall Semester: April 1st ~ April 30th ■ Late applications will NOT be accepted. ■ Application Confirmation: Please note that individual confirmation of application receipt will not be sent. ■ Follow-up Contact: The office will reach out only to those who require changes or additional document submissions after the application period has concluded |

| ④ Academic Calendar |  |
| --- | --- |
| Academic Semesters | ■ 2026 Spring Semester: March 3rd ~ June 22nd, 2026 (tentative) ■ 2026 Fall Semester: August 31st ~ December 18th, 2026 (tentative) |
| Academic Year | ■ 2026 AY: March 1st, 2026 ~ February 28th, 2027 (tentative) ■ 2027 AY: March 1st, 2027 ~ February 29th, 2028 (tentative) |

| ⑤ Acceptance Package |
| --- |
| ■ The SKKU OIR will provide each accepted exchange and visiting student with an Acceptance Package, which includes the Certificate of Admission (CoA) and a Letter of Acceptance (LoA) required for visa applications. ■ Timeline (Expected) Fall Semester: Late June to early July Spring Semester: Late December to early January ■ Important Condition for Issuance: Please be advised that the timeline above applies only to students who have successfully submitted all required documents in their complete and final form. ■ Warning on Delays: The issuance of the Acceptance Package is strictly contingent upon the verification of your documents. Any delay in submission or the submission of incomplete documents will directly result in a delay in the issuance of your package, which may subsequently affect your visa application schedule. |

| ⑥ Exchange/Visiting Student Orientation |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Date | August 28th(subject to change) | Venue | Humanities and Social Sciences Campus (Seoul) |

| ⑦ Expected Arrival Date |
| --- |
| ■ Early Arrival: It is highly recommended that students arrive at SKKU a few days earlier than the orientation date. ■ Deadline: If a student does not arrive in Korea by September 8th, his/her exchange program will automatically be cancelled. ■ Course Registration: Please note that no additional course registration sessions will be provided for late arrivals, as the registration process is conducted entirely online. |

| ⑧ SKKU Credit System |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SKKU Credit | Class Hours / semester | Self-Study Hours / semester | SKKU Credit | Class Hours / semester | Self-Study Hours / semester |
| 1 | 15 hrs | 30 hrs | 4 | 60 hrs | 120 hrs |
| 2 | 30 hrs | 60 hrs | 5 | 75 hrs | 150 hrs |
| 3 | 45 hrs | 90 hrs | 6 | 90 hrs | 180 hrs |
| ■ Credit Transferability: Students must consult with their home university regarding the compatibility and transferability of credits earned at SKKU, as the home institution holds the final authority over credit recognition. ■ Credit Definition: To earn one (1) SKKU credit per semester, students must complete a minimum of 45 hours of study, which includes 15 hours of in-class instruction and 30 hours of individual self-study. |  |  |  |  |  |

| ⑨ Maximum Credits & Credit Conversion |
| --- |
| ■ Maximum Credits: 18 SKKU credits (Approximately 6~7 courses) ■ Credit Conversion & Transfer: The credit transfer policy should be determined by the home institution. ■ SKKU can provide supporting information and references for credit conversion and transfer. ■ Important Policies 1) As all exchange and visiting students are classified as undergraduate (bachelor's degree) students in the SKKU system, they must follow a separate procedure for enrolling in graduate-level classes. 2) Details regarding graduate course enrollment will be announced during the course registration period. |

| ⑩ Course Information |  |
| --- | --- |
| Course Catalog | ■ Access: The Course Catalog is available on the official English website: http://www.skku.edu/eng ■ Navigation Path: Main > International > Study at SKKU > Inbound Exchange Program > Course Information > Course Catalog. ■ Syllabus Download: Course syllabi can be downloaded by double-clicking the specific course code within the catalog. |
| Course Registration | ■ Spring Semester: in February ■ Fall Semester: in August ■ Notification: Accepted students will be notified of the specific registration period and procedures via email. |
| □ The number of English-taught courses may be limited for undergraduate majors not listed below: Humanities and Social Sciences Natural Sciences and Engineering · Business Administration / Global Business Administration · Civil and Environmental Engineering · Economics / Global Economics · Software · Media & Communication · Systems Management Engineering · Political Science and Diplomacy · Mechanical Engineering · English Language and Literature · Architecture · Sociology · Psychology · Film, Television and Multimedia ■ Some courses in Global Business Administration and Global Economics may be restricted to exchange and visiting students. (Details regarding the above statement can be verified during the course registration period.) ■ Detailed restrictions for specific courses can be verified during the course registration period. □ The course restriction policy applies to various areas, including but not limited to the following programs: Graduate Programs Undergraduate Programs · Specialty Graduate Schools · School of Medicine - SKK Graduate School of Business · School of Pharmacy - SKK Graduate School of China · Public Affairs (course codes beginning with GLD) - Graduate School of Law · Law - Graduate School of Governance · College of Art - Graduate School of Education - Courses in the College of Art are open to exchange - Graduate School of TESOL/Translation and visiting students. However, please be advised that · Special Graduate Schools very few courses are conducted in English within this · Graduate School of Medicine college. · Graduate School of Pharmacy - The Theatre major is not open to exchange students. |  |

However, please be advised that very few courses are conducted in English within this college. - The Theatre major is not open to exchange students. |

| ⑪ IEC (International Exchange Course): Course Packet for Exchange/Visiting Student |
| --- |
| To provide academic courses specifically designed for international exchange and visiting students, the SKKU OIR offers the following IEC courses. Course Code Title Category/Field IEC4007 Economics in Global Environments Economics IEC4008 Understanding Asian Culture Asian & Korean Studies IEC4009 Contemporary Korean Society & Culture Asian & Korean Studies IEC4010 Political & Economic Development in Korea Asian & Korean Studies IEC4014 Comparative Thought and Culture: Horizons East and West Humanities/Interdisciplinary IEC4017 Popular Culture and Digital Media Humanities/Interdisciplinary * Notice: The IEC course list is subject to change and courses may be added or removed without prior notice depending on university circumstances. |

| --- | --- | --- |
