| ⑫ Korean Language Program (RKP, IKP, BKP) |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Program | Campus | Detail | Credit | Note |
| Regular Korean (RKP) | Seoul | • Duration: 4 hours per day • Days: Monday ~ Friday (5 days a week) • Class Hours 09:00 - 12:50 or 14:00 - 17:50 | 12 | ■ Program Extension: Students taking the Regular Korean Program for two consecutive semesters must re-apply for the second semester according to the announced procedure. ■ Class Placement: Course levels are assigned based on a mandatory placement test. Students are not permitted to select or change their assigned classes. ■ Scheduling Conflicts: If you plan to take other academic courses alongside RKP, you must ensure there are no scheduling overlaps. RKP classes require full attendance during their designated hours. ■ Academic Calendar: RKP operates on its own separate academic schedule, which differs from the standard university calendar. Please check the specific dates on the https://skb.skku.edu/ksli_eng/program/regular.do |
| Intensive Korean (IKP) | Seoul | • Duration: 6 hours per week • Days: Mon/Wed or Tue/Thu | 6 | ■ Program Purpose: Designed for students who wish to pursue intensive Korean language study alongside their regular academic coursework. ■ Placement Policy: Class levels are determined by a mandatory placement test. Students are not permitted to arbitrarily select or request changes to their assigned classes. |
| Basic Korean (BKP) | Seoul & Suwon | • Duration: 3 hours per week • Days: Mon/Wed or Tue/Thu | 3 | ■ Course Objective: A "Survival Korean" course specifically designed for absolute beginners to help with daily life in Korea. ■ Registration: Enrollment is available during the standard course registration period. ■ Capacity Warning: Please note that seats are limited and will be filled on a first-come, first-served basis. Early registration is recommended. |
| Detailed application procedures and schedules for RKP and IKP will be communicated to accepted students via email. |  |  |  |  |

| ⑬ Accommodation (Dormitory) |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Campus | Dormitory | Fee / four months (Subject to change) | Location |
| Seoul (Humanities and Social Sciences campus) | C-House | 1,700 USD (Meal plan not available) | Off-campus |
|  | M-House |  |  |
| Suwon (Natural Sciences Campus) | Shin-gwan | 1,400 USD (Meal plan available, but the cost not included in the dormitory fee) | On-campus |
| ■ Accommodation Availability: Starting from the 2026 Academic Year, please be advised that dormitory placement may not be guaranteed for all exchange and visiting students due to high demand. ■ Off-campus Housing Support: For students who are not assigned to a dormitory or prefer to live independently, basic tips and resources for finding private accommodation in Seoul will be provided. ■ Random Assignment: Dormitories and room types are randomly assigned. Requests for changes are not accepted. ■ Campus Verification: Before applying, students must verify the campus where their desired courses are held. ■ Payment Warning: International wire transfers may take several days. Failure to remit the full fee by the deadline will result in automatic cancellation of the housing application. ■ Application Info: Housing application details will be sent via email only to students who have successfully submitted all required admission documents. ※ Please note that all information provided is subject to change |  |  |  |

| ⑭ Visa and Residence Card |
| --- |
| ■ Visa Requirements · Visa Types: Exchange students must apply for a D-2-6 visa, and visiting students must apply for a D-2-8 visa. Pre-entry Application: Students must secure their D-2 visa in their home country before entering Korea. · Important: SKKU is not responsible for any issues arising from entering Korea on a tourist visa (K-ETA). ■ Residence Card (formerly ARC) · Application Methods: You may apply for your Residence Card individually or through a group application managed by the university's designated agency (Hire Diversity). Please note that agency fees may apply. · Issuance Timeline: It typically takes about 45 days to receive the card. This timeline is subject to change by the Immigration Office and is the same for both individual and group applications. · Travel Restrictions: If you leave Korea after entering on a D-2 visa before your Residence Card is issued, your visa will be automatically invalidated. · International travel is only permitted after you have physically received your Residence Card. We strongly recommend planning trips after the midterm exams. ■ Visa Extensions · Personal Extensions: Requests for visa extensions for personal reasons after the semester ends must be handled individually. The university does not provide administrative assistance for post-program extensions. |

| ⑮ Mandatory Health Insurance: National Health Insurance Service (NHIS) |
| --- |
| ■ In accordance with Korean law, all international students holding a D-2 visa are required to subscribe to the National Health Insurance (NHI). ■ Automatic Enrollment: Enrollment occurs automatically once your Residence Card is issued. No separate application is required. ■ Monthly Premium: Approximately USD 60 per month. · Note: This fee is billed monthly. Students do not need to take any initial action for enrollment. ■ Visa Restrictions: Please be aware that failure to pay the monthly premiums may result in restrictions on visa extensions or other administrative disadvantages. ■ Supplemental Insurance: Since the NHI may not cover all medical contingencies (e.g., specific emergencies or private hospital room charges), we strongly recommend maintaining personal full-coverage insurance during your stay. |

| ⑯ Student Life & Buddy Program (SG MAPLE) |
| --- |
| ■ The SKKU OIR and HI-Club (a student group supporting international students) manage a dedicated buddy program called SG MAPLE. This program is designed to help you settle into Korean life and build lasting friendships with SKKU students. ■ Experience Korean Culture: Throughout the semester, you can participate in weekly or monthly cultural activities to experience various aspects of Korea. ■ Exciting Events & Field Trips: Enjoy your exchange period by joining field trips to famous tourist spots, participating in Sports Day, and engaging in diverse social events with your buddies. ■ Stay Connected: Follow the HI-Club on Instagram for the latest updates on events and matching schedules. ■ Instagram: @skku_hiclub |

※ Note: The information provided in this Fact Sheet is subject to change without prior notice, depending on the university’s internal policies
and circumstances.

| ⓐ SKKU ISS (International Summer Semester) |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Description | The SKKU International Summer Semester (ISS) is an annual 4-week summer program hosted at Sungkyunkwan University. Details about this year’s program are available on the official website. Each year, the program brings together highly motivated students from partner universities around the world to study at SKKU’s Seoul campus and engage in a vibrant international learning environment. ISS offers a wide range of courses taught in English by renowned professors from leading universities worldwide, covering diverse academic fields. Some courses incorporate field trips and experiential learning activities, allowing students to connect classroom knowledge with real-world contexts in Seoul and beyond. In addition to regular academic courses, the program also offers a Research Internship Track, through which students can join research laboratories at SKKU and work closely with faculty members on academic research projects. Beyond the classroom, students participate in various cultural activities designed to introduce Korean history, traditions, and contemporary culture, creating opportunities to experience Korea while building friendships with peers from around the world. Exchange students are eligible for a 100% tuition scholarship, meaning that tuition fees are waived. (Please note that cultural activity fees may still apply.) |  |  |
| Official Website | https://summer.skku.edu (QuickLink) | Contact | issoffice@skku.edu / +82-2-760-0184 |

| ⓑ SKKU WISE (Winter International Student Experience) |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Description | The SKKU Winter International Student Experience (WISE) is an annual 3-week winter program held from late December to early January. Details about this year’s program are available on the official website. Similar to the summer program, WISE combines academic coursework with cultural experiences, offering students a unique opportunity to study in Korea during the winter season. Courses are delivered primarily by distinguished SKKU professors in an intensive 12-day format, allowing students to engage deeply with their subjects while experiencing campus life at SKKU. In addition to the academic program, students can participate in a range of cultural activities designed to introduce Korean history, traditions, and contemporary culture. Exchange students are eligible for a 100% tuition scholarship, meaning that tuition fees are waived. (Please note that cultural activity fees may still apply.) |  |  |
| Official Website | https://winter.skku.edu (QuickLink) | Contact | wiseoffice@skku.edu / +82-2-760-0184 |

text:
EXCHANGE STUDENT SERVICES
UF FACT SHEET 2025-2026
CONTACT
University of Florida International Center
1765 Stadium Rd. 170 Hub
P.O. Box 113225
Gainesville, FL 32611
www.internationalcenter.ufl.edu
UF OUTBOUND
STUDY ABROAD SERVICES
John J. Mulligan
Interim Director, Study Abroad Sevices
jmulligan@ufic.ufl.edu
OUTGOING COORDINATORS
Advisors vary by region.
INBOUND TO UF
Amila Tica
Coordinator, Exchange Student Services
atica@ufic.ufl.edu
+1-352-294-3333
IMPORTANT DATES
Nomination Application
Fall Semester April 1 May 1
Spring Semester September 1 October 1
Summer Semester February 1 March 1
2025-2026 Academic Calendar
• Fall 2025: August 21 - December 12
• Spring 2026: January 12 - May 1
Please note that these dates are general semester dates. Graduate Business
school dates and Law school dates may be different than those listed above.
APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS
• Stage 1: Partner School Nomination; Partner school submits on-line nomination.
• Stage 2: UF International Center Online Application
• Stage 3: Post Acceptance Consecutive Processes
A. Student Visa application – apply at nearest US Embassy/Consulate
B. UF student account set-up and pre-registration requirments – process
internal to UF

ENGLISH PROFICIENCY
Per federal regulations, J1 Visa holders must verify they have proficient English
level to participate in their program. Partner schools should include appropriate
documentation at the time of the online nomination. Options for verification are:
1. Student is a passport holder of a country where English is an official
language. Listed here.
2. Student has attended a university in a country where English is an official
language. Listed here. Transcript required at the time of application
submission.
3. Student has achieved sufficient scores on English language competency
exam:
- IELTS Academic: 6.0 Overall
- MELAB: 77
- TOEFL iBT: 80
- TOEFL PBT: 550
- Verbal GRE: 140
- GATEWAY English Test: 425
- CEFR: B2
4. Home University can verify proficiency. Select this option at the time of
nomination. May submit additional documentation in support (for example,
letter of verification).
VISA INFORMATION
• The UF International Center online application covers meeting criteria for the
J1 visa status.
• Upon submission of a complete application and acceptance, Exchange
Student Services will issue a form of eligibility for J1 status sponsorship, DS-
2019 Form.
• Students then receive instructions to apply for their J1 visa.
ACCOMMODATIONS
• On-Campus Housing is limited and therefore not guaranteed to students.
• Students can indicate interest in living on-campus via their online application.
Upon submission of the complete application, students will be considered on
a first come, first serve basis until slots are filled.
• The on-campus dorm for exchange students is Weaver Hall. Weaver Hall
is part of the International Living Learning Community. Please note, to
increase the opportunity for exchange students to live on-campus, students
may be assigned to other dorms outside of Weaver Hall.
• UF Housing will contact students directly to begin the housing application
process.
• UF offers support for off-campus housing through the Off Campus Life office.
Ultimately, students are responsible for their own off campus housing.
International Center
UNIVERSITY of FLORIDA

HEALTH INSURANCE
All UF students are required to have health insurance that meets Affordable Care
Act (ACA) coverage standards. This coverage standard also fulfills international
student visa requirements. The UF Health Insurance policy is an “opt-out”
system. All UF students, including exchange students, will be automatically
enrolled in UF’s Health Insurance Plan. Students can either:
1. Stay enrolled in the UF Health Plan, OR
2. Submit a waiver to request approval for an outside policy by deadline
(outside policy must be comparable to ACA coverage).
NOTE: UF does not accept overseas or travel insurance plans. Students who do
not wish to purchase the UF plan should contact the UF Health Compliance Office
for more information. For additional questions, contact: insurance@ufic.ufl.edu.
ACADEMICS
Minimum credits required per semester
• Undergraduate Students: 12 (typically 4 courses worth 3 credits each)
• Graduate Students: 9 (typically 3 courses worth 3 credits each)
Important Considerations
• Students are allowed to enroll in one 100% on-line course per semester
• Students may not be eligible to participate in restricted enrollment programs
• Students must primarily choose courses from their hosting college. Students
may choose up to one course outside of their hosting college, unless
otherwise specified by their UF academic and exchange advisor.
BUDGETING & COSTS
Estimated Cost of Living:
https://internationalcenter.ufl.edu/j-1-studentscholar/partner-school-exchange-
students/estimated-costs-budgets
Application Funding Requirement: The U.S. government requires J-1 students
to prove sufficient funds for the duration of their program. To meet this
requirement, students must show they have a minimum USD $2300 per month of
the program.
STUDENT LIFE & RESOURCES
• Student Activities and Involvement – Check out student organizations and
daily campus events at this website: https://studentinvolvement.ufl.edu/get-
involved
• UF NaviGators International – Connects International Students with
American students through a unique mentorship program.
https://www.facebook.com/ufnavigatorsintl
• Counselling & Wellness Center (CWC) - https://www.counseling.ufl.edu/cwc
• Gainesville Regional Transit System (RTS) – Students can ride any
Gainesville RTS bus free with their Gator 1 ID card. www.go-rts.com
International Center • Disability Resource Center – https://disability.ufl.edu
UNIVERSITY of FLORIDA • COVID-19 Updates & Resources – https://coronavirus.ufhealth.org

text:
Please note: many of the questions and issues in this fact sheet are addressed in the
Handbook for International Exchange Students accessible as a PDF file on the Purdue
Study Abroad website: http://www.studyabroad.purdue.edu/incoming/
Programs for Study Abroad
Purdue University
302 Wood Street
West Lafayette, IN 47907
USA
Tel +765 494 2383
Fax +765 496 1989
web site www.studyabroad.purdue.edu
Contact: Nancy J. Bennett
Assistant Director
njbennett@purdue.edu
1. Term dates and application deadlines
fall semester or academic year early August late December March 15
spring semester early January early May October 15
2. Exchange Program Application and required documents
a) download application from http://www.studyabroad.purdue.edu/incoming/
b) clear copy of passport
c) original signed letter from bank attesting to availability of $5,525
d) transcript (in English)
e) information about English language ability if language of instruction is not
English
3. Housing: see website above
application for campus housing form is downloadable from web site
deposit required
off-campus housing must be found by student; Purdue cannot offer assistance in
locating rooms, apartments or roommates

4. Courses:
see http://www.purdue.edu/Purdue/course_info/
students need to list requested courses on application
students must enroll in a minimum of 12 credit hours per semester
5. Orientation: Exchange students are required to participate in the International
Student Orientation organized by the Purdue Office of International Students and
Scholars. This takes place one week prior to the beginning of fall and spring semester.
6. Visa: The exchange student application and the supporting documents are
forwarded to the Purdue Office of International Students and Scholars for the
preparation of a DS 2019 visa document. With that document the student applies at the
closest U.S. consulate for a student visa.
7. Credits: Purdue uses the credit hour system. Since most courses at Purdue are
worth 3 or 4 credits, students generally take 4 to 5 courses per semester. Exchange
students in the past have commented that courses at Purdue involve a lot more work so
we do not recommend that they take more than five courses per semester.
8. Grades: Academic performance in each course is evaluated by the professor using
letter grades of “A” to “F” . The grading system used to evaluate a student’s academic
performance is based on a four-point scale. At the end of the semester you will receive
a number of credits corresponding to the courses you have successfully completed.
These credits are multiplied by your grades to determine your “grade-point average”
(G.P.A.). A G.P.A. provides a general indication of overall academic performance and is
used by graduate school admissions offices and employers interested in a student's
academic history. Generally, undergraduate students are expected to complete their
studies with a “C” average or better.
9. Costs and Budgets: Tuition is to be paid at your home university. Applicants must
show that they have a minimum of $5,525 to cover the following: housing and meals,
$5,030 and books and supplies, $ 495. these figures do not include costs for
entertainment or travel within the U.S.
10. The Purdue Office of International Students and Scholars organizes an
International Friendship Program. Please see http://www.iss.purdue.edu/Programs/IFP/

title: UW Foster Inbound Exchange Welcome Booklet_0.pdf
text:
Foster Inbound
Exchange Student
Welcome
Booklet

Welcome to the Michael G. Foster School of
Business
Welcome to the University of Washington! Situated in the heart of Seattle, the University prides
itself not only on its academic merits, but a fun, fast, urban environment as well. As you will find
out, there are endless activities and places to experience in Seattle. In order to make your stay as
enjoyable as possible, we would like to share some information with you. What you will find in
the welcome packet is a list of campus events and information centers, as well as a more general
look at what Seattle offers. Our hope is that you will not only enjoy the academic benefits of the
University but the city of Seattle, and the beautiful Pacific Northwest, as well!
Sincerely,
Theresa Maloney
Assistant Director

CAMPUS SEATTLE PACIFIC NORTHWEST
4.
Campus Life / Events
6.
Seattle / Events / Attractions
10.
Pacific Northwest: Places to Visit
12.
Contact Us / Resources

Campus Life
01. The Arts
Meany Hall
Meany Hall for the Performing Arts is located on the southwest corner of the UW’s Central Plaza (“Red Square”). The theater
features the UW World Series and world renowned dancers and artists. Discounts are offered for students and faculty.
https://meanycenter.org/
Henry Art Gallery
The only museum dedicated to contemporary art in our region, the Henry is internationally recognized for our groundbreaking
exhibitions, for being on the edge of contemporary art and culture, and for being the first to premiere and sponsor new works
by artists of note. Admission is free with Husky Card.
https://henryart.org/
Burke Museum
Dedicated to natural history and culture in the Pacific Northwest, the Burke Museum is located on UW’s campus. Free admission
with Husky Card.
http://www.burkemuseum.org/
02. Sports and Activities
Intramural Activities Building (IMA)
The IMA staff invites you to enjoy the exercise, sports and fitness opportunities
available to students, faculty and staff members at the University of Washington.
Intramural Sports
From racquetball to soccer, the intramural program allows anyone to participate an
organized sport. Sign up with a team or play as a free agent!
http://www.washington.edu/ima/intramurals/
Waterfront Activities Center
The Waterfront Activities Center (WAC), located directly behind Husky Stadium on
Union Bay and the Montlake Cut, offers canoe, kayak and rowboat rentals.
Gear Garage
Sharing a building with the WAC, the Gear Garage offers economical equipment rental
for camping, biking, fishing, rock climbing, spike ball, horseshoes, snowshoeing, bocce
ball and more!
https://www.washington.edu/ima/uwild/equipment-rental/
Golf Driving Range

text:
| Undergraduate Exchange Fact Sheet 2026-2027 UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON FOSTER SCHOOL OF BUSINESS Study business where innovation thrives and opportunity surrounds you. At the Michael G. Foster School of Business, you’ll learn from top-ranked faculty in the heart of Seattle - home to global business leaders and breathtaking natural beauty. #1 Undergraduate Business Program in the U.S. Northwest 50,000+ students from over 100 countries |
| --- |
|  |
|  |

| Foster School of Business Undergraduate Contacts Josie Kraft | Associate Director Outgoing Exchange Manager & Agreements tel: +1.206.616.3806 email: jgkraft@uw.edu Theresa Maloney | Assistant Director Incoming Exchange Manager tel: +1.206.221.2205 email: tmaloney@uw.edu Global Business Center Foster School of Business University of Washington Founders Hall, Box 353200 Seattle, WA 98195-3200 USA Websites Foster Inbound Exchange Student Website UW Visiting Exchange Student Website Global Business Center Orientations Foster Inbound Exchange Orientation UW Study Abroad Office and International Student Services Orientation | SPECIALIZATIONS AT FOSTER Accounting Entrepreneurship Finance Human Resources Management Information Systems Marketing Operations and Supply Chain Management COURSES Students must attend the UW on a full-time basis. A full-time course load is 12-18 UW credits per quarter. 18 credits is the maximum. Quarters run for 10 weeks plus 1 week for final exams. Foster Inbound Exchange Students typically take three or four 300- to 400-level business courses with each business course carrying 4 UW credits. Demand and space constraints make Finance, Information Systems, and Accounting courses difficult to get into. Foster Inbound Exchange Students are allowed to take as many non-business coursework as they like if they meet the prerequisites and are granted access by the department. LEARNING EXPECTATIONS Class formats include lecture and discussion, in-class presentations and case studies. Attendance in required. Grading is based on papers, group projects, case studies, class participation and exams. Exam formats may vary. Typically exams are held during the final week of the quarter. LENGTH OF CLASS A typical 300- or 400-level 4-credit business course runs 2 days per week, for 2 hours per day, for a total of 4 hours of class time each week or 40 hours of class time during a quarter. Courses usually run either Monday and Wednesday, or Tuesday and Thursday anytime from 8:30 a.m. until 5:20 p.m. Courses outside the Foster School operate on different schedules. COURSE REGISTRATION Please check out the Foster Inbound Exchange Student Website to the left to learn more about the process and considerations for business course registration. |
| --- | --- |

| EXCHANGE APPLICATION Application Nomination Application Admissions Academic Term Open Deadline Deadline Decisions Autumn Quarter Early Late May/ March 1 March 15 (September - December) January Early June Winter Quarter Early Mid/late August 1 August 15 (January - March) June October Spring Quarter Early Mid/late November 1 November 15 (March-June) September January NOMINATION LINK SENT BY EMAIL There will be two mandatory orientation sessions to attend at the start of the quarter. One is organized by the UW Study Abroad Office and the other by the Foster School of Business. Both orientations are important and required. They will take place a few days before the quarter begins or on the first day of classes. APPLICATION REQUIREMENTS GPA: Equivalent of 3.0 out of 4.0 Be enrolled at a partner school at the 3rd or 4th year level English Proficiency Requirements*: TOEFL (IBT): minimum 76, recommended 105 IELTS: minimum 6.0, recommended 7.0 Duolingo: minimum 110, recommended 131 Exception: If your primary and secondary education took place in Australia, Canada (English- speaking provinces), the United Kingdom, Ireland, New Zealand or the U.S., you are exempt from this requirement. *Please note that letters from home universities are no longer accepted. |
| --- |
|  |

T H E U W E X C H A N G E

| ACADEMICS UW Academic Calendar Time Schedule with quarter-specific offerings Foster business course syllabi and business course tracker Foster School of Business undergraduate curriculum UW Grading Scale |

| STUDENT LIFE Foster Inbound Exchange Student Website UW Visiting Exchange Student Website Over 1,000 Registered Student Organizations (RSOs) with 30+ being Foster-specific Recreational sports, classes and events CIRCLE (Center for International Relations & Cultural Leadership Exchange) |
| --- |

| HOUSING On campus housing is available for students who indicate they are interested in on campus housing in their UW exchange application, and who apply by the housing priority deadline. There are also many off campus options should students want to arrange their housing independently. |
| --- |

| ESTIMATED EXPENSES As part of the exchange agreement, students will receive a waiver of tuition and technology fees up to 18 credits. Please note that the following fees are not covered by the tuition waiver: U-PASS (bus pass) Health Insurance (ISHIP) Course fees if applicable (Some courses charge additional fees for instructional and/or laboratory) |
| --- |

| VISA INFORMATION Exchange students will study at UW under the J-1 visa category unless they have US citizenship or permanent residence. Students who need a visa will submit proof of finances and other documentation once accepted. Students will receive an electronic copy of their DS-2019. |

Academic Information
Course requirement & ECTS
► A semester is composed of 30 ECTS and an
academic year of 60 ECTS.
► In certain exchange programs outside of the Double
Degrees, students could be allowed to follow fewer
ECTS (with previous authorization of home university)
but no fewer than 25 ECTS.
► Courses cannot be mixed and matched between
programs.
► Grenoble Ecole de Management reserves the right
to modify courses in the interest of academic
development.
Timetable
► Please note that the organization of the semester and of the academic year can differ from your home
university.
► At GEM, you will have about 25-30 hours of class during the week. The timetable is planned for one semester,
but some changes can occur during the semester.
► A course can take place during the whole semester as well as for one month only, even if the final exam is at
the end of the semester.
French as a Foreign Language (FLE)
► All our English exchange programs include a compulsory “French as Foreign Language” (FLE) module.
► A placement test will be carried out upon arrival to set up the group levels (complete beginners are welcome).
► If the home university does not recognize the French course, students will be able to choose alternative business
modules.

Additional information and contacts
Housing
We provide assistance with finding accommodation in Grenoble and Paris through our housing platform managed
by Studapart. Booking accommodation without GEM guidance may lead to an unsatisfactory experience. Our help
aims to ensure that students find safe and suitable accommodation for their student lifestyle. Once the accommodation
is booked through the student platform, students can request a housing certificate necessary for the visa application to
the residence. GEM cannot provide you with this.
Visa
Visa applications can take up to 3 months; students need to start this process as soon as they receive the
acceptance letter. We recommend the students to consult the official French visa wizard to help them know if they
need a visa to come and to which consulate submit the application.
It is also advisable to contact the local Campus France agency for guidance.
Grants for exchange students
Follow the French Institute, Campus France or the French Embassy of your home country on social media for financial
aid opportunities. Please note that applications deadlines are very early, up to a year before the start of your study
abroad experience, so plan ahead.
Diversity, disabilities, accessibility
Students with disabilities benefit from special accommodation and personalized support to facilitate their education
and professional integration. For this, a file must be filled out and submitted to the dedicated service upon entering
GEM.

Resits will no longer be conducted remotely under any circumstances. Students required to take resit examinations must therefore be physically present at the designated Excelia campus on the scheduled dates. Excelia issues electronic transcripts, in PDF format. The digital signature on the transcript is the equivalent of a handwritten signature and official stamp. Digital documents are therefore considered official records. Exchange students can download their electronically signed transcripts from their WEBGAIA account. The electronic transcript of records is a valid format for all situations where signed and stamped paper documents are required. text:
INTERNATIONAL STUDENT EXCHANGE PROGRAM Fact Sheet
School of Business, Renmin University of China
43rd in FT MBA Ranking 2016 43rd in FT Global EMBA Ranking 2014 49th in FT EE Ranking 2014

| Name of University | School of Business, Renmin University of China |
| --- | --- |
| Overview | As one of China’s premier business schools, RBS boasts the longest history of management education in China, dating back to 1950. With close to 4,000 students and over 150 faculty members, it is the biggest and the most internationalized school among all 23 schools at Renmin University of China (total student population: 22,000+; ranked NO.1 in social sciences and humanities in China by the Ministry of Education). RBS is ranked No.1 in China in the national assessment of Business Administration discipline. Our school has obtained both EQUIS and AACSB accreditations, and ranked among the top 50 by the Financial Times in MBA, EMBA, and EE programs. We’re also a member of the GNAM (Global Network for Advanced Management) initiated by Yale School of Management. We offer two programs in English--BBA (Bachelor of Business Administration) and IMBA (international MBA). |
| Exchange Office | International Relations Office |
| Address | R605, Mingde Business Building |
| Email (for student enquiries) | rbsexchange@163.com |
| Skype Account | rbsexchange@163.com (account name: International.RBS) |

| Courses offered in English | Previously, course options were mainly limited to our Bachelor in Business Administration program (for undergrads) and International MBA program (for graduate students), along with a Chinese language training module. Starting with Spring 2014 semester, incoming exchange students have access to courses taught in English at other schools in Renmin University of China, including the School of Economics, School of Finance, School of Labor Relations and Human Resources, and Hanqing Advanced Institute of Economics and Finance. |
| --- | --- |
| Language Requirement | Fluent English |

| Course Information Course Load | http://2010.rbs.org.cn/templates/T_eng_new_list2/index.aspx?nodeid=442&page =ContentPage&contentid=1148 Course load of local students--- 1. MBA We require our full-time MBA students to get 47 credits (about 15 compulsories and 6 electives) in the first year, and have them focus on thesis-writing and field work in the second year. One credit is equivalent to 15 class hours. 2. Undergraduate Starting from the 2012 intake, all local undergrad students have to take around 140 credits (instead of the previously 170 credits) before graduation (including 4- credit internship report and 4-credit thesis writing). The total number of required credits might slightly vary depending on different majors/specializations. On average, students should complete about 15-18 credits each semester. Normally, compulsory courses are 3-credit each, and elective courses are 2-credit each. 1 credit stands for 17 contact hours. For example, 3 credits course is "3 hours per week" for 17 weeks = 51 hours in total. In general, 1 Renmin credit is equivalent to 2 ECTS credits. |
| --- | --- |

SSKKEEMMAA CCAAMMPPUUSSEESS GGEENNEERRAALL IINNFFOORRMMAATTIIOONN
SOPHIA ANTIPOLIS - France MASTER PROGRAMME / GLOBAL BBA PROGRAMME
General background: The Sophia Antipolis campus is located on the French Riviera in Sophia Antipolis, a technology park which is
home to several renowned companies, research institutes and schools of higher education. Most of SKEMA’s students live either in
Antibes or Juan les Pins, coastal towns close to Sophia Antipolis, easily accessible by bus.
Food: Lunch can be bought at the cafeteria for ¤3.25 from Monday to Friday. Sandwiches and salad bar are also available as well as
microwave ovens for students’ use.
Transport: Most students fly to Nice Côte d’Azur Airport, which is 45 min’ drive from Sophia Antipolis campus. Students can park
in the campus. There is a bus line run by the General Council of the region that costs ¤1,50. All main locations around the campus are
accessible by bus. There are two kinds of monthly plans available for students: Under 26 years old: ¤20 - Over 26 years old: ¤30.
Campus facilities: Computer labs and wireless networks are available on campus. 2 Trading rooms, 6 Amphitheatres from
150 to 600 seats, 50 Lecture rooms from 20 to 80 seats. Multimedia library.
LILLE - France MASTER PROGRAMME / GLOBAL BBA PROGRAMME
General background: The Lille campus is located in the town centre between the two railway stations (Lille Flandres & Lille Europe),
next to the old town and the business centre. Lille is only 1 hour from Paris, 38 minutes from Brussels and 1h20mn from London by
train. Lille is the main student town after Paris. The region is well known for its dynamic economic activity: several companies have
set up their headquarters here in order to be logistically at the centre of Europe.
Food: Students can eat at the University Restaurant near the school. On the campus, a cafeteria offers quick snacks at reasonable
prices. The school is located above the shopping centre where you can find Carrefour supermarket.
Transport: Most students arrive either at the Lille Flandres station or the Lille Europe station. Ilévia is the company that runs all the
buses, tramways and metro. They offer low prices for students under 28.
Campus facilities: There are computer labs and wireless networks on the Lille campus, including the library and the common
facilities.
France MASTER PROGRAMME
GRAND PARIS -
General background: Paris continues to be one of the most alluring cities in the world for cultural and economic activities. SKEMA
Business School’s Grand Paris Campus in Suresnes is a central site 13 minutes by car from Les Champs Elysées. The campus is
spread across 14,000 m2, including 1,500 m2 of rooftop terrace with views of the Seine and the Eiffel Tower.
Food: Students have access to the cafeteria, which will serve a variety of international cuisine.
Transport: Most students arrive by Tram - line T2 (Les Coteaux) or by train - line L (Val d’Or) - or by bus - lines 175 (Clavel station),
263 Monge station) or 471 (Avenue de Suresnes station). They also can come by bicycle ( Vélib ) or by car (possibility to park in the
Grand Paris Campus parking lot).
Campus facilities: The knowledge Centre is a space serving three functions: “library” (documentation), “factory” (production
facility) and “academy” (research to train and educate). It is also virtual, via its data-rich resource portal that is accessible at all
times.
NC - USA MASTER PROGRAMME / GLOBAL BBA PROGRAMME
RALEIGH -
General background: The SKEMA US campus is situated in Raleigh, North Carolina, about 1h by plane from NYC.
The SKEMA building is located on the Centennial campus of our partner North Carolina State University and is surrounded by many
international companies.
Housing & Food: SKEMA provides students with a Raleigh Housing Guide which includes a number of student residences located
on and around campus. All apartments are close to the SKEMA campus (access by bus) and fully equipped. The housing usually
costs an average of ¤750/¤1100 per month. Students can eat at university dining halls (cafeterias) or at several small restaurants/
cafés on campus which serve breakfast, lunch and dinner.
Transport: The nearest airport to SKEMA US campus is Raleigh/Durham International Airport (RDU) which is about 24 km away.
Your student ID gives access to the free Wolfline bus transport to go anywhere on campus and in Raleigh.
Campus facilities: Students have access to all NCSU facilities including impressive sporting facilities and libraries, bus lines, health
centre, dining halls, and much more.
HOUSING ON FRENCH CAMPUSES:
SKEMA campuses in France do not have on-campus accommodation but we have agreements with a number of residences located in the campus area.
Housing usually costs an average of ¤650 up to ¤1000 per month. SKEMA provides a housing portal to assist students.
For further information: housing@skema.edu
HEALTH INSURANCE FOR THE FRENCH CAMPUSES:
Exchange students are required to arrange their own insurance covering illnesses and accidents during the period of their stay in France. All the international students attending
SKEMA on exchange must purchase health insurance before applying for their student visa. Non EU citizen students studying for more than three months at SKEMA, are required
to enroll in the French “Sécurité Sociale” once they arrive in France. All students must have repatriation coverage during their stay at the host country.
3

SSKKEEMMAA CCAAMMPPUUSSEESS GGEENNEERRAALL IINNFFOORRMMAATTIIOONN
SUZHOU - China MASTER PROGRAMME
General background: Suzhou has been called the Venice of the East because of its many canals, beautiful natural environment and
traditional gardens. Situated one hour from Shanghai (2nd industrial city of China) Suzhou is a well-known high-technology centre
with 118 of the top 500 companies in the world.
Housing & Food: SKEMA has negotiated a certain number of apartments close to the campus. The housing usually costs on
average ¤350 per month. On campus, students can eat at several small restaurants and fast food restaurants which are all
reasonably priced. Students can also prepare meals in their flats which are conveniently located to school.
Transport: To get from the airport to campus, students can go by taxi (2h30 mn cost 600-800 RmB), train (1h30mn- cost 120
RmB) or bus (2h30mn- cost 130 RmB). As a service to students, SKEMA will be organizing shuttle buses from Shanghai Pudong
Airport to Suzhou campus on selected dates at the beginning of each semester (cost 200 RmB).
Campus facilities: All essential services are available on campus: restaurants, laudromat, travel agent, phone card kiosk, buses,
taxis, etc. Nearby, there is a large library and sport facility.
BELO HORIZONTE - Brazil MASTER PROGRAMME / GLOBAL BBA PROGRAMME
General background: Belo Horizonte, Brazil’s third most important city for business, is 360km from Rio de Janeiro and 500km from
São Paulo. It is ranked among the 10 most dynamic cities for business in Latin America by the magazine América Economia and is
also considered the Brazilian Silicon Valley with more than 200 startups and 10 incubators.
Housing & Food: SKEMA has negotiated a certain number of apartments in hotel residences close to the campus. The housing
usually costs an average of ¤800 per month. SKEMA also provides a housing portal to assist students.
Students can eat in the dining halls (cafeterias) or at several small restaurants/cafés on campus.
Transport: Flights from Europe have a layover in Rio de Janeiro or São Paulo airports before taking a domestic flight to Belo
Horizonte. Students have access to the campus by public bus.
Campus facilities: Students have access to all facilities including impressive sporting facilities and libraries, computer labs, dining
halls, and much more.
UAE CURRENTLY NOT OPEN TO INCOMING EXCHANGE STUDENTS
DUBAI -
General background: At the crossroads of the Indo-Pacific, Asian and African regions, Dubai is now one of the world’s biggest
magnets for talent. Located at the heart of the Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC), this campus is a thriving hub for students
keen on making an active contribution to the world of tomorrow and the renewal of a region long defined by its dependence on oil.
In the United Arab Emirates, young people from around the world are eager to play a key role in a financial and economic centre of
influence.
South Africa CURRENTLY NOT OPEN TO INCOMING EXCHANGE STUDENTS
STELLENBOSCH -
General background: By joining forces with Stellenbosch University, SKEMA has chosen a prestigious partner to establish its
African campus near Cape Town, South Africa. Students benefit from the exceptional facilities offered by the university, including a
vast library, a music school with concert halls, and first-class sports facilities (stadiums, gymnasiums, Olympic pools, etc.).
Housing: Students are eligible for on-campus university housing and can also benefit from an extensive list of private
accommodations.
Campus facilities: SKEMA students and participants will benefit from the many facilities of the Stellenbosch University that
include an extensive library, a music school, concert halls, an athletics stadium, several Olympic swimming pools and sports fields
(rugby , football, tennis, hockey, cricket, squash…).
HEALTH INSURANCE FOR THE INTERNATIONAL CAMPUSES:
Exchange students are required to arrange their own insurance covering illnesses, accidents and repatriation during the period of their stay in the host country. All the international
students attending SKEMA on exchange must purchase health insurance before applying for their student visa.
TO PREPARE STUDENT’S DEPARTURE ONCE SELECTED, CONTACT:
Yana MENCHENKOVA, International Coordinator
international.campuses@skema.edu

| Bachelor in Management (BSc) Fact sheet Edition 2026-2027 |

| --- |
| ESCP Business School |
| Established in 1819, ESCP is widely recognised as one of the first business schools in history. Its mission is to develop the next generation of transnational business leaders, preparing them to embrace the opportunities offered by cultural diversity. Founded in Paris, the school helped shape European identity and continues to be a promoter of innovation and research in a variety of fields. As well as a rich heritage, ESCP is also multi-accredited with national and international awards and certifications including EQUIS, AACSM, EFMD MBA, EFMD EMBA, and 6 European Higher Education accreditations. With its six urban campuses in Berlin, London, Madrid, Paris, Turin, and Warsaw, ESCP's true European Identity enables the provision of a unique style of cross- cultural business education and a global perspective on international management issues. Our students make up a group of rare cultural diversity, representing over 90 different countries. 2 |

|  |
| --- |
| Academic information |
| PROGRAMME Bachelor in Management (BSc) General information : https://escp.eu/programmes/bachelor-in-management-BSc Each undergraduate student at ESCP studies for 3 years, in 3 European countries, to get the BSc degree in Management. The curriculum of the programme includes 3 years (= 6 semesters) organized between the European campuses of ESCP Business School, the same core courses being taught on the different campuses. Languages of instruction All the courses offered to international exchange students are taught in English. The required level is C1 ( 6.5 IELTS / TOEFL IBT 90 / CAE 180). Pedagogy Innovative teaching, based on a blended learning model including case studies, group projects, workshops, lectures provided by faculty and executives from ESCP's corporate partners. Exams Final exams are held during a specific exam week. The assessments might include: essays, in-class presentations, written quizzes and examinations, and group projects. 3 |

| Exchange student applications |  |
| --- | --- |
| APPLICATION REQUIREMENTS. As exchange students will integrate our Bachelor in Management programme, they will be studying with local and international students who are generally 18 to 22 years old. We would advise you to nominate students who are between the ages of 18 and 24. After the official nomination, students will receive instructions for their online registration, and additional information about their exchange programme, contacts, and logistics. SUPPORTING DOCUMENTS REQUIRED FOR APPLICATION • Transcripts of previous years at university • Copy of passport or national ID card • Profile picture used for digital student card | 5 |

| Class rules The evaluation and grading system |
| --- |
| CLASS ATTENDANCE is strictlymandatory. Students are allowed up to 3 missed lecture for 36-hour core course and up to 2 missed lectures for a 24-hour elective. After that, in principle, the student is not accepted the course. Note thatno course can be dropped afterthe session has alreadystarted. CREDIT SYSTEM/WORKLOAD The credits received in the Bachelor are in accordance with the European Transfer Credit system (ECTS), based on students’ workloads, i.e. including face-to-face course attendance andpersonalwork. The workload per semester is 30 ECTS, with a combination of 36-hour (6 ECTS cr.) and 24-hour(3ECTScr.)courses(excludinglanguageclasses). RESULTS, TRANSCRIPTS OF GRADES Students can see their results online (after completing a short evaluation survey for each course)and downloadtheirofficialtranscriptsofgradesfromtheintranetportal. Students’ academic performance is evaluated according to a grade point scale out of 20. ESCP Grading (out of 20) and GPA Each semester, the student GPA is updated based on the following calculation, for validated courses only: average of the final grades (local grading / 20), weighted by the ECTScreditvalueofeachcourse. Our Parisian
campus
The Champerret campus benefits from an urban
location in the west of Paris, close to the most
beautiful avenue in the world, the Champs Elysées,
the Palais des Congrès, and one of the largest
business districts in Europe, La Défense. It is also
adjacent to two other cities (Levallois-Perret and
Neuilly-sur-Seine) that offer very dynamic and
pleasant areas for students to stay during their
studies.
Like all of ESCP's campuses in Paris, the Champerret
campus has an unobstructed view of the Eiffel
Tower from several classrooms! With a surface area
of 17,000m², many improvements are underway to
welcomestudentsinthe bestconditions.

classrooms

meetings

varietyoflocalandinternational specialities

Academic
information
PROGRAMME
Master in Management
ACADEMIC OFFER
From a selection of approximately 70 electives depending on the semester, taught in
French or English, we provide a stimulating environment for students to develop their
skillsandknowledge.
● 30-hour electivestaught3hpersessiononceaweek,during10weeks= 5 ECTS
● 15-hour electives taught 3h per session, during 5 weeks = 2.5 ECTS, starting
eitheratthe beginningofthesemesterormid-semester
The maximum workload authorised is 180 hours (30 ECTS) per semester, which is a
maximum of 6 courses of 30 hours, or a combination of 30-hour and 15-hour courses
(excluding language classes). Note that students need to be registered for at least 5
ECTS (1x30h course or 2x 15h courses)duringtheirexchangesemester.
The Summer “semester” is an intensive 4-week study programme offering a limited
number of regular electives (120 hours - 20 ECTS maximum). 1 student enrolled in the
Summersemestercountsashalfaspotinourbalances.
LANGUAGE COURSE
Exchange students may enroll upon arrival in a weekly French class, at no additional
cost. The course is 2 hours per week and is for credit (1 ECTS). All French levels are
accepted, as the course will divide students into groups. Note that there is also
possibilitytoattendthe Frenchcoursefornocreditasanauditor.
PEDAGOGY
Innovative teaching, based on case studies, group projects, workshops, lectures
provided by faculty and executives from ESCP's corporate partners, give students all
theskillstheyneedtoenterthejobmarket.
EXAMS
Final exams are held during the last course session. The final assessment for electives
might include: essays, in-class presentations, written quizzes and examinations, and
groupprojects.

system
CLASS ATTENDANCE
is strictlymandatory.
Students are allowed1missed lecture for a15-hourelective and2missedlectures for
a30-hourelective.Afterthat, thestudentwillbeexpelledfromthecourse.
Note thatno course can be dropped afterthe mandatoryorientationday.
CREDIT SYSTEM/WORKLOAD
The maximum authorized workload per semester is 180 hours (30 ECTS) per
semester, which is a maximum of 6x 30-hour courses, or a combination of 30-hour
and 15-hour courses (excluding language classes). Please note that students are
required to take a minimum of 5 ECTS (1x 30h course or 2x 15h courses) during
theirexchange semester.
RESULTS
Students can see their results on their intranet after completing a short evaluation
surveyforeachcourseusuallyinFebruary(S1)andJune(S2).
Students’ academic performance is evaluated according to a grade point scale out
of 20.
Officialtranscriptswillbeavailable fordownloadfromtheirintranetaswell.
ESCP GPA (out of 20)
Eachsemester,thestudentGPAisupdatedbasedonthefollowingcalculation:
Average of the final grades (for validated courses only), weighted by the ECTS value
ofeachcourse.
ESCP PERCENTILE
Each semester, students are ranked for each course on each campus based on the
followingpercentilecalculation:
[(number of students registered in the course – ranking based on the final grade) *
100/number of students registered in the course]. The best student will get 99% and
thelastonewillget0%.

information

the Student Affairs platform CampusLife once they
receive theirESCPemailaddressand password.
HOUSING
ESCP has no accommodation on campus. However,
students can check out offers from our housing partners
(student residencies, co-living companies, private
landlords…)onCampusLife.
FEES
Notuition/registrationfeesforvisitingstudents.

certificate covering them for the whole duration of their

RecommendationscanalsobefoundonCampusLife.

suburbs)

(depending on the type of accommodation and
location)

€6)

Please note that no internships are possible for
exchange students.

Embassy/Consulate for the latest visa information. Exchange students should not

2026-2027

Established in 1914, the Freeman School of Business at
Tulane University is a founding AACSB member with
prestigious international accreditation. With over 3,000
students globally, Freeman has built a reputation for
developing business leaders who positively impact
organizations and communities.
Today, the Freeman School of Business is a globally
recognized institution serving over 3,000 students
worldwide. Its innovative programs blend exceptional
classroom instruction with hands-on learning
experiences to develop business leaders who make
positive impacts in both professional settings and
community environments.

home institution

Application procedure
Nomination procedure & deadlines
(proceeded by a student)
(proceeded by a partner)
After students are nominated to GSOM they
Inquire a link to proceed with nominations
receive an e-mail with further instructions
from any GSOM International Office team
necessary for their application.
member.
The nomination deadlines: The application deadlines are:
by April 25 for Fall semester May 15 for Fall semester
by October 15 for Spring semester October 25 for Spring semester
Free mover option
A student who is not officially nominated by a partner University or is coming from the
University that has no student exchange agreement with GSOM SPbU can be accepted
for a semester as a free mover student (on a fee-paying basis).

Students’ application package includes:
• latest university academic report (transcript) reflecting grades and GPA
• English language proficiency confirmation comparable to the min level expected:
TOEFL ibt 80/ IELTS 6.0 or B2 on a test administered by a teacher qualified to work with CEFR
• a resume/CV
• passport copy (which must be valid for min 18 months since mid-August for those
arriving in Fall; since mid-January for those arriving in Spring).
• if you plan to take courses which are taught in Russian: Russian language proficiency
confirmation at the B2 level.
Academic calendar Fall semester Spring semester
01.09. – 31.01 11.02. – 06.07
Preliminary Two weeks prior to semester start (to be reconfirmed
Arrival date annually by announcing the exact date to the students)
Preliminary Last week of August in Fall + around 2 days to enter Russia;
Introduction days
First week of February in Spring + around 2 days to enter
Russia.
*All dates change slightly and are timely reconfirmed each semester to the selected students.
Abstrain from planning ANY trips (including the return date) until a complete exam
schedule is published: only midterm and online exams can be retaken. Note that
GSOM SPbU doesn’t provide with the alternative exam arrangements.

Introduction period: Smoother adjustment to a new culture
Students’ application package includes:
Participation: highly recommended, though not obligatory.
• latest university academic report (transcript) reflecting grades and GPA
Program: tours around GSOM SPbU campuses, information meeting with key persons,
• English language proficiency confirmation comparable to the min level expected:
Russian language crash course and a concurrent social and cultural program organized
TOEFL
by GSOM Buddy Team.
ibt 80/ IELTS 6.0 or B2 on a test administered by a teacher qualified to work with CEFR
NB: On the first days of the Intro week, all exchange students must deal with the
• a resume/CV registration at Federal Migration Service; thus coming to Int.Office right upon arrival is a
must.
• passport copy (which must be valid for min 18 months since mid-August for those
arriving in Fall; since mid-January for those arriving in Spring).
• if you plan to take courses which are taught in Russian: Russian language proficiency
Doing business in Russia: Get below the surface of preconceived ideas about living and
working in Russia
confirmation at the B2 level.
Twice a year at the beginning of the semester a three week intensive module Doing
Business in Russia is held for all newly arrived international students* at GSOM. The
course includes company visits, guest lectures from business practitioners and
students’ final business project presentations.
*the availability of the course to bachelor and CEMS students is reconfirmed each semester
30 ECTS full-time workload
Exchange students are expected to complete 30 ECTS/semester (including a Foreign
language course).
If your desirable workload significantly differs from the required one, you must enclose a
statement from your home university confirming it.
Class attendance is mandatory and crucial for your grade.
Courses for Exchange Students
The course list is annually reviewed and once confirmed is published with a few
changes before the start of each semester.

Special study conditions due to medical reasons
In case it is officially prescribed for a student to study under special conditions due to
medical reasons, it must be supported upon the student’s arrival by presenting to the
International office an official medical document stating certain conditions to be taken
into account.
Health Insurance: Safety net to avoid extra expenses in case of health problems
• must cover the whole period of the stay in Russia
• required when extending single entry visa (check the guide to see GSOM requirements).
• may become a reason for rejection of a visa application if absent.
Visa
An official letter of invitation from GSOM SPbU is required to apply for a visa (prepared by
GSOM within 4 weeks after application deadline).
According to Russian Federation legislation, students may only request a 90 day Russian
student visa with a single entry. Upon the arrival students are officially enrolled to GSOM
SPbU (20 working days), after which they are invited to GSOM IRO to apply for a multi-
entry visa. The processing time of extending visa is 5 weeks. You should not therefore
plan to travel outside of SPb during this period.
Accommodation in SPbU Dorms: Quick social networking and money-saving option
Booking: automatically provided to all international students.
Cost: up to 100 euro/month.
Master exchange students are placed in ulitsa Kapitanskaya, dom 3, (30 min
by public transportation from GSOM). Conditions: basic, shared rooms for 2-3 students with
joint kitchen and shower facilities.
Bachelor exchange students are offered a space in the territory of the Mikhailovskaya Dacha
campus. Conditions: 3-4 rooms, one for each student, in a flat-type blocks with showers and
equipped kitchen.
NB: Student is allocated a place in the dormitory in accordance with the order established by
the University (it is impossible to choose a roommate unless offered before your arrival by
SPbU’s initiative).
Private accommodation & Registration in the city
Students may stay «off-campus» but must arrange for this independently. Those students
who will choose to stay at a private place will have to deal with the registration procedure
individually together with the owner of the place they rent (see the relevant page in the
students’ guide for more information). Monthly rent for a 1 bedroom apartment ranges
from 30,000 Rubles and higher. There are many options on the internet as well as some
tips in the GSOM exchange student Facebook group. GSOM doesn’t accumulate this kind
of information and is not entitled to advice on the matter.

Obligatory Official Medical Check-Up for Migration Registration Purposes
Since 2022 all international citizens staying in Russia for more than 90 days must undergo
obligatory medical check-up and submit their photos and fingerprints for Migration Registration
purposes at the main Muti-Functional Center (ul. Krasnogo Tekstilschika, dom 10-12).
• This service is provided on a fee-paying basis covered at a foreign citizen’s expenses.
• The cost of the service varies around 7 000 rubles.
• Details can be studied in the relevant section in the guide.
Conditions and cost of living
There are many shopping centers in SPb as well as a number of local markets,
convenience stores with the most common daily goods and 24/7 supermarkets.
Public transportation (per ride): bus, 50 R., metro 60 R., and the semi-private minibuses
(marshrutkas) – 60 R. Student public transport card can be purchased for the duration
of the exchange semester.
A hot meal in the GSOM cafeteria with soup or salad and a main course and a glass of a
fruit drink: 250 R.
Living costs depend on life style and spending habits. On average an international
student spends about 25,000 -30,000 RUR (excl. rent)*.
See more examples of specific prices.
Booking return tickets
AVOID booking your return ticket until you know the exact dates of the semester
confirmed by the academic offices (as a rule announced to you with the relevant course
lists) as the date of the end of the semester will be the date when your visa expires.
Otherwise you risk being forced to change your tickets.
GSOM also does not recommend to plan your return date until you have an exam
schedule with dates of final assessment for all the courses you are registered for.
Public Holidays Fall Semester Spring Semester
November 4 – National February 23 – Defender of
Unity Day Motherland’s Day
January 1-7 – March 8 – International Women’s Day
New Year Holidays May 1 – Spring and Labor Day
January 7 – Orthodox May 9 – Victory Day
Christmas
June 12 – Russia National Day

We look forward to welcoming you at St.
Petersburg University and GSOM!

EXCHANGE PROGRAM INFORMATION
Undergraduate Majors: Finance
Finance Economics
Accounting
Marketing
Data Science
Business Administration
Language of Instructions: Both English-taught and Chinese-taught courses are offered; please see the
course list for specific availability.
Course List: https://en.gsm.pku.edu.cn/exchange/Incoming_Exchange/Academics.htm
Please check the website for updates posted in March (for upcoming Fall
courses) and September (for upcoming Spring courses).
Language Requirements: Students must be proficient either in Chinese or English.
Nominees must have a GPA of 3.0 or above, or meet the equivalent criteria at their
GPA Requirement:
home institutions.
Language Courses: In each semester, Guanghua offers three levels of "Business Chinese" for students
with different language foundations.
Full-time Workload: Courses offered at Guanghua are worth 2 or 3 credits, with each credit
equivalent to 15-18 contact hours. Exchange students are required to take a
minimum of 4 credits up to a maximum of 18 credits per semester.
Exams: For the Fall semester 2025, most courses will last 16 weeks, meaning that they
will conclude by Dec. 28, 2025. The final exams will take place within 2 weeks
after the final session, depending on the instructors' arrangement. The semester
officially ends on January 11, 2026.
For the Spring semester 2026, the course information will be published in Fall
2025, please kindly wait in patience and refer to the official announcement.
View the Academic Calendar of 2025-2026.

| EXCHANGE PROGRAM INFORMATION |
| --- |

GRADING
Fall Semester/Academic Year Exchange
Nomination Period: February 15 to March 30
Spring Semester Exchange
Nomination Period: August 15 to September 30

| NOMINATION DEADLINES |
| --- |

NOMINATION
* Undergraduate students who are P.R. China passport holders are generally not eligible to participate in Guanghua’s
exchange program except in limited circumstances ( If the exchange has an imbalance in favor of our partner
school, it may be possible to accept a limited number of P.R.C. nationals as discussed on a case-by-case basis.).
* All partners are kindly requested to nominate students through our nomination portal; portal login information has
been provided to each partner university’s program coordinator for outgoing exchange. The nomination portal can
be accessed at:
http://exchange.gsm.pku.edu.cn/nomination/web/login.html
STUDENT APPLICATION
STEP ONE: APPLY ONLINE
1. PKU Online Application
1)Application for undergraduate students holding an international passport: http://www.studyatpku.com
2)Application for undergraduate students holding a Hong Kong, Macau, or Taiwan passport:
http://162.105.209.64/exchange/web/login.html
2. Guanghua Online Application: http://exchange.gsm.pku.edu.cn/nomination/student/login.html
FALL SEMESTER APPLICATION DEADLINES SPRING SEMESTER APPLICATION DEADLINE
First Round of the Application: April 15 First Round of the Application: October 15
Second Round of the Application: May 15 Second Round of the Application: November 15
STEP TWO: MAIL A COMPLETE SET OF MATERIALS TO OUR OFFICE
•Printed PKU application form
•Resume
•Official academic transcript (an unofficial transcript will NOT be accepted)
•Official nomination letter from the exchange office of your home university
•A copy of the photo page of your valid passport (if your passport will expire before the end of your exchange
program, please submit a copy of your current passport and inform us that you will be applying for a new passport)
•One passport-sized photo, attached to the application form
•One-page letter of motivation highlighting your academic and personal goals for your exchange
Detailed information is available on our website: http://exchange.gsm.pku.edu.cn/.
The submitted materials must be original documents or notarized copies in either Chinese or English. Any missing
documents may result in a delay processing your admission.
The package of all listed application documents must be mailed to our office in due time.

LIVING ACCOMMODATIONS
International students can apply for housing at the PKU Global Village, but availability is not guaranteed. Due to the
limited number of dorms, many students will need to find off-campus accommodations. Our team will provide
assistance and share relevant housing information. We recommend that students remain flexible regarding this
matter.
Off-campus housing generally ranges from US$450 – 650 per month for a single room in a two-bedroom / three-
bedroom apartment.
Living Expenses
Depending on your living situation and your personal spending habits, non-housing expenditures typically average
US$350 – 450 per month.
HEALTH INSURANCE
All international passport holders are required to buy health insurance through Peking University on the day of
registration. The insurance costs approximately RMB 400 per semester (subject to change).
Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan passport holders are required to buy travel insurance on their own.
VISA
International passport holders who are planning to stay longer than three months must obtain a visa to enter and study
in China. The visa application process for international passport holders is listed below; a different process with
different documentation is required for students from Hong Kong, Macau, or Taiwan.
Step 1: Submit a program application to Peking University and the Guanghua School of Management
Step 2: Application approved and admissions documents sent to the address on file
Step 3: Apply for a Study Visa (X1/ X2) at a local Chinese Embassy or Consulate using your admissions documents,
which usually takes around 2 weeks.
Travel visa (L-visa) , Q visa and S Visa are NOT acceptable.

FACILITIES
Modernized library services, computer labs, cafés, on-campus restaurants, student organizations, bookstores, gyms,
and other student facilities.
STUDENT SERVICE
GISA (Guanghua International Students Association)
We have a buddy program run through GISA where students from similar programs are matched with incoming
exchange students during their period of study. The buddy serves as a resource and guide for the exchange student.
GISA can be contacted at gisa@gsm.pku.edu.cn
Career Services
A number of career resources will be available to exchange students during their stay. These include access to all
company presentations organized at Guanghua, employer contact database listings, job postings, and on-campus job
descriptions. Additional services include appointments with staff members/career advisors, optional participation in
career service seminars and information sessions. Students also have opportunities to join job fairs and networking
events and sign up for mock interviews and resume clinics. The Career Development Centre is located in Room 108 at
Guanghua. More information is available on their website: http://en.gsm.pku.edu.cn/cdc/index.htm.
Exchange Coordination Services
Guanghua’s Office of International Relations manages exchange student services.
Visa Issues
For transferring or extending your visa, please contact the PKU International Students Division (PKU ISD) in the New
Sun Student Center, Room 328.

Introduction: 

The University of Ljubljana (UL) was established in 1919 and is situated in Slovenia’s capital, Ljubljana. It was founded on the basis of centuries of educational tradition and is the most large-scale university in Slovenia, with over 50,000 current students and 130 different majors and study programs. As the country’s economy grows rapidly, UL progressively develops into an internationalized university. In the last ten years, UL has eagerly participated in global academic research projects and various education programs. In 2013, UL cooperated in 421 EU projects and was also present in Slovenia government-hosted cooperative education programs. In addition, UL is a member of numerous international networks in Europe, Australia, Central America, and other countries. These networks have allowed student exchanges with over 500 universities. The university also cooperates with more than a hundred universities across Europe, allowing students to go on exchange in many different countries. Under these programs, UL continues to provide the best opportunities to both outgoing and incoming exchange students from other universities. From classroom lectures to housing, UL provides a complete service that allows exchange students to fully immerse themselves in this unique educational and cultural experience.

Introduction: 

The University of St. Petersburg was established in 1724 and is one of most historic universities in Russia. The University’s development is bound tightly with the cultural and scientific developments of the former Soviet Union and Russia. St. Petersburg is also a cradle for many outstanding intellectuals. The Graduate School of Management at the University of St. Petersburg has been committed to internationalization since earlier times. The School is not only a member of the CEMS Global Alliance in Management Education (CEMS) and Partners in International Management (PIM); it has also acquired two top international business accreditations AMBA and AACSB accreditations.

text:
Exchange Program Fact Sheet
Academic Year Spring 2025

| Contact | Incoming & Outgoing Student Coordinator: Kapik Yeung Associate Director for Academic Affairs & Student Experience Email: kyeung@brandeis.edu Partnership email: globalexchange@brandeis.edu |
| --- | --- |
| Website | www.brandeis.edu/global (Brandeis International Business School) www.brandeis.edu/isso (Brandeis International Students & Scholars Office) |
| Application Deadlines | Nominating Deadlines: ● October 10, 2024 – (Spring 2025 semester) Nominations from coordinators should submit this form that includes the following: ● Demographic background information (First/Last Name, Citizenship, Date of Birth, Sex at Birth, E-mail Address, and Degree Program) ● Semester of exchange ● Completed English Language Verification Form |
| Required Paperwork | Upon acceptance from Brandeis International Business School, students must complete the following online forms: ● Brief Application ● VIDOF (for visa application) ● Health Form |
| Language Requirement | ● All exchange students must have a high proficiency in English ● All courses are taught in English. ● We do not have a TOEFL score requirement for exchange students, however, we expect that the nominating office understands that all courses are taught in English and strong English language skills are required. |

| English Language Courses | Intensive language courses for learning English are NOT offered through Brandeis. English Language Learning workshops and tutoring are offered. |
| --- | --- |
| Academics at Brandeis International Business School |  |
| Academic Pre-Requisites | Exchange students MUST be enrolled in a graduate level program in their home university. |
| Courses Available to Exchange Students | Courses are available on a space available basis when course prerequisites are met. |
| Fields of Study | Economics, Business and Finance. |
| Departments Available to Exchange Students | Exchange students may enroll in any course at the business school with open enrollment when students have satisfied the prerequisite coursework at their home institution. Due to space limitations and heavy demand, priority will be given to full-time degree enrolled students. Students are not able to take class outside of the Brandeis Campus. |
| Full-Time Class-Load | In order to maintain their J-1 immigration status, exchange students must remain enrolled in a minimum of 3 courses or equivalent (12 credits) per semester. Depending on their language level and their home requirements, students may enroll in a maximum of five full-time courses. We have full-semester and half-semester courses, called modules. Exchange students are permitted to add and drop courses using the online system. Some courses require permission codes provided by the Exchange adviser. |
| Exchange Student Status | Exchange student status is Non-Degree Status. |

| Learning Expectations, | Typically, classes meet once each week for a total of 3 hours. Some courses meet twice a week at 1.5 hours/session. Students are expected to |
| --- | --- |

| Class Format, Coursework & Assessment | attend all classes and class participation is very important in the Brandeis academic setting. Academic integrity is crucial to the Brandeis International Business School mission, and we expect all students to cite papers/projects appropriately and according to Brandeis and business school policies. The majority of classes at Brandeis are case-based. During orientation, a case-study session is conducted to orient the students to the case analysis format. The majority of classes have midterms, final exams, projects and papers. |
| --- | --- |
| Grading System | Brandeis uses a “letter-grading” scheme: A+ excellent A excellent A- above average B+ above average B average B- satisfactory C+ below average D not satisfactory F failing A grade of at least a B- is required to earn credit. |
| Credit System | 4 credits = full semester course (3 hours/week for 14 weeks) 2 credits = module half semester course (3 hours/week for 7 weeks) |
| Academic Calendar |  |
| Fall Semester | ● Exchange students MUST participate in orientation, dates will be sent to them well in advance. |
| Academic Calendar | The academic calendar, and calendar highlights can be found at: https://www.brandeis.edu/registrar/calendar/highlights-24-25.html |
| Other Relevant Dates | Please check the academic calendar for winter/spring breaks and other holidays, which the university observes and on which no classes are held. |
| Spring Semester | ● Exchange students MUST participate in orientation, the date will be sent to them well in advance. |
| Anticipated Expenses |  |

| Estimated Expenses Estimates are in U.S. dollars. Expect 3-5% increase each year. Based on 2023. | Fall or Spring Semester Books & Supplies 1,018.00 Housing/Food 9,803.00 Transportation 1,455.00 Medical/Insurance 1,992.00 Personal 2,389.00 ______ TOTAL $ 16,657.00* this is an estimate, please budget for between $16,000 and $18,000 |
| --- | --- |
| Immigration and Insurance Requirements |  |
| Health Insurance Requirements | Both Massachusetts State Law and J-1 Exchange Visitor Program require exchange students to have appropriate health insurance. Due to laws that went into effect in January 2011, there are now more specific requirements regarding acceptable insurance coverage. Students should not assume that insurance policies that were accepted previously will still be accepted. The new law requires that the policy: 1. be purchased from a United States corporation 2. be purchased in the United States 3. cannot cover emergency care only 4. provides coverage for mental health and substance abuse care 5. provides coverage of pre-existing conditions 6. provides a prescription subsidy Exchange students will automatically be enrolled in the Brandeis group health insurance, referred to as SHP; unless they can demonstrate that they have insurance that satisfies all of the above requirements. Brandeis University cannot exempt students from the requirements of law. |
| Visa Requirements | Once a student has been accepted, and they have completed the online VIDOF form, the International Students & Scholars Office (ISSO) will create a DS-2019 form which will be mailed directly to the student. The DS-2019 must be submitted to the U.S. consulate or embassy in the student’s home country, along with the visa application and other required documents. Please make sure to check with your consulate office regarding any other forms necessary prior to attending your interview for a U.S. student visa. |
